notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.provsql: The time is the load of the database (its tables and their provenance, as tddlog's time includes parsing its fact files) and the queries'; the start of the server is not timed.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.provsql: The time is the load of the database (its tables and their provenance, as tddlog's time includes parsing its fact files) and the queries'; the start of the server is not timed.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.provsql: The time is the load of the database (its tables and their provenance, as tddlog's time includes parsing its fact files) and the queries'; the start of the server is not timed.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.provsql: The time is the load of the database (its tables and their provenance, as tddlog's time includes parsing its fact files) and the queries'; the start of the server is not timed.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.provsql: The time is the load of the database (its tables and their provenance, as tddlog's time includes parsing its fact files) and the queries'; the start of the server is not timed.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.provsql: The time is the load of the database (its tables and their provenance, as tddlog's time includes parsing its fact files) and the queries'; the start of the server is not timed.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.provsql: The time is the load of the database (its tables and their provenance, as tddlog's time includes parsing its fact files) and the queries'; the start of the server is not timed.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

answers.ref_note: The reference is ProbLog's d-DNNF, given one query at a time (problog_each.py).

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.provsql: The time is the load of the database (its tables and their provenance, as tddlog's time includes parsing its fact files) and the queries'; the start of the server is not timed.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.agrum: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.genfer: Genfer answers dice2genfer.py's translation of the Dice program in floating point, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.geni: Geni computes in single precision and prints seven decimals, so differences of up to 5e-8 from the reference are its print precision.
notes.libdai: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pgmpy: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads.
notes.pluck: The time is the whole process's, with Julia loading Pluck; the tables take Pluck's own time, the warm one where it ran a second time in the process, else the in-process one.
notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.provsql: The time is the load of the database (its tables and their provenance, as tddlog's time includes parsing its fact files) and the queries'; the start of the server is not timed.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

notes.prism: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value. The time includes the JVM's start.
notes.provsql: The time is the load of the database (its tables and their provenance, as tddlog's time includes parsing its fact files) and the queries'; the start of the server is not timed.
notes.psi: Psi answers dice2psi.py's translation of the Dice program exactly, one run per component of the program's value, the times added.
notes.psouffle: The Soufflé program is compiled into a C++ program, which then runs: the time is both, the compilation's added to the run's, though PSouffle's paper times the run alone. PSouffle prints probabilities with eight decimals.
notes.scallop: Scallop keeps every proof of each tuple (its top-k proofs at the largest k its command line takes), so its answer is exact. The time includes tddlog's grounding of the program, which Scallop reads.
notes.storm: The model is the Markov chain dice2prism.py writes of the Dice program, a model per component of its value.
notes.tensorinference: Reads the UAI file and the observations that Merlin reads; the time is the whole process's, and the tables take its own, timed as Alea.jl's after a warm-up on a small model (warm-up s): the warm one where it solved the instance a second time in the process (where the first took under a third of the limit), else the in-process one less Julia's compilation within it (compile s); without Julia's start and the package's load, with the search for a contraction order.

/*
This program is inspired by the morphological characteristics of the Stromboli
Italian island.
The Stromboli island is located at the intersection of two geological faults, 
one in the southwest-northeast direction, the other in the east-west direction,
and contains one of the three volcanoes that are active in Italy. 
This program models the possibility that an eruption or an earthquake occurs at Stromboli.

From
Elena Bellodi and Fabrizio Riguzzi. Structure learning of probabilistic logic 
programs by searching the clause space. Theory and Practice of Logic 
Programming, FirstView Articles, 2014
*/
:- use_module(library(pita)).

:- if(current_predicate(use_rendering/1)).
:- use_rendering(c3).
:- endif.

:- pita.

:- begin_lpad.

eruption : 0.6 ; earthquake : 0.3 :- 
  sudden_energy_release,
  fault_rupture(_).
% If there is a sudden energy release under the island and there is a fault 
% rupture, then there can be an eruption of the volcano on the island with 
% probability 0.6 or an earthquake in the area with probability 0.3

sudden_energy_release : 0.7.
% The energy release occurs with probability 0.7 

fault_rupture(southwest_northeast).
fault_rupture(east_west).
% we are sure that ruptures occur in both faults

:- end_lpad.

/** <examples>

?- prob(eruption,Prob). % what is the probability of an eruption?
% expected result 0.588
?- prob(earthquake,Prob). % what is the probability of an earthquake?
% expected result 0.357
?- prob(eruption,Prob),bar(Prob,C). % what is the probability of an eruption?
% expected result 0.588
?- prob(earthquake,Prob),bar(Prob,C). % what is the probability of an earthquake?
% expected result 0.357


*/

main :-
    forall((Q = eruption, prob(Q, P)), format("~q:\t~w~n", [Q, P])),
    forall((Q = earthquake, prob(Q, P)), format("~q:\t~w~n", [Q, P])).

*/

:- use_module(library(pita)).

:- if(current_predicate(use_rendering/1)).
:- use_rendering(graphviz).

female:0.5.

qualified:0.5.


admitted:-  deptB,female,qualified.
admitted:- \+ deptB,\+ female.

deptB:- female.
deptB:0.5:- \+ female.

:-end_lpad.

adjusted_effect_of_female(P):-
  prob(admitted,(female,deptB),PAFB),
  prob(deptB,PB),
  P is PAFB*PB.

adjusted_effect_of_male(P):-
  prob(admitted,(\+ female, \+ deptB),PAFA),
  prob(admitted,(\+ female,deptB),PAFB),

*/

    forall((Q = admitted, prob(Q, (female), P)), format("~q:\t~w~n", [Q, P])).

  (match rel

:- begin_lpad.

holdsAt(F, T) :-
  initially(F),
  \+ clipped(0, F, T).
holdsAt(F, T2) :- 
  initiates(F, T1),
  T1 < T2 ,
  \+ clipped(T1 ,F, T2 ).
clipped(T1 ,F, T3) :-
  terminates(F, T2),
  T1 < T2 , T2 < T3.

initiates(locatedIn(A, B), T):0.66 :- 
  happens(arrive(A, B), T).
terminates(locatedIn(A, D), T):0.66 :-
  happens(arrive(A, B), T),
  B \= D.
initially(locatedIn(bob, garden)).
happens(arrive(bob, kitchen), 3). 
happens(arrive(bob, garage), 5).

:- end_lpad.

% 1.0

% 0.34

% 0.66

% 0.66.

*/

;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over

;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their

(define (choose . ps)

# cplint_multiple_paths_simple.pl: a ProbLog program written in SPPL by tddlog's scripts/problog2ppl.py,
# first order as it is written. The facts and the joins of the rules are Python
# constants, computed before the first sample: each rule's matches a list
# comprehension over the relations its body joins, a recursive component's
# tuples a fixpoint of its rules, and the tuples that the queries and the
# evidence read. Then each probabilistic fact and each instance of a
# probabilistic rule samples a coin, and each instance of a tuple that is read
# sets a variable of its own, in a `for` over its component's instances: 1
# where its body holds or an earlier instance of its tuple does, the last of a
# tuple's instances its holding. A cycle of tuples that read each other does so
# in as many stages as it has tuples, each stage reading the one before. The
# queries are the events of queries_(), asked of the model given the evidence:
#
#   sppl_dice.py PROGRAM.sppl
#
# queries
# component 0 bool query0

from functools import reduce
from itertools import accumulate

yes_ = lambda: true_ << {1}
no_ = lambda: true_ << {0}
all_ = lambda es_: reduce(lambda a_, b_: a_ & b_, es_) if es_ else yes_()
fix_ = lambda g_, x_: (lambda y_: x_ if y_ == x_ else fix_(g_, y_))(g_(x_))
dedup_ = lambda xs_: list(dict.fromkeys(xs_))
index_ = lambda ts_: {t_: j_ for j_, t_ in enumerate(ts_)}
by_ = lambda ts_, ps_: reduce(lambda d_, j_: d_.setdefault(tuple(ts_[j_][p_] for p_ in ps_), []).append(j_) or d_,
                              range(len(ts_)), {})
idiv_ = lambda a_, b_: abs(a_) // abs(b_) * (1 if (a_ < 0) == (b_ < 0) else -1)
# the heads of relation q_ that matches ms_ give; a coin's index for each probability below 1
heads_ = lambda q_, ms_: [h_ for m_ in ms_ for r_, h_ in m_[1] if r_ == q_]
coins_of_ = lambda ps_, c0_: [None if p_ >= 1 else c0_ + n_
                              for p_, n_ in zip(ps_, accumulate([0] + [int(x_ < 1) for x_ in ps_]))]
# a relation's instances, each (its tuple's index, its coin and value or None, its refs); their indexes by tuple
facts_ = lambda i_, ts_, cs_: [(i_[t_], None if c_ is None else (c_, 1), []) for t_, c_ in zip(ts_, cs_)]
inst_ = lambda q_, i_, ms_, ks_, c0_: [(i_[h_], None if ks_ is None else (c0_ + ks_[m_[0]], n_ + 1), m_[2])
                                      for m_ in ms_ for n_, (r_, h_) in enumerate(m_[1]) if r_ == q_]
by_tuple_ = lambda es_, n_: (lambda d_: [d_.get((j_,), []) for j_ in range(n_)])(by_(es_, (0,)))
# the tuples (relation, index) that a tuple's instances read; those that tuples us_ read in turn, where ok_
reads_ = lambda u_: ([(r_, k_) for m_ in of_[u_[0]][u_[1]] for r_, k_, _, _ in insts_[u_[0]][m_][2]]
                     if u_[0] in of_ else [])
reach_ = lambda us_, ok_: fix_(lambda s_: s_ | {w_ for u_ in s_ for w_ in reads_(u_) if ok_(w_)}, frozenset(us_))
# a component's steps, each (relation, instance, stage, cycle), over the tuples of its relations c_ that the
# queries and the evidence read: its cycles of tuples (the tuples that reach the same ones), each after the
# cycles it reads (which reach fewer), in as many stages as it has tuples, each stage reading the one before
cycles_ = lambda rs_: sorted(reduce(lambda d_, u_: d_.setdefault(rs_[u_], []).append(u_) or d_, sorted(rs_),
                                    {}).values(), key=lambda us_: (len(rs_[us_[0]]), us_[0]))
steps_ = lambda c_: [(u_[0], m_, s_, g_) for g_, us_ in enumerate(cycles_(
                         {u_: reach_([u_], lambda w_: w_[0] in c_) for u_ in used_ if u_[0] in c_}))
                     for s_ in range(1, len(us_) + 1) for u_ in us_ for m_ in of_[u_[0]][u_[1]]]
# a step's tuple and stage; the step of a tuple's last instance at each stage; a tuple's last stage and its
# cycle; the step before each, where it is an earlier instance of its tuple at its stage
key_ = lambda x_: (x_[0], insts_[x_[0]][x_[1]][0], x_[2])
at_of_ = lambda st_: {key_(x_): k_ for k_, x_ in enumerate(st_)}
ends_ = lambda st_: {key_(x_)[:2]: (x_[2], x_[3]) for x_ in st_}
prev_ = lambda st_: [k_ - 1 if k_ and key_(st_[k_ - 1]) == key_(st_[k_]) else None for k_ in range(len(st_))]
# events: a fact's; a tuple's at stage s_ (None its last, 0 before the first); a step's coin and body, which
# reads the tuples of its own cycle at the stage before; the step's or the one before it
fact_ = lambda c_, v_: (yes_() if v_ else no_()) if c_ is None else coins_[c_] << {v_}
value_ = lambda a_, at_s_, end_, u_, v_, s_: (lambda t_: (no_() if v_ else yes_()) if t_ == 0
                                              else a_[at_s_[u_ + (t_,)]] << {v_})(end_[u_][0] if s_ is None else s_)
coin_ = lambda c_: [] if c_ is None else [coins_[c_[0]] << {c_[1]}]
step_ = lambda st_, end_, k_: (lambda q_, m_, s_, g_: all_(coin_(insts_[q_][m_][1]) + [
    at_[r_](j_, v_, s_ - 1 if w_ and end_[(r_, j_)][1] == g_ else None)
    for r_, j_, v_, w_ in insts_[q_][m_][2]]))(*st_[k_])
ev_ = lambda e_, p_, acc_: e_ if p_ is None else e_ | (acc_(p_) << {1})
holds_ = lambda q_, t_, v_: (lambda j_: (no_() if v_ else yes_()) if j_ is None else at_[q_](j_, v_, None))(
    ix_[q_].get(t_))

a_ft = [()]
a_fp = [0.3]
a_c0 = 0
a_cd = [{1: p_, 0: 1 - p_} for p_ in a_fp if p_ < 1]
a_fc = coins_of_(a_fp, a_c0)
# b/0: 1 facts, each a tuple and its probability
b_ft = [()]
b_fp = [0.4]
b_c0 = a_c0 + len(a_cd)
b_cd = [{1: p_, 0: 1 - p_} for p_ in b_fp if p_ < 1]
b_fc = coins_of_(b_fp, b_c0)

a_t = a_ft
a_i = index_(a_t)

b_t = b_ft
b_i = index_(b_t)

# rule 1: p :- a, b.
rule1_m = [((), (('p', ()),), [('a', j1, 1, 0), ('b', j2, 1, 0)])
    for j1 in [a_i.get(())] if j1 is not None
    for j2 in [b_i.get(())] if j2 is not None]
# rule 2: p :- \+ a, \+ b.
rule2_m = [((), (('p', ()),), [] + n2 + n4)
    for n2 in [[('a', j1, 0, 0) for j1 in [a_i.get(())] if j1 is not None]]
    for n4 in [[('b', j3, 0, 0) for j3 in [b_i.get(())] if j3 is not None]]]
p_t = dedup_(heads_('p', rule1_m + rule2_m))
p_i = index_(p_t)
p_inst = inst_('p', p_i, rule1_m, None, 0) + inst_('p', p_i, rule2_m, None, 0)
p_of = by_tuple_(p_inst, len(p_t))

at_ = {
    'a': lambda j_, v_, s_: fact_(a_fc[j_], v_),
    'b': lambda j_, v_, s_: fact_(b_fc[j_], v_),
    'p': lambda j_, v_, s_: value_(comp3_acc, comp3_at, comp3_end, ('p', j_), v_, s_),}
ix_ = {'a': a_i, 'b': b_i, 'p': p_i}
coin_d_ = a_cd + b_cd
insts_ = {'p': p_inst}
of_ = {'p': p_of}
# the tuples the queries and the evidence read, and those their instances read in turn
asked_ = [('p', ())]
used_ = reach_([(q_, ix_[q_][t_]) for q_, t_ in asked_ if t_ in ix_.get(q_, {})], lambda w_: True)
comp3_steps = steps_({'p'})
comp3_at = at_of_(comp3_steps)
comp3_end = ends_(comp3_steps)
comp3_prev = prev_(comp3_steps)
comp3_ev = lambda k_: ev_(step_(comp3_steps, comp3_end, k_), comp3_prev[k_], lambda i_: comp3_acc[i_])
queries_ = lambda: [holds_('p', (), 1)]

coins_ = array(len(coin_d_))
comp3_acc = array(len(comp3_steps))

true_ ~= atomic(loc=1)
for n_ in range(len(coin_d_)):
    coins_[n_] ~= discrete(coin_d_[n_])
# p/0: an instance holds where its body or an earlier instance of its tuple does
for k_ in range(len(comp3_steps)):
    if comp3_ev(k_):
        comp3_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=1)
    else:
        comp3_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=0)

  ix)

(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))
;; the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

(define (constant s) (or (string->number s) (string->symbol s)))
;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
(define (facts path)
  (define db (make-hash))
  (for ([line (in-lines (open-input-file path))])
    (define f (string-split line "\t" #:trim? #f))
    (define p (string->number (cadr f)))
    (add! (hash-ref! db (car f) make-hash) (map constant (cddr f)) (if (>= p 1) #t (flip p))))

;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone.

  (define (datum s)
    (define d (read (open-input-string s)))
    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))
  (define rows
    (for/list ([line (in-list (string-split text "\n"))]
               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))
  (if (null? rows)

      (for/list ([r (in-list rows)]

(define b-facts (hash-ref db "b/0" (make-hash)))

(define b b-facts)

  (for ([x1 (in-list (probe a (list)))])
    (for ([x2 (in-list (probe b (list)))])

  ;; 0.7::p :- \+ a, b.

    (add! p (list) (&& (! (holds a (list))) x1 (flip 0.7))))

  (for ([x1 (in-list (probe p (list)))])
    (for ([x2 (in-list (probe b (list)))])
      (add! evidence- (list) (&& x1 x2)))))

(statement (observe! (holds evidence- (list))))
(define dists
  (list (distribution (holds a (list)))))
(statement (report dists))

/*
Existence uncertainty/unknown objects.
This programs models a domain where the number of objects is uncertain.
In particular, the number of objects follows a geometric distribution 
with parameter 0.7.
We can ask what is the probability that the object number n exists.
From
Poole, David. "The independent choice logic and beyond." Probabilistic 
inductive logic programming. Springer Berlin Heidelberg, 2008. 222-243.
*/


:- use_module(library(pita)).

:- if(current_predicate(use_rendering/1)).
:- use_rendering(c3).
:- endif.

:- pita.

:- set_pita(depth_bound,true).
:- set_pita(depth,5).

:- begin_lpad.
numObj(N, N) :-
  \+ more(N).

numObj(N, N2) :-
  more(N),
  N1 is N + 1,
  numObj(N1, N2).

more(_):0.3.

obj(I):-
 numObj(0,N),
 between(1, N, I).

:- end_lpad.



/** <examples>

?- prob(obj(2),P). what is the probability that object 2 exists?
% expected result 0.08189999999999999
?- prob(obj(2),P),bar(P,C). what is the probability that object 2 exists?
% expected result 0.08189999999999999
?- prob(numObj(0,2),P). % what is the probability that there are 2 objects?
% expected result 0.063

*/

main :-
    forall((Q = obj(2), prob(Q, P)), format("~q:\t~w~n", [Q, P])),
    forall((Q = numObj(0,2), prob(Q, P)), format("~q:\t~w~n", [Q, P])).

    (add! (hash-ref! db (car f) make-hash) (map constant (cddr f)) (if (>= p 1) #t (flip p))))
  db)

;; The distribution of v, a list of (value . probability): Roulette's query
;; at the module's level (`display-pmf`), read back from the table it
;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone.
(define (distribution v)
  (define text (with-output-to-string (λ () (display-pmf v))))
  (define (datum s)
    (define d (read (open-input-string s)))
    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))
  (define rows
    (for/list ([line (in-list (string-split text "\n"))]
               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))
  (if (null? rows)
      (list (cons (datum text) 1))
      (for/list ([r (in-list rows)]
                 #:unless (equal? r '("Value" "Probability")))
        (cons (datum (car r)) (string->number (cadr r))))))
(define (real p) (if (exact? p) (exact->inexact p) p))
(define (probability dist v)
  (define e (assoc v dist))
  (if e (cdr e) 0))
(define (report dists)
  (for ([dist (in-list dists)] [k (in-naturals 1)])
    (printf "roulette ~a true ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #t)))
    (printf "roulette ~a false ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #f)))))

(define db (facts (vector-ref (current-command-line-arguments) 0)))
(define toss-facts (hash-ref db "toss/1" (make-hash)))

(define toss toss-facts)

(define demand-1 (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; demand_1(Coin) :- toss(Coin).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs toss)])
    (match-define (cons (list Coin) x1) t2)
    (add! demand-1 (list Coin) #t))
  ;; demand_1(Coin) :- toss(Coin).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs toss)])
    (match-define (cons (list Coin) x1) t2)
    (add! demand-1 (list Coin) #t)))

(define biased (make-hash))
(define fair (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; 0.9::fair(Coin); 0.1::biased(Coin) :- demand_1(Coin).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs demand-1)])
    (match-define (cons (list Coin) x1) t2)
    (let ([chosen (choose 0.9 0.1)])
      (add! fair (list Coin) (&& x1 (list-ref chosen 0)))
      (add! biased (list Coin) (&& x1 (list-ref chosen 1))))))

(define heads (make-hash))
(define tails (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; 0.5::heads(Coin); 0.5::tails(Coin) :- toss(Coin), fair(Coin).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs toss)])
    (match-define (cons (list Coin) x1) t2)
    (for ([x3 (in-list (probe fair (list Coin)))])
      (let ([chosen (choose 0.5 0.5)])
        (add! heads (list Coin) (&& x1 x3 (list-ref chosen 0)))
        (add! tails (list Coin) (&& x1 x3 (list-ref chosen 1))))))
  ;; 0.6::heads(Coin); 0.4::tails(Coin) :- toss(Coin), biased(Coin).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs toss)])
    (match-define (cons (list Coin) x1) t2)
    (for ([x3 (in-list (probe biased (list Coin)))])
      (let ([chosen (choose 0.6 0.4)])
        (add! heads (list Coin) (&& x1 x3 (list-ref chosen 0)))
        (add! tails (list Coin) (&& x1 x3 (list-ref chosen 1)))))))

(define dists
  (list (distribution (holds heads (list 'coin2)))
        (distribution (holds tails (list 'coin2)))
        (distribution (holds heads (list 'coin1)))
        (distribution (holds tails (list 'coin1)))))
(statement (report dists))

# cplint_eruption.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    sudden_energy_release_facts = get(db, "sudden_energy_release/0", Relation())
    fault_rupture_facts = get(db, "fault_rupture/1", Relation())

    fault_rupture = fault_rupture_facts

    sudden_energy_release = sudden_energy_release_facts

    earthquake = Relation()
    eruption = Relation()
    # 0.6::eruption; 0.3::earthquake :- sudden_energy_release, fault_rupture(_A1).
    for x1 in probe(sudden_energy_release, ())
        for ((_A1,), x2) in fault_rupture
            chosen = choose(0.6, 0.3)
            add!(eruption, (), x1 & x2 & chosen[1])
            add!(earthquake, (), x1 & x2 & chosen[2])
        end
    end

    queries = (holds(eruption, ()), holds(earthquake, ()))
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

# cplint_swish_admission.pl: a ProbLog program written in SPPL by tddlog's scripts/problog2ppl.py,
# first order as it is written. The facts and the joins of the rules are Python
# constants, computed before the first sample: each rule's matches a list
# comprehension over the relations its body joins, a recursive component's
# tuples a fixpoint of its rules, and the tuples that the queries and the
# evidence read. Then each probabilistic fact and each instance of a
# probabilistic rule samples a coin, and each instance of a tuple that is read
# sets a variable of its own, in a `for` over its component's instances: 1
# where its body holds or an earlier instance of its tuple does, the last of a
# tuple's instances its holding. A cycle of tuples that read each other does so
# in as many stages as it has tuples, each stage reading the one before. The
# queries are the events of queries_(), asked of the model given the evidence:
#
#   sppl_dice.py PROGRAM.sppl
#
# queries
# component 0 bool query0

from functools import reduce
from itertools import accumulate

yes_ = lambda: true_ << {1}
no_ = lambda: true_ << {0}
all_ = lambda es_: reduce(lambda a_, b_: a_ & b_, es_) if es_ else yes_()
fix_ = lambda g_, x_: (lambda y_: x_ if y_ == x_ else fix_(g_, y_))(g_(x_))
dedup_ = lambda xs_: list(dict.fromkeys(xs_))
index_ = lambda ts_: {t_: j_ for j_, t_ in enumerate(ts_)}
by_ = lambda ts_, ps_: reduce(lambda d_, j_: d_.setdefault(tuple(ts_[j_][p_] for p_ in ps_), []).append(j_) or d_,
                              range(len(ts_)), {})
idiv_ = lambda a_, b_: abs(a_) // abs(b_) * (1 if (a_ < 0) == (b_ < 0) else -1)
# the heads of relation q_ that matches ms_ give; a coin's index for each probability below 1
heads_ = lambda q_, ms_: [h_ for m_ in ms_ for r_, h_ in m_[1] if r_ == q_]
coins_of_ = lambda ps_, c0_: [None if p_ >= 1 else c0_ + n_
                              for p_, n_ in zip(ps_, accumulate([0] + [int(x_ < 1) for x_ in ps_]))]
# a relation's instances, each (its tuple's index, its coin and value or None, its refs); their indexes by tuple
facts_ = lambda i_, ts_, cs_: [(i_[t_], None if c_ is None else (c_, 1), []) for t_, c_ in zip(ts_, cs_)]
inst_ = lambda q_, i_, ms_, ks_, c0_: [(i_[h_], None if ks_ is None else (c0_ + ks_[m_[0]], n_ + 1), m_[2])
                                      for m_ in ms_ for n_, (r_, h_) in enumerate(m_[1]) if r_ == q_]
by_tuple_ = lambda es_, n_: (lambda d_: [d_.get((j_,), []) for j_ in range(n_)])(by_(es_, (0,)))
# the tuples (relation, index) that a tuple's instances read; those that tuples us_ read in turn, where ok_
reads_ = lambda u_: ([(r_, k_) for m_ in of_[u_[0]][u_[1]] for r_, k_, _, _ in insts_[u_[0]][m_][2]]
                     if u_[0] in of_ else [])
reach_ = lambda us_, ok_: fix_(lambda s_: s_ | {w_ for u_ in s_ for w_ in reads_(u_) if ok_(w_)}, frozenset(us_))
# a component's steps, each (relation, instance, stage, cycle), over the tuples of its relations c_ that the
# queries and the evidence read: its cycles of tuples (the tuples that reach the same ones), each after the
# cycles it reads (which reach fewer), in as many stages as it has tuples, each stage reading the one before
cycles_ = lambda rs_: sorted(reduce(lambda d_, u_: d_.setdefault(rs_[u_], []).append(u_) or d_, sorted(rs_),
                                    {}).values(), key=lambda us_: (len(rs_[us_[0]]), us_[0]))
steps_ = lambda c_: [(u_[0], m_, s_, g_) for g_, us_ in enumerate(cycles_(
                         {u_: reach_([u_], lambda w_: w_[0] in c_) for u_ in used_ if u_[0] in c_}))
                     for s_ in range(1, len(us_) + 1) for u_ in us_ for m_ in of_[u_[0]][u_[1]]]
# a step's tuple and stage; the step of a tuple's last instance at each stage; a tuple's last stage and its
# cycle; the step before each, where it is an earlier instance of its tuple at its stage
key_ = lambda x_: (x_[0], insts_[x_[0]][x_[1]][0], x_[2])
at_of_ = lambda st_: {key_(x_): k_ for k_, x_ in enumerate(st_)}
ends_ = lambda st_: {key_(x_)[:2]: (x_[2], x_[3]) for x_ in st_}
prev_ = lambda st_: [k_ - 1 if k_ and key_(st_[k_ - 1]) == key_(st_[k_]) else None for k_ in range(len(st_))]
# events: a fact's; a tuple's at stage s_ (None its last, 0 before the first); a step's coin and body, which
# reads the tuples of its own cycle at the stage before; the step's or the one before it
fact_ = lambda c_, v_: (yes_() if v_ else no_()) if c_ is None else coins_[c_] << {v_}
value_ = lambda a_, at_s_, end_, u_, v_, s_: (lambda t_: (no_() if v_ else yes_()) if t_ == 0
                                              else a_[at_s_[u_ + (t_,)]] << {v_})(end_[u_][0] if s_ is None else s_)
coin_ = lambda c_: [] if c_ is None else [coins_[c_[0]] << {c_[1]}]
step_ = lambda st_, end_, k_: (lambda q_, m_, s_, g_: all_(coin_(insts_[q_][m_][1]) + [
    at_[r_](j_, v_, s_ - 1 if w_ and end_[(r_, j_)][1] == g_ else None)
    for r_, j_, v_, w_ in insts_[q_][m_][2]]))(*st_[k_])
ev_ = lambda e_, p_, acc_: e_ if p_ is None else e_ | (acc_(p_) << {1})
holds_ = lambda q_, t_, v_: (lambda j_: (no_() if v_ else yes_()) if j_ is None else at_[q_](j_, v_, None))(
    ix_[q_].get(t_))

# female/0: 1 facts, each a tuple and its probability
female_ft = [()]
female_fp = [0.5]
female_c0 = 0
female_cd = [{1: p_, 0: 1 - p_} for p_ in female_fp if p_ < 1]
female_fc = coins_of_(female_fp, female_c0)
# qualified/0: 1 facts, each a tuple and its probability
qualified_ft = [()]
qualified_fp = [0.5]
qualified_c0 = female_c0 + len(female_cd)
qualified_cd = [{1: p_, 0: 1 - p_} for p_ in qualified_fp if p_ < 1]
qualified_fc = coins_of_(qualified_fp, qualified_c0)

female_t = female_ft
female_i = index_(female_t)

# rule 3: deptB :- female.
rule3_m = [((), (('deptB', ()),), [('female', j1, 1, 0)])
    for j1 in [female_i.get(())] if j1 is not None]
# rule 4: 0.5::deptB :- \+ female.
rule4_m = [((), (('deptB', ()),), [] + n2)
    for n2 in [[('female', j1, 0, 0) for j1 in [female_i.get(())] if j1 is not None]]]
deptB_t = dedup_(heads_('deptB', rule3_m + rule4_m))
deptB_i = index_(deptB_t)
rule4_k = index_(dedup_([m_[0] for m_ in rule4_m]))
rule4_c0 = qualified_c0 + len(qualified_cd)
rule4_cd = [{1: 0.5, 0: 1 - (0.5)}] * len(rule4_k)
deptB_inst = inst_('deptB', deptB_i, rule3_m, None, 0) + inst_('deptB', deptB_i, rule4_m, rule4_k, rule4_c0)
deptB_of = by_tuple_(deptB_inst, len(deptB_t))

qualified_t = qualified_ft
qualified_i = index_(qualified_t)

# rule 1: admitted :- deptB, female, qualified.
rule1_m = [((), (('admitted', ()),), [('deptB', j1, 1, 0), ('female', j2, 1, 0), ('qualified', j3, 1, 0)])
    for j1 in [deptB_i.get(())] if j1 is not None
    for j2 in [female_i.get(())] if j2 is not None
    for j3 in [qualified_i.get(())] if j3 is not None]
# rule 2: admitted :- \+ deptB, \+ female.
rule2_m = [((), (('admitted', ()),), [] + n2 + n4)
    for n2 in [[('deptB', j1, 0, 0) for j1 in [deptB_i.get(())] if j1 is not None]]
    for n4 in [[('female', j3, 0, 0) for j3 in [female_i.get(())] if j3 is not None]]]
admitted_t = dedup_(heads_('admitted', rule1_m + rule2_m))
admitted_i = index_(admitted_t)
admitted_inst = inst_('admitted', admitted_i, rule1_m, None, 0) + inst_('admitted', admitted_i, rule2_m, None, 0)
admitted_of = by_tuple_(admitted_inst, len(admitted_t))

at_ = {
    'female': lambda j_, v_, s_: fact_(female_fc[j_], v_),
    'deptB': lambda j_, v_, s_: value_(comp2_acc, comp2_at, comp2_end, ('deptB', j_), v_, s_),
    'qualified': lambda j_, v_, s_: fact_(qualified_fc[j_], v_),
    'admitted': lambda j_, v_, s_: value_(comp4_acc, comp4_at, comp4_end, ('admitted', j_), v_, s_),}
ix_ = {'female': female_i, 'deptB': deptB_i, 'qualified': qualified_i, 'admitted': admitted_i}
coin_d_ = female_cd + qualified_cd + rule4_cd
insts_ = {'deptB': deptB_inst, 'admitted': admitted_inst}
of_ = {'deptB': deptB_of, 'admitted': admitted_of}
# the tuples the queries and the evidence read, and those their instances read in turn
asked_ = [('admitted', ()), ('female', ())]
used_ = reach_([(q_, ix_[q_][t_]) for q_, t_ in asked_ if t_ in ix_.get(q_, {})], lambda w_: True)
comp2_steps = steps_({'deptB'})
comp2_at = at_of_(comp2_steps)
comp2_end = ends_(comp2_steps)
comp2_prev = prev_(comp2_steps)
comp2_ev = lambda k_: ev_(step_(comp2_steps, comp2_end, k_), comp2_prev[k_], lambda i_: comp2_acc[i_])
comp4_steps = steps_({'admitted'})
comp4_at = at_of_(comp4_steps)
comp4_end = ends_(comp4_steps)
comp4_prev = prev_(comp4_steps)
comp4_ev = lambda k_: ev_(step_(comp4_steps, comp4_end, k_), comp4_prev[k_], lambda i_: comp4_acc[i_])
queries_ = lambda: [holds_('admitted', (), 1)]
evidence_ = lambda: all_([holds_('female', (), 1)])

coins_ = array(len(coin_d_))
comp2_acc = array(len(comp2_steps))
comp4_acc = array(len(comp4_steps))

true_ ~= atomic(loc=1)
for n_ in range(len(coin_d_)):
    coins_[n_] ~= discrete(coin_d_[n_])
# deptB/0: an instance holds where its body or an earlier instance of its tuple does
for k_ in range(len(comp2_steps)):
    if comp2_ev(k_):
        comp2_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=1)
    else:
        comp2_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=0)
# admitted/0: an instance holds where its body or an earlier instance of its tuple does
for k_ in range(len(comp4_steps)):
    if comp4_ev(k_):
        comp4_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=1)
    else:
        comp4_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=0)
condition(evidence_())

:- use_module(library(pita)).

:- pita.

:- begin_lpad.

holdsAt(F, T) :-
  initially(F),
  \+ clipped(0, F, T).
holdsAt(F, T2) :- 
  initiates(F, T1),
  T1 < T2 ,
  \+ clipped(T1 ,F, T2 ).
clipped(T1 ,F, T3) :-
  terminates(F, T2),
  T1 < T2 , T2 < T3.

initiates(locatedIn(A, B), T):0.66 :- 
  happens(arrive(A, B), T).
terminates(locatedIn(A, D), T):0.66 :-
  happens(arrive(A, B), T),
  B \= D.
initially(locatedIn(bob, garden)).
happens(arrive(bob, kitchen), 3). 
happens(arrive(bob, garage), 5).

:- end_lpad.

?- prob(holdsAt(locatedIn(bob,garden),2),P).
% 1.0
?- prob(holdsAt(locatedIn(bob,garden),4),P). 
% 0.34
?- prob(holdsAt(locatedIn(bob,kitchen),4),P).
% 0.66
?- prob(holdsAt(locatedIn(bob,garage),6),P).
% 0.66.

yes_ = lambda: true_ << {1}
no_ = lambda: true_ << {0}
all_ = lambda es_: reduce(lambda a_, b_: a_ & b_, es_) if es_ else yes_()
fix_ = lambda g_, x_: (lambda y_: x_ if y_ == x_ else fix_(g_, y_))(g_(x_))
dedup_ = lambda xs_: list(dict.fromkeys(xs_))
index_ = lambda ts_: {t_: j_ for j_, t_ in enumerate(ts_)}
by_ = lambda ts_, ps_: reduce(lambda d_, j_: d_.setdefault(tuple(ts_[j_][p_] for p_ in ps_), []).append(j_) or d_,
                              range(len(ts_)), {})
idiv_ = lambda a_, b_: abs(a_) // abs(b_) * (1 if (a_ < 0) == (b_ < 0) else -1)
# the heads of relation q_ that matches ms_ give; a coin's index for each probability below 1
heads_ = lambda q_, ms_: [h_ for m_ in ms_ for r_, h_ in m_[1] if r_ == q_]
coins_of_ = lambda ps_, c0_: [None if p_ >= 1 else c0_ + n_
                              for p_, n_ in zip(ps_, accumulate([0] + [int(x_ < 1) for x_ in ps_]))]
# a relation's instances, each (its tuple's index, its coin and value or None, its refs); their indexes by tuple
facts_ = lambda i_, ts_, cs_: [(i_[t_], None if c_ is None else (c_, 1), []) for t_, c_ in zip(ts_, cs_)]
inst_ = lambda q_, i_, ms_, ks_, c0_: [(i_[h_], None if ks_ is None else (c0_ + ks_[m_[0]], n_ + 1), m_[2])
                                      for m_ in ms_ for n_, (r_, h_) in enumerate(m_[1]) if r_ == q_]
by_tuple_ = lambda es_, n_: (lambda d_: [d_.get((j_,), []) for j_ in range(n_)])(by_(es_, (0,)))
# the tuples (relation, index) that a tuple's instances read; those that tuples us_ read in turn, where ok_
reads_ = lambda u_: ([(r_, k_) for m_ in of_[u_[0]][u_[1]] for r_, k_, _, _ in insts_[u_[0]][m_][2]]
                     if u_[0] in of_ else [])
reach_ = lambda us_, ok_: fix_(lambda s_: s_ | {w_ for u_ in s_ for w_ in reads_(u_) if ok_(w_)}, frozenset(us_))
# a component's steps, each (relation, instance, stage, cycle), over the tuples of its relations c_ that the
# queries and the evidence read: its cycles of tuples (the tuples that reach the same ones), each after the
# cycles it reads (which reach fewer), in as many stages as it has tuples, each stage reading the one before
cycles_ = lambda rs_: sorted(reduce(lambda d_, u_: d_.setdefault(rs_[u_], []).append(u_) or d_, sorted(rs_),
                                    {}).values(), key=lambda us_: (len(rs_[us_[0]]), us_[0]))
steps_ = lambda c_: [(u_[0], m_, s_, g_) for g_, us_ in enumerate(cycles_(
                         {u_: reach_([u_], lambda w_: w_[0] in c_) for u_ in used_ if u_[0] in c_}))
                     for s_ in range(1, len(us_) + 1) for u_ in us_ for m_ in of_[u_[0]][u_[1]]]
# a step's tuple and stage; the step of a tuple's last instance at each stage; a tuple's last stage and its
# cycle; the step before each, where it is an earlier instance of its tuple at its stage
key_ = lambda x_: (x_[0], insts_[x_[0]][x_[1]][0], x_[2])
at_of_ = lambda st_: {key_(x_): k_ for k_, x_ in enumerate(st_)}
ends_ = lambda st_: {key_(x_)[:2]: (x_[2], x_[3]) for x_ in st_}
prev_ = lambda st_: [k_ - 1 if k_ and key_(st_[k_ - 1]) == key_(st_[k_]) else None for k_ in range(len(st_))]
# events: a fact's; a tuple's at stage s_ (None its last, 0 before the first); a step's coin and body, which
# reads the tuples of its own cycle at the stage before; the step's or the one before it
fact_ = lambda c_, v_: (yes_() if v_ else no_()) if c_ is None else coins_[c_] << {v_}
value_ = lambda a_, at_s_, end_, u_, v_, s_: (lambda t_: (no_() if v_ else yes_()) if t_ == 0
                                              else a_[at_s_[u_ + (t_,)]] << {v_})(end_[u_][0] if s_ is None else s_)
coin_ = lambda c_: [] if c_ is None else [coins_[c_[0]] << {c_[1]}]
step_ = lambda st_, end_, k_: (lambda q_, m_, s_, g_: all_(coin_(insts_[q_][m_][1]) + [
    at_[r_](j_, v_, s_ - 1 if w_ and end_[(r_, j_)][1] == g_ else None)
    for r_, j_, v_, w_ in insts_[q_][m_][2]]))(*st_[k_])
ev_ = lambda e_, p_, acc_: e_ if p_ is None else e_ | (acc_(p_) << {1})
holds_ = lambda q_, t_, v_: (lambda j_: (no_() if v_ else yes_()) if j_ is None else at_[q_](j_, v_, None))(
    ix_[q_].get(t_))

# push/0: 1 facts, each a tuple and its probability
push_ft = [()]
push_fp = [1.0]
push_c0 = 0
push_cd = [{1: p_, 0: 1 - p_} for p_ in push_fp if p_ < 1]
push_fc = coins_of_(push_fp, push_c0)

push_t = push_ft
push_i = index_(push_t)

# rule 1: 0.4::light :- push.
rule1_m = [((), (('light', ()),), [('push', j1, 1, 0)])
    for j1 in [push_i.get(())] if j1 is not None]
light_t = dedup_(heads_('light', rule1_m))
light_i = index_(light_t)
rule1_k = index_(dedup_([m_[0] for m_ in rule1_m]))
rule1_c0 = push_c0 + len(push_cd)
rule1_cd = [{1: 0.4, 0: 1 - (0.4)}] * len(rule1_k)
light_inst = inst_('light', light_i, rule1_m, rule1_k, rule1_c0)
light_of = by_tuple_(light_inst, len(light_t))

# rule 2: replace :- \+ light.
rule2_m = [((), (('replace', ()),), [] + n2)
    for n2 in [[('light', j1, 0, 0) for j1 in [light_i.get(())] if j1 is not None]]]
replace_t = dedup_(heads_('replace', rule2_m))
replace_i = index_(replace_t)
replace_inst = inst_('replace', replace_i, rule2_m, None, 0)
replace_of = by_tuple_(replace_inst, len(replace_t))

at_ = {
    'push': lambda j_, v_, s_: fact_(push_fc[j_], v_),
    'light': lambda j_, v_, s_: value_(comp2_acc, comp2_at, comp2_end, ('light', j_), v_, s_),
    'replace': lambda j_, v_, s_: value_(comp3_acc, comp3_at, comp3_end, ('replace', j_), v_, s_),}
ix_ = {'push': push_i, 'light': light_i, 'replace': replace_i}
coin_d_ = push_cd + rule1_cd
insts_ = {'light': light_inst, 'replace': replace_inst}
of_ = {'light': light_of, 'replace': replace_of}
# the tuples the queries and the evidence read, and those their instances read in turn
asked_ = [('replace', ()), ('light', ())]
used_ = reach_([(q_, ix_[q_][t_]) for q_, t_ in asked_ if t_ in ix_.get(q_, {})], lambda w_: True)
comp2_steps = steps_({'light'})
comp2_at = at_of_(comp2_steps)
comp2_end = ends_(comp2_steps)
comp2_prev = prev_(comp2_steps)
comp2_ev = lambda k_: ev_(step_(comp2_steps, comp2_end, k_), comp2_prev[k_], lambda i_: comp2_acc[i_])
comp3_steps = steps_({'replace'})
comp3_at = at_of_(comp3_steps)
comp3_end = ends_(comp3_steps)
comp3_prev = prev_(comp3_steps)
comp3_ev = lambda k_: ev_(step_(comp3_steps, comp3_end, k_), comp3_prev[k_], lambda i_: comp3_acc[i_])
queries_ = lambda: [holds_('replace', (), 1), holds_('light', (), 1)]

coins_ = array(len(coin_d_))
comp2_acc = array(len(comp2_steps))
comp3_acc = array(len(comp3_steps))

true_ ~= atomic(loc=1)
for n_ in range(len(coin_d_)):
    coins_[n_] ~= discrete(coin_d_[n_])
# light/0: an instance holds where its body or an earlier instance of its tuple does
for k_ in range(len(comp2_steps)):
    if comp2_ev(k_):
        comp2_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=1)
    else:
        comp2_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=0)
# replace/0: an instance holds where its body or an earlier instance of its tuple does
for k_ in range(len(comp3_steps)):
    if comp3_ev(k_):
        comp3_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=1)
    else:
        comp3_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=0)

#lang roulette/example/disrupt
;; cplint_alarm.pl: a ProbLog program written for Roulette by tddlog's
;; scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a hash
;; from its tuples (lists of constants) to whether each holds, a Boolean of the
;; coins; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from the
;; facts file named on the command line; each rule is a loop over the
;; relations its body joins. Each query's distribution is Roulette's, at the
;; module's level (`display-pmf`), given the evidence; the program prints
;; `roulette K true P` and `roulette K false P` for the K-th query.

(require racket/port racket/string racket/match)

;; A statement of the program: a definition, which the language does not
;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

;; the tuple t of r holds also where x does
(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))
;; whether the tuple t of r holds
(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))
;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their
;; values at positions ps (from 0)
(define (index r . ps)
  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])
    (hash-update! ix (for/list ([p (in-list ps)]) (list-ref t p)) (λ (es) (cons (cons t x) es)) null))
  ix)
;; whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))
;; the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

(define (constant s) (or (string->number s) (string->symbol s)))
;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
(define (facts path)
  (define db (make-hash))
  (for ([line (in-lines (open-input-file path))])
    (define f (string-split line "\t" #:trim? #f))
    (define p (string->number (cadr f)))
    (add! (hash-ref! db (car f) make-hash) (map constant (cddr f)) (if (>= p 1) #t (flip p))))
  db)

;; The distribution of v, a list of (value . probability): Roulette's query
;; at the module's level (`display-pmf`), read back from the table it
;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone.
(define (distribution v)
  (define text (with-output-to-string (λ () (display-pmf v))))
  (define (datum s)
    (define d (read (open-input-string s)))
    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))
  (define rows
    (for/list ([line (in-list (string-split text "\n"))]
               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))
  (if (null? rows)
      (list (cons (datum text) 1))
      (for/list ([r (in-list rows)]
                 #:unless (equal? r '("Value" "Probability")))
        (cons (datum (car r)) (string->number (cadr r))))))
(define (real p) (if (exact? p) (exact->inexact p) p))
(define (probability dist v)
  (define e (assoc v dist))
  (if e (cdr e) 0))
(define (report dists)
  (for ([dist (in-list dists)] [k (in-naturals 1)])
    (printf "roulette ~a true ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #t)))
    (printf "roulette ~a false ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #f)))))

(define db (facts (vector-ref (current-command-line-arguments) 0)))

(define burg (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; 0.1::burg(t); 0.9::burg(f).
  (let ([chosen (choose 0.1 0.9)])
    (add! burg (list 't) (list-ref chosen 0))
    (add! burg (list 'f) (list-ref chosen 1))))

(define earthq (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; 0.2::earthq(t); 0.8::earthq(f).
  (let ([chosen (choose 0.2 0.8)])
    (add! earthq (list 't) (list-ref chosen 0))
    (add! earthq (list 'f) (list-ref chosen 1))))

(define alarm (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; alarm(t) :- burg(t), earthq(t).
  (for ([x1 (in-list (probe burg (list 't)))])
    (for ([x2 (in-list (probe earthq (list 't)))])
      (add! alarm (list 't) (&& x1 x2))))
  ;; 0.8::alarm(t); 0.2::alarm(f) :- burg(t), earthq(f).
  (for ([x1 (in-list (probe burg (list 't)))])
    (for ([x2 (in-list (probe earthq (list 'f)))])
      (let ([chosen (choose 0.8 0.2)])
        (add! alarm (list 't) (&& x1 x2 (list-ref chosen 0)))
        (add! alarm (list 'f) (&& x1 x2 (list-ref chosen 1))))))
  ;; 0.8::alarm(t); 0.2::alarm(f) :- burg(f), earthq(t).
  (for ([x1 (in-list (probe burg (list 'f)))])
    (for ([x2 (in-list (probe earthq (list 't)))])
      (let ([chosen (choose 0.8 0.2)])
        (add! alarm (list 't) (&& x1 x2 (list-ref chosen 0)))
        (add! alarm (list 'f) (&& x1 x2 (list-ref chosen 1))))))
  ;; 0.1::alarm(t); 0.9::alarm(f) :- burg(f), earthq(f).
  (for ([x1 (in-list (probe burg (list 'f)))])
    (for ([x2 (in-list (probe earthq (list 'f)))])
      (let ([chosen (choose 0.1 0.9)])
        (add! alarm (list 't) (&& x1 x2 (list-ref chosen 0)))
        (add! alarm (list 'f) (&& x1 x2 (list-ref chosen 1)))))))

(define dists
  (list (distribution (holds alarm (list 't)))
        (distribution (holds alarm (list 'f)))))
(statement (report dists))

/*
This program models the occurrence of an earthquake depending on its possible 
causes.
From
F. Riguzzi and N. Di Mauro. Applying the information bottleneck to statistical 
relational learning. Machine Learning, 86(1):89-114, 2012
*/
:- use_module(library(pita)).

:- if(current_predicate(use_rendering/1)).
:- use_rendering(c3).
:- endif.

:- pita.

:- begin_lpad.

earthquake(X, strong) : 0.3 ; earthquake(X, moderate) : 0.5 :-
  fault_rupture(X).
% if an earthquake at a site X is caused only by the rupture of a 
% geological fault, we have a strong earthquake with probability 0.3, 
% a moderate earthquake with probability 0.5 and no earthquake with probability 
% 0.2

earthquake(X, strong) : 0.2 ; earthquake(X, moderate) : 0.6 :-
  volcanic_eruption(X).
% if an earthquake at a site X is caused only by a volcanic eruption, 
% we have a strong earthquake with probability 0.2, 
% a moderate earthquake with probability 0.6 and no earthquake with probability 
% 0.2


fault_rupture(stromboli).
% there is a fault rupture at stromboli

volcanic_eruption(stromboli).
% there is a volcanic eruption at stromboli

volcanic_eruption(eyjafjallajkull).
% there is a volcanic eruption at eyjafjallajkull

:- end_lpad.

/** <examples>

?- prob(earthquake(stromboli,strong),Prob).  % what is the probability of a strong 
% earthquake at stromboli?
% expected result 0.43999999999999995
?- prob(earthquake(stromboli,moderate),Prob).  % what is the probability of a moderate
% earthquake at stromboli?
% expected result 0.7999999999999998
?- prob(earthquake(eyjafjallajkull,strong),Prob).  % what is the probability of a strong 
% earthquake at eyjafjallajkull?
% expected result 0.2
?- prob(earthquake(eyjafjallajkull,moderate),Prob). % what is the probability of a moderate
% earthquake at eyjafjallajkull?
% expected result 0.6
?- prob(earthquake(stromboli,strong),Prob),bar(Prob,C).  % what is the probability of a strong 
% earthquake at stromboli?
% expected result 0.43999999999999995
?- prob(earthquake(stromboli,moderate),Prob),bar(Prob,C).  % what is the probability of a moderate
% earthquake at stromboli?
% expected result 0.7999999999999998
?- prob(earthquake(eyjafjallajkull,strong),Prob),bar(Prob,C).  % what is the probability of a strong 
% earthquake at eyjafjallajkull?
% expected result 0.2
?- prob(earthquake(eyjafjallajkull,moderate),Prob),bar(Prob,C). % what is the probability of a moderate
% earthquake at eyjafjallajkull?
% expected result 0.6


*/

main :-
    forall((Q = earthquake(stromboli,strong), prob(Q, P)), format("~q:\t~w~n", [Q, P])),
    forall((Q = earthquake(stromboli,moderate), prob(Q, P)), format("~q:\t~w~n", [Q, P])),
    forall((Q = earthquake(eyjafjallajkull,strong), prob(Q, P)), format("~q:\t~w~n", [Q, P])),
    forall((Q = earthquake(eyjafjallajkull,moderate), prob(Q, P)), format("~q:\t~w~n", [Q, P])).
texts.24396a9e008bb5e30831d1dd9337ed3d57f1656c:
# cplint_trigger.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    pull_trigger_facts = get(db, "pull_trigger/1", Relation())

    pull_trigger = pull_trigger_facts

    death = Relation()
    # 0.16666666666666666::death :- pull_trigger(left_gun).
    for x1 in probe(pull_trigger, (:left_gun,))
        add!(death, (), x1 & flip(0.16666666666666666))
    end
    # 0.16666666666666666::death :- pull_trigger(right_gun).
    for x1 in probe(pull_trigger, (:right_gun,))
        add!(death, (), x1 & flip(0.16666666666666666))
    end

    queries = (holds(death, ()),)
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

A six-sided die is repeatedly thrown until the outcome is six.
on(T,F) means that on the Tth throw the face F came out.
From
J. Vennekens, S. Verbaeten, and M. Bruynooghe. Logic programs with annotated 
disjunctions. In International Conference on Logic Programming, 
volume 3131 of LNCS, pages 195-209. Springer, 2004.

:- use_module(library(pita)).

:- if(current_predicate(use_rendering/1)).
:- use_rendering(c3).
:- endif.

:- pita.

:- begin_lpad.

% on(T,F) means that the die landed on face F at time T

on(0,1):1/6;on(0,2):1/6;on(0,3):1/6;
on(0,4):1/6;on(0,5):1/6;on(0,6):1/6.
% at time 0 the dice lands on one of its faces with equal probability

on(X,1):1/6;on(X,2):1/6;on(X,3):1/6;
on(X,4):1/6;on(X,5):1/6;on(X,6):1/6:-
  X1 is X-1,X1>=0,on(X1,_),
  \+ on(X1,6).
% at time T the die lands on one of its faces with equal probability if
% at the previous time point it was thrown and it did not land on face 6

  on(0,1),
  on(1,1).

:- end_lpad.

#lang roulette/example/disrupt
;; cplint_swish_admission.pl: a ProbLog program written for Roulette by tddlog's
;; scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a hash
;; from its tuples (lists of constants) to whether each holds, a Boolean of the
;; coins; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from the
;; facts file named on the command line; each rule is a loop over the
;; relations its body joins. Each query's distribution is Roulette's, at the
;; module's level (`display-pmf`), given the evidence; the program prints
;; `roulette K true P` and `roulette K false P` for the K-th query.

(require racket/port racket/string racket/match)

;; A statement of the program: a definition, which the language does not
;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

;; the tuple t of r holds also where x does
(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))
;; whether the tuple t of r holds
(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))
;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their
;; values at positions ps (from 0)
(define (index r . ps)
  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])
    (hash-update! ix (for/list ([p (in-list ps)]) (list-ref t p)) (λ (es) (cons (cons t x) es)) null))
  ix)
;; whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))
;; the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

(define (constant s) (or (string->number s) (string->symbol s)))
;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
(define (facts path)
  (define db (make-hash))
  (for ([line (in-lines (open-input-file path))])
    (define f (string-split line "\t" #:trim? #f))
    (define p (string->number (cadr f)))
    (add! (hash-ref! db (car f) make-hash) (map constant (cddr f)) (if (>= p 1) #t (flip p))))
  db)

;; The distribution of v, a list of (value . probability): Roulette's query
;; at the module's level (`display-pmf`), read back from the table it
;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone.
(define (distribution v)
  (define text (with-output-to-string (λ () (display-pmf v))))
  (define (datum s)
    (define d (read (open-input-string s)))
    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))
  (define rows
    (for/list ([line (in-list (string-split text "\n"))]
               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))
  (if (null? rows)
      (list (cons (datum text) 1))
      (for/list ([r (in-list rows)]
                 #:unless (equal? r '("Value" "Probability")))
        (cons (datum (car r)) (string->number (cadr r))))))
(define (real p) (if (exact? p) (exact->inexact p) p))
(define (probability dist v)
  (define e (assoc v dist))
  (if e (cdr e) 0))
(define (report dists)
  (for ([dist (in-list dists)] [k (in-naturals 1)])
    (printf "roulette ~a true ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #t)))
    (printf "roulette ~a false ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #f)))))

(define db (facts (vector-ref (current-command-line-arguments) 0)))
(define female-facts (hash-ref db "female/0" (make-hash)))
(define qualified-facts (hash-ref db "qualified/0" (make-hash)))

(define female female-facts)

(define deptB (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; deptB :- female.
  (for ([x1 (in-list (probe female (list)))])
    (add! deptB (list) x1))
  ;; 0.5::deptB :- \+ female.
  (add! deptB (list) (&& (! (holds female (list))) (flip 0.5))))

(define qualified qualified-facts)

(define admitted (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; admitted :- deptB, female, qualified.
  (for ([x1 (in-list (probe deptB (list)))])
    (for ([x2 (in-list (probe female (list)))])
      (for ([x3 (in-list (probe qualified (list)))])
        (add! admitted (list) (&& x1 x2 x3)))))
  ;; admitted :- \+ deptB, \+ female.
  (add! admitted (list) (&& (! (holds deptB (list))) (! (holds female (list))))))

(statement (observe! (holds female (list))))
(define dists
  (list (distribution (holds admitted (list)))))
(statement (report dists))

/*
Model checking of a Markov chain: we want to know what is the likelihood
that on an execution of the chain from a start state s, a final state t
will be reached?
From
Gorlin, Andrey, C. R. Ramakrishnan, and Scott A. Smolka. "Model checking with probabilistic tabled logic programming." Theory and Practice of Logic Programming 12.4-5 (2012): 681-700.
*/

:- use_module(library(pita)).

:- if(current_predicate(use_rendering/1)).
:- use_rendering(c3).
:- use_rendering(graphviz).
:- endif.

:- pita.

:- set_pita(depth_bound,true).
:- set_pita(depth,5).


:- begin_lpad.

% reach(S, I, T) starting at state S at instance I,
%   state T is reachable.
reach(S, I, T) :-
  trans(S, I, U),
  reach(U, next(I), T).

reach(S, _, S).

% trans(S,I,T) transition from S at instance I goes to T

trans(s0,S,s0):0.5; trans(s0,S,s1):0.3; trans(s0,S,s2):0.2.

trans(s1,S,s1):0.4; trans(s1,S,s3):0.1; trans(s1,S,s4):0.5.

trans(s4,_,s3).
:- end_lpad.

markov_chain(digraph(G)):-
    findall(edge(A -> B,[label=P]),
      (clause(trans(A,_,B,_,_,_),
        (get_var_n(_,_,_,_,Probs,_),equalityc(_,_,N,_))),
        nth0(N,Probs,P)),
      G0),
    findall(edge(A -> B,[label=1.0]),
      clause(trans(A,_,B,_,_,_),onec(_,_)),
      G1),
    append(G0,G1,G).


/** <examples>

?- prob(reach(s0,0,s0),P).
% expecte result ~ 1.

?- prob(reach(s0,0,s1),P).
% expecte result ~ 0.5984054054054054.

?- prob(reach(s0,0,s2),P).
% expecte result ~ 0.4025135135135135.

?- prob(reach(s0,0,s3),P).
% expecte result ~ 0.5998378378378378.

?- prob(reach(s0,0,s4),P).
% expecte result ~ 0.49948717948717947.

?- prob(reach(s1,0,s0),P).
% expecte result ~ 0.

?- markov_chain(G).
% draw the Markov chain
*/

main :-
    forall((Q = reach(s0,0,s0), prob(Q, P)), format("~q:\t~w~n", [Q, P])),

path(X,X).

path(X,Y):-
  path(X,Z),edge(Z,Y).

% there is an edge between X and Z and there is a path between Z and Y

edge(a,b):0.2.

edge(b,e):0.5.
edge(a,c):0.3.
edge(c,d):0.4.
edge(d,e):0.4.
edge(a,e):0.1.

      clause(edge(A,B,_,_),(get_var_n(_,_,_,[P|_],_),_)),
