#lang roulette/example/disrupt
;; cplint_mendelc.pl: a ProbLog program written for Roulette by tddlog's
;; scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a hash
;; from its tuples (lists of constants) to whether each holds, a Boolean of the
;; coins; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from the
;; facts file named on the command line; each rule is a loop over the
;; relations its body joins. Each query's distribution is Roulette's, at the
;; module's level (`display-pmf`), given the evidence; the program prints
;; `roulette K true P` and `roulette K false P` for the K-th query.

(require racket/port racket/string racket/match)

;; A statement of the program: a definition, which the language does not
;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

;; the tuple t of r holds also where x does
(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))
;; whether the tuple t of r holds
(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))
;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their
;; values at positions ps (from 0)
(define (index r . ps)
  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])
    (hash-update! ix (for/list ([p (in-list ps)]) (list-ref t p)) (λ (es) (cons (cons t x) es)) null))
  ix)
;; whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))
;; the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

(define (constant s) (or (string->number s) (string->symbol s)))
;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
(define (facts path)
  (define db (make-hash))
  (for ([line (in-lines (open-input-file path))])
    (define f (string-split line "\t" #:trim? #f))
    (define p (string->number (cadr f)))
    (add! (hash-ref! db (car f) make-hash) (map constant (cddr f)) (if (>= p 1) #t (flip p))))
  db)

;; The distribution of v, a list of (value . probability): Roulette's query
;; at the module's level (`display-pmf`), read back from the table it
;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone.
(define (distribution v)
  (define text (with-output-to-string (λ () (display-pmf v))))
  (define (datum s)
    (define d (read (open-input-string s)))
    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))
  (define rows
    (for/list ([line (in-list (string-split text "\n"))]
               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))
  (if (null? rows)
      (list (cons (datum text) 1))
      (for/list ([r (in-list rows)]
                 #:unless (equal? r '("Value" "Probability")))
        (cons (datum (car r)) (string->number (cadr r))))))
(define (real p) (if (exact? p) (exact->inexact p) p))
(define (probability dist v)
  (define e (assoc v dist))
  (if e (cdr e) 0))
(define (report dists)
  (for ([dist (in-list dists)] [k (in-naturals 1)])
    (printf "roulette ~a true ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #t)))
    (printf "roulette ~a false ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #f)))))

(define db (facts (vector-ref (current-command-line-arguments) 0)))
(define mother-facts (hash-ref db "mother/2" (make-hash)))
(define father-facts (hash-ref db "father/2" (make-hash)))
(define cg-facts (hash-ref db "cg/3" (make-hash)))

(define father father-facts)

(define mother mother-facts)

;; cg/3: recursive; the rules applied in stages from no tuple, each
;; reading the stage before, until a stage adds no tuple and the stages number the tuples
(define coins3 (make-hash))   ; by instance, of `0.5::cg(X,1,A); 0.5::cg(X,1,B) :- mother(Y,X), cg(Y,1,A), cg(Y,2,B).`
(define coins4 (make-hash))   ; by instance, of `0.5::cg(X,2,A); 0.5::cg(X,2,B) :- father(Y,X), cg(Y,1,A), cg(Y,2,B).`
(define (stage-cg cg)
  (define next-cg (hash-copy cg-facts))
  (define cg-by-1-2 (index cg 0 1))
  ;; 0.5::cg(X,1,A); 0.5::cg(X,1,B) :- mother(Y,X), cg(Y,1,A), cg(Y,2,B).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs mother)])
    (match-define (cons (list Y X) x1) t2)
    (for ([t4 (in-list (hash-ref cg-by-1-2 (list Y 1) null))])
      (match-define (cons (list _ _ A) x3) t4)
      (for ([t6 (in-list (hash-ref cg-by-1-2 (list Y 2) null))])
        (match-define (cons (list _ _ B) x5) t6)
        (let ([chosen (hash-ref! coins3 (list X A B Y) (λ () (choose 0.5 0.5)))])
          (add! next-cg (list X 1 A) (&& x1 x3 x5 (list-ref chosen 0)))
          (add! next-cg (list X 1 B) (&& x1 x3 x5 (list-ref chosen 1)))))))
  ;; 0.5::cg(X,2,A); 0.5::cg(X,2,B) :- father(Y,X), cg(Y,1,A), cg(Y,2,B).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs father)])
    (match-define (cons (list Y X) x1) t2)
    (for ([t4 (in-list (hash-ref cg-by-1-2 (list Y 1) null))])
      (match-define (cons (list _ _ A) x3) t4)
      (for ([t6 (in-list (hash-ref cg-by-1-2 (list Y 2) null))])
        (match-define (cons (list _ _ B) x5) t6)
        (let ([chosen (hash-ref! coins4 (list X A B Y) (λ () (choose 0.5 0.5)))])
          (add! next-cg (list X 2 A) (&& x1 x3 x5 (list-ref chosen 0)))
          (add! next-cg (list X 2 B) (&& x1 x3 x5 (list-ref chosen 1)))))))
  (list next-cg))
(define-values (cg)
  (let loop ([rels (list (make-hash))] [stage 0] [before -1])
    (define size (for/sum ([r (in-list rels)]) (hash-count r)))
    (if (or (< stage size) (not (= size before)))
        (loop (apply stage-cg rels) (+ stage 1) size)
        (apply values rels))))

(define cg-by-3 (index cg 2))
(define cg-by-2-3 (index cg 1 2))
(define color (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; color(X,purple) :- cg(X,_,p).
  (for ([t2 (in-list (hash-ref cg-by-3 (list 'p) null))])
    (match-define (cons (list X _ _) x1) t2)
    (add! color (list X 'purple) x1))
  ;; color(X,white) :- cg(X,1,w), cg(X,2,w).
  (for ([t2 (in-list (hash-ref cg-by-2-3 (list 1 'w) null))])
    (match-define (cons (list X _ _) x1) t2)
    (for ([x3 (in-list (probe cg (list X 2 'w)))])
      (add! color (list X 'white) (&& x1 x3)))))

(define dists
  (list (distribution (holds color (list 's 'purple)))
        (distribution (holds color (list 's 'white)))
        (distribution (holds cg (list 's 1 'p)))
        (distribution (holds cg (list 's 1 'w)))
        (distribution (holds cg (list 's 2 'p)))
        (distribution (holds cg (list 's 2 'w)))))
(statement (report dists))

% Russian roulette with two guns, left_gun and right_gun

death : 1/6 :- pull_trigger(left_gun).
% if you pull the trigger of the left gun, you are dead with probability 1/6

death : 1/6 :- pull_trigger(right_gun).

# cplint_markov_network.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    intelligent_facts = get(db, "intelligent/0", Relation())
    good_marks_facts = get(db, "good_marks/0", Relation())
    difficult_course_facts = get(db, "difficult_course/0", Relation())
    good_teacher_facts = get(db, "good_teacher/0", Relation())

    difficult_course = difficult_course_facts

    good_marks = good_marks_facts

    intelligent = intelligent_facts

    factor1 = Relation()
    # 0.3::factor1 :- \+ intelligent, \+ good_marks.
    add!(factor1, (), !holds(intelligent, ()) & !holds(good_marks, ()) & flip(0.3))
    # 0.3::factor1 :- \+ intelligent, good_marks.
    for x1 in probe(good_marks, ())
        add!(factor1, (), !holds(intelligent, ()) & x1 & flip(0.3))
    end
    # 0.1::factor1 :- intelligent, \+ good_marks.
    for x1 in probe(intelligent, ())
        add!(factor1, (), !holds(good_marks, ()) & x1 & flip(0.1))
    end
    # 0.3::factor1 :- intelligent, good_marks.
    for x1 in probe(intelligent, ())
        for x2 in probe(good_marks, ())
            add!(factor1, (), x1 & x2 & flip(0.3))
        end
    end

    factor2 = Relation()
    # 0.3::factor2 :- \+ difficult_course, \+ good_marks.
    add!(factor2, (), !holds(difficult_course, ()) & !holds(good_marks, ()) & flip(0.3))
    # 0.3::factor2 :- \+ difficult_course, good_marks.
    for x1 in probe(good_marks, ())
        add!(factor2, (), !holds(difficult_course, ()) & x1 & flip(0.3))
    end
    # 0.3::factor2 :- difficult_course, \+ good_marks.
    for x1 in probe(difficult_course, ())
        add!(factor2, (), !holds(good_marks, ()) & x1 & flip(0.3))
    end
    # 0.1::factor2 :- difficult_course, good_marks.
    for x1 in probe(difficult_course, ())
        for x2 in probe(good_marks, ())
            add!(factor2, (), x1 & x2 & flip(0.1))
        end
    end

    good_teacher = good_teacher_facts

    factor3 = Relation()
    # 0.3::factor3 :- \+ good_teacher, \+ good_marks.
    add!(factor3, (), !holds(good_teacher, ()) & !holds(good_marks, ()) & flip(0.3))
    # 0.3::factor3 :- \+ good_teacher, good_marks.
    for x1 in probe(good_marks, ())
        add!(factor3, (), !holds(good_teacher, ()) & x1 & flip(0.3))
    end
    # 0.1::factor3 :- good_teacher, \+ good_marks.
    for x1 in probe(good_teacher, ())
        add!(factor3, (), !holds(good_marks, ()) & x1 & flip(0.1))
    end
    # 0.3::factor3 :- good_teacher, good_marks.
    for x1 in probe(good_teacher, ())
        for x2 in probe(good_marks, ())
            add!(factor3, (), x1 & x2 & flip(0.3))
        end
    end

    factor4 = Relation()
    # 0.3::factor4 :- \+ difficult_course, \+ good_teacher.
    add!(factor4, (), !holds(difficult_course, ()) & !holds(good_teacher, ()) & flip(0.3))
    # 0.3::factor4 :- \+ difficult_course, good_teacher.
    for x1 in probe(good_teacher, ())
        add!(factor4, (), !holds(difficult_course, ()) & x1 & flip(0.3))
    end
    # 0.3::factor4 :- difficult_course, \+ good_teacher.
    for x1 in probe(difficult_course, ())
        add!(factor4, (), !holds(good_teacher, ()) & x1 & flip(0.3))
    end
    # 0.1::factor4 :- difficult_course, good_teacher.
    for x1 in probe(difficult_course, ())
        for x2 in probe(good_teacher, ())
            add!(factor4, (), x1 & x2 & flip(0.1))
        end
    end

    evidence_ = Relation()
    # evidence :- factor1, factor2, factor3, factor4.
    for x1 in probe(factor1, ())
        for x2 in probe(factor2, ())
            for x3 in probe(factor3, ())
                for x4 in probe(factor4, ())
                    add!(evidence_, (), x1 & x2 & x3 & x4)
                end
            end
        end
    end

    queries = (holds(good_marks, ()),)
    evidence = holds(evidence_, ())
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

;; cplint_swish_smoking.pl: a ProbLog program written in Pluck by tddlog's scripts/problog2ppl.py,
;; first order as it is written. A relation is a list of its tuples, each (Pair
;; TUPLE HOLDING), a symbol a constructor of its own and an integer a natural;
;; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), drawn once; each rule a
;; concat_map over the relations its body joins, a tuple that several instances
;; give holding where one does (`union`). Query cK asks the K-th query, given the
;; evidence.

(define-type weight (Sure) (Chance p))
(define (draw w) (match w Sure => (True) Chance p => (flip p)))
(define (draw_all fs) (map (lambda f -> (Pair (fst f) (draw (snd f)))) fs))
;; rel with the tuple t, holding where v does too
(define (insert eq t v rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (Cons (Pair t v) (Nil))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (Cons (Pair t (or (snd e) v)) rest) (Cons e (insert eq t v rest)))))
(define (union eq rel xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => rel
    Cons x rest => (union eq (insert eq (fst x) (snd x) rel) rest)))
;; whether the tuple t of rel holds; whether one of the tuples that p accepts does
(define (holds eq rel t)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (snd e) (holds eq rest t))))
(define (any_holds p rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (p (fst e)) (or (snd e) (any_holds p rest)) (any_holds p rest))))
(define (concat_map f xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Nil)
    Cons x rest => (append (f x) (concat_map f rest))))
(define (between lo hi) (if (> lo hi) (Nil) (Cons lo (between (S lo) hi))))
(define (size_of rels) (fold (lambda acc r -> (+ acc (length r))) 0 rels))
;; the coins of a probabilistic rule in a recursion, kept by instance across the stages: the
;; instances xs, each (Pair KEY (Pair BODY HEADS)), with the coin of each KEY in table (a new
;; one drawn where it has none): (Pair TABLE' the heads, each (Pair TUPLE HOLDING))
(define (coin_of eq k table)
  (match table
    Nil => (Pair (False) (False))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) k) (Pair (True) (snd e)) (coin_of eq k rest))))
(define (attach eq draw pick table xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Pair table (Nil))
    Cons x rest =>
    (let ((found (coin_of eq (fst x) table))
          (c (if (fst found) (snd found) (draw)))
          (table2 (if (fst found) table (Cons (Pair (fst x) c) table)))
          (more (attach eq draw pick table2 rest))
          (body (fst (snd x))))
      (Pair (fst more) (append (mapi (lambda h i -> (Pair h (and body (pick c i)))) (snd (snd x))) (snd more))))))

(define-type tuple0 (T0))
(define (eq_smoker a b) (True))
(define (eq_tar a b) (True))
(define (eq_cancer a b) (True))

;; smoker/0: 1 facts
(define smoker_facts
  (Cons (Pair (T0) (Chance 0.5))
  (Nil)))

;; the evidence and the queries
(define (program)
  (let ((smoker_base (draw_all smoker_facts))
        (smoker smoker_base)
        (rule1 (Cons (Cons (Pair (T0) (and (not (any_holds (lambda t1 -> (match t1 T0 => (True))) smoker)) (flip 0.05))) (Nil)) (Nil)))
        (rule2 (concat_map (lambda e2 -> (match (fst e2) T0 => (Cons (Cons (Pair (T0) (and (snd e2) (flip 0.95))) (Nil)) (Nil)))) smoker))
        (tar (union eq_tar (Nil) (append (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule1) (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule2))))
        (rule3 (Cons (Cons (Pair (T0) (and (and (not (any_holds (lambda t3 -> (match t3 T0 => (True))) smoker)) (not (any_holds (lambda t4 -> (match t4 T0 => (True))) tar))) (flip 0.1))) (Nil)) (Nil)))
        (rule4 (concat_map (lambda e6 -> (match (fst e6) T0 => (Cons (Cons (Pair (T0) (and (and (not (any_holds (lambda t5 -> (match t5 T0 => (True))) tar)) (snd e6)) (flip 0.9))) (Nil)) (Nil)))) smoker))
        (rule5 (concat_map (lambda e8 -> (match (fst e8) T0 => (Cons (Cons (Pair (T0) (and (and (not (any_holds (lambda t7 -> (match t7 T0 => (True))) smoker)) (snd e8)) (flip 0.05))) (Nil)) (Nil)))) tar))
        (rule6 (concat_map (lambda e9 -> (match (fst e9) T0 => (concat_map (lambda e10 -> (match (fst e10) T0 => (Cons (Cons (Pair (T0) (and (and (snd e9) (snd e10)) (flip 0.85))) (Nil)) (Nil)))) tar))) smoker))
        (cancer (union eq_cancer (Nil) (append (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule3) (append (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule4) (append (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule5) (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule6))))))
        (q11 (holds eq_cancer cancer (T0))))
    (Pair (holds eq_smoker smoker (T0)) (Cons q11 (Nil)))))

(query c0 (let ((m (program))) (Posterior (index 0 (snd m)) (fst m))))

# cplint_bag_game.pl: a ProbLog program written in SPPL by tddlog's scripts/problog2ppl.py,
# first order as it is written. The facts and the joins of the rules are Python
# constants, computed before the first sample: each rule's matches a list
# comprehension over the relations its body joins, a recursive component's
# tuples a fixpoint of its rules, and the tuples that the queries and the
# evidence read. Then each probabilistic fact and each instance of a
# probabilistic rule samples a coin, and each instance of a tuple that is read
# sets a variable of its own, in a `for` over its component's instances: 1
# where its body holds or an earlier instance of its tuple does, the last of a
# tuple's instances its holding. A cycle of tuples that read each other does so
# in as many stages as it has tuples, each stage reading the one before. The
# queries are the events of queries_(), asked of the model given the evidence:
#
#   sppl_dice.py PROGRAM.sppl
#
# queries
# component 0 bool query0

from functools import reduce
from itertools import accumulate

yes_ = lambda: true_ << {1}
no_ = lambda: true_ << {0}
all_ = lambda es_: reduce(lambda a_, b_: a_ & b_, es_) if es_ else yes_()
fix_ = lambda g_, x_: (lambda y_: x_ if y_ == x_ else fix_(g_, y_))(g_(x_))
dedup_ = lambda xs_: list(dict.fromkeys(xs_))
index_ = lambda ts_: {t_: j_ for j_, t_ in enumerate(ts_)}
by_ = lambda ts_, ps_: reduce(lambda d_, j_: d_.setdefault(tuple(ts_[j_][p_] for p_ in ps_), []).append(j_) or d_,
                              range(len(ts_)), {})
idiv_ = lambda a_, b_: abs(a_) // abs(b_) * (1 if (a_ < 0) == (b_ < 0) else -1)
# the heads of relation q_ that matches ms_ give; a coin's index for each probability below 1
heads_ = lambda q_, ms_: [h_ for m_ in ms_ for r_, h_ in m_[1] if r_ == q_]
coins_of_ = lambda ps_, c0_: [None if p_ >= 1 else c0_ + n_
                              for p_, n_ in zip(ps_, accumulate([0] + [int(x_ < 1) for x_ in ps_]))]
# a relation's instances, each (its tuple's index, its coin and value or None, its refs); their indexes by tuple
facts_ = lambda i_, ts_, cs_: [(i_[t_], None if c_ is None else (c_, 1), []) for t_, c_ in zip(ts_, cs_)]
inst_ = lambda q_, i_, ms_, ks_, c0_: [(i_[h_], None if ks_ is None else (c0_ + ks_[m_[0]], n_ + 1), m_[2])
                                      for m_ in ms_ for n_, (r_, h_) in enumerate(m_[1]) if r_ == q_]
by_tuple_ = lambda es_, n_: (lambda d_: [d_.get((j_,), []) for j_ in range(n_)])(by_(es_, (0,)))
# the tuples (relation, index) that a tuple's instances read; those that tuples us_ read in turn, where ok_
reads_ = lambda u_: ([(r_, k_) for m_ in of_[u_[0]][u_[1]] for r_, k_, _, _ in insts_[u_[0]][m_][2]]
                     if u_[0] in of_ else [])
reach_ = lambda us_, ok_: fix_(lambda s_: s_ | {w_ for u_ in s_ for w_ in reads_(u_) if ok_(w_)}, frozenset(us_))
# a component's steps, each (relation, instance, stage, cycle), over the tuples of its relations c_ that the
# queries and the evidence read: its cycles of tuples (the tuples that reach the same ones), each after the
# cycles it reads (which reach fewer), in as many stages as it has tuples, each stage reading the one before
cycles_ = lambda rs_: sorted(reduce(lambda d_, u_: d_.setdefault(rs_[u_], []).append(u_) or d_, sorted(rs_),
                                    {}).values(), key=lambda us_: (len(rs_[us_[0]]), us_[0]))
steps_ = lambda c_: [(u_[0], m_, s_, g_) for g_, us_ in enumerate(cycles_(
                         {u_: reach_([u_], lambda w_: w_[0] in c_) for u_ in used_ if u_[0] in c_}))
                     for s_ in range(1, len(us_) + 1) for u_ in us_ for m_ in of_[u_[0]][u_[1]]]
# a step's tuple and stage; the step of a tuple's last instance at each stage; a tuple's last stage and its
# cycle; the step before each, where it is an earlier instance of its tuple at its stage
key_ = lambda x_: (x_[0], insts_[x_[0]][x_[1]][0], x_[2])
at_of_ = lambda st_: {key_(x_): k_ for k_, x_ in enumerate(st_)}
ends_ = lambda st_: {key_(x_)[:2]: (x_[2], x_[3]) for x_ in st_}
prev_ = lambda st_: [k_ - 1 if k_ and key_(st_[k_ - 1]) == key_(st_[k_]) else None for k_ in range(len(st_))]
# events: a fact's; a tuple's at stage s_ (None its last, 0 before the first); a step's coin and body, which
# reads the tuples of its own cycle at the stage before; the step's or the one before it
fact_ = lambda c_, v_: (yes_() if v_ else no_()) if c_ is None else coins_[c_] << {v_}
value_ = lambda a_, at_s_, end_, u_, v_, s_: (lambda t_: (no_() if v_ else yes_()) if t_ == 0
                                              else a_[at_s_[u_ + (t_,)]] << {v_})(end_[u_][0] if s_ is None else s_)
coin_ = lambda c_: [] if c_ is None else [coins_[c_[0]] << {c_[1]}]
step_ = lambda st_, end_, k_: (lambda q_, m_, s_, g_: all_(coin_(insts_[q_][m_][1]) + [
    at_[r_](j_, v_, s_ - 1 if w_ and end_[(r_, j_)][1] == g_ else None)
    for r_, j_, v_, w_ in insts_[q_][m_][2]]))(*st_[k_])
ev_ = lambda e_, p_, acc_: e_ if p_ is None else e_ | (acc_(p_) << {1})
holds_ = lambda q_, t_, v_: (lambda j_: (no_() if v_ else yes_()) if j_ is None else at_[q_](j_, v_, None))(
    ix_[q_].get(t_))

# red/0: 1 facts, each a tuple and its probability
red_ft = [()]
red_fp = [0.4]
red_c0 = 0
red_cd = [{1: p_, 0: 1 - p_} for p_ in red_fp if p_ < 1]
red_fc = coins_of_(red_fp, red_c0)
# green/0: 1 facts, each a tuple and its probability
green_ft = [()]
green_fp = [0.9]
green_c0 = red_c0 + len(red_cd)
green_cd = [{1: p_, 0: 1 - p_} for p_ in green_fp if p_ < 1]
green_fc = coins_of_(green_fp, green_c0)
# blue/0: 1 facts, each a tuple and its probability
blue_ft = [()]
blue_fp = [0.5]
blue_c0 = green_c0 + len(green_cd)
blue_cd = [{1: p_, 0: 1 - p_} for p_ in blue_fp if p_ < 1]
blue_fc = coins_of_(blue_fp, blue_c0)
# yellow/0: 1 facts, each a tuple and its probability
yellow_ft = [()]
yellow_fp = [0.6]
yellow_c0 = blue_c0 + len(blue_cd)
yellow_cd = [{1: p_, 0: 1 - p_} for p_ in yellow_fp if p_ < 1]
yellow_fc = coins_of_(yellow_fp, yellow_c0)

blue_t = blue_ft
blue_i = index_(blue_t)

green_t = green_ft
green_i = index_(green_t)

red_t = red_ft
red_i = index_(red_t)

yellow_t = yellow_ft
yellow_i = index_(yellow_t)

# rule 1: win :- red, green.
rule1_m = [((), (('win', ()),), [('red', j1, 1, 0), ('green', j2, 1, 0)])
    for j1 in [red_i.get(())] if j1 is not None
    for j2 in [green_i.get(())] if j2 is not None]
# rule 2: win :- blue, yellow.
rule2_m = [((), (('win', ()),), [('blue', j1, 1, 0), ('yellow', j2, 1, 0)])
    for j1 in [blue_i.get(())] if j1 is not None
    for j2 in [yellow_i.get(())] if j2 is not None]
win_t = dedup_(heads_('win', rule1_m + rule2_m))
win_i = index_(win_t)
win_inst = inst_('win', win_i, rule1_m, None, 0) + inst_('win', win_i, rule2_m, None, 0)
win_of = by_tuple_(win_inst, len(win_t))

at_ = {
    'blue': lambda j_, v_, s_: fact_(blue_fc[j_], v_),
    'green': lambda j_, v_, s_: fact_(green_fc[j_], v_),
    'red': lambda j_, v_, s_: fact_(red_fc[j_], v_),
    'yellow': lambda j_, v_, s_: fact_(yellow_fc[j_], v_),
    'win': lambda j_, v_, s_: value_(comp5_acc, comp5_at, comp5_end, ('win', j_), v_, s_),}
ix_ = {'blue': blue_i, 'green': green_i, 'red': red_i, 'yellow': yellow_i, 'win': win_i}
coin_d_ = red_cd + green_cd + blue_cd + yellow_cd
insts_ = {'win': win_inst}
of_ = {'win': win_of}
# the tuples the queries and the evidence read, and those their instances read in turn
asked_ = [('win', ())]
used_ = reach_([(q_, ix_[q_][t_]) for q_, t_ in asked_ if t_ in ix_.get(q_, {})], lambda w_: True)
comp5_steps = steps_({'win'})
comp5_at = at_of_(comp5_steps)
comp5_end = ends_(comp5_steps)
comp5_prev = prev_(comp5_steps)
comp5_ev = lambda k_: ev_(step_(comp5_steps, comp5_end, k_), comp5_prev[k_], lambda i_: comp5_acc[i_])
queries_ = lambda: [holds_('win', (), 1)]

coins_ = array(len(coin_d_))
comp5_acc = array(len(comp5_steps))

true_ ~= atomic(loc=1)
for n_ in range(len(coin_d_)):
    coins_[n_] ~= discrete(coin_d_[n_])
# win/0: an instance holds where its body or an earlier instance of its tuple does
for k_ in range(len(comp5_steps)):
    if comp5_ev(k_):
        comp5_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=1)
    else:
        comp5_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=0)

/*
Program describing the Mendelian rules of inheritance of the color of pea 
plants. It considers a family of four grandparents, two parents and a child.
The problem is, given the alleles of the grandparents, predict the
probability of the color (or of its alleles) of a pea plant.
From
H. Blockeel. Probabilistic logical models for mendel's experiments: An exercise.
In Inductive Logic Programming (ILP 2004), Work in Progress Track, 2004.
*/
:- use_module(library(pita)).

:- if(current_predicate(use_rendering/1)).
:- use_rendering(c3).
:- endif.

:- pita.

:- begin_lpad.

mother(m,s).
mother(mm,m).
mother(mf,f).
father(f,s).
father(fm,m).
father(ff,f).
% family with 7 members: grandparents, partents and s

% cg(I,C,A) means that individual I has color allele A on chromosome C
% the color alleles are p and w and the chromosomes are 1 and 2
% color(I,Col) means that individual I has color Col
% Col can be purple or white



cg(mm,1,p).
cg(mm,2,w).
cg(fm,1,p).
cg(fm,2,p).
cg(mf,1,w).
cg(mf,2,w).
cg(ff,1,w).
cg(ff,2,p).
% we know with certainty the alleles of the grandparants of s


cg(X,1,A):0.5 ; cg(X,1,B):0.5 :- mother(Y,X),cg(Y,1,A), cg(Y,2,B).
% the color allele of an individual on chromosome 1 is inherited from its 
% mother. The two alleles of the mother have equal probability of being
% transmitted
 
cg(X,2,A):0.5 ; cg(X,2,B):0.5 :- father(Y,X),cg(Y,1,A), cg(Y,2,B).
% the color allele of an individual on chromosome 2 is inherited from its 
% father. The two alleles of the mother have equal probability of being
% transmitted


color(X,purple) :- cg(X,_,p).
% if an individual has a p allele its color is purple, i.e., purple is
% dominant

color(X,white) :- cg(X,1,w), cg(X,2,w).
% if an individual has two w alleles its color is white, i.e., white is
% recessive

:- end_lpad.

/** <examples>

?- prob(color(s,purple),Prob). % what is the probability that the color of s' flowers is purple?
% expected result 0.8125
?- prob(color(s,white),Prob). % what is the probability that the color of s' flowers is white?
% expected result 0.1875
?- prob(cg(s,1,p),Prob). % what is the probability that the color allele on chromosme 1 of s is p?
% expected result 0.75
?- prob(cg(s,1,w),Prob). % what is the probability that the color allele on chromosme 1 of s is w?
% expected result 0.25
?- prob(cg(s,2,p),Prob). % what is the probability that the color allele on chromosme 2 of s is p?
% expected result 0.25
?- prob(cg(s,2,w),Prob). % what is the probability that the color allele on chromosme 2 of s is w?
% expected result 0.75
?- prob(color(s,purple),Prob),bar(Prob,C). % what is the probability that the color of s' flowers is purple?
% expected result 0.8125
?- prob(color(s,white),Prob),bar(Prob,C). % what is the probability that the color of s' flowers is white?
% expected result 0.1875
?- prob(cg(s,1,p),Prob),bar(Prob,C). % what is the probability that the color allele on chromosme 1 of s is p?
% expected result 0.75
?- prob(cg(s,1,w),Prob),bar(Prob,C). % what is the probability that the color allele on chromosme 1 of s is w?
% expected result 0.25
?- prob(cg(s,2,p),Prob),bar(Prob,C). % what is the probability that the color allele on chromosme 2 of s is p?
% expected result 0.25
?- prob(cg(s,2,w),Prob),bar(Prob,C). % what is the probability that the color allele on chromosme 2 of s is w?

;; cplint_coin2.pl: a ProbLog program written in Pluck by tddlog's scripts/problog2ppl.py,
;; first order as it is written. A relation is a list of its tuples, each (Pair
;; TUPLE HOLDING), a symbol a constructor of its own and an integer a natural;
;; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), drawn once; each rule a
;; concat_map over the relations its body joins, a tuple that several instances
;; give holding where one does (`union`). Query cK asks the K-th query, given the
;; evidence.

(define-type weight (Sure) (Chance p))
(define (draw w) (match w Sure => (True) Chance p => (flip p)))
(define (draw_all fs) (map (lambda f -> (Pair (fst f) (draw (snd f)))) fs))
;; rel with the tuple t, holding where v does too
(define (insert eq t v rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (Cons (Pair t v) (Nil))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (Cons (Pair t (or (snd e) v)) rest) (Cons e (insert eq t v rest)))))
(define (union eq rel xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => rel
    Cons x rest => (union eq (insert eq (fst x) (snd x) rel) rest)))
;; whether the tuple t of rel holds; whether one of the tuples that p accepts does
(define (holds eq rel t)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (snd e) (holds eq rest t))))
(define (any_holds p rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (p (fst e)) (or (snd e) (any_holds p rest)) (any_holds p rest))))
(define (concat_map f xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Nil)
    Cons x rest => (append (f x) (concat_map f rest))))
(define (between lo hi) (if (> lo hi) (Nil) (Cons lo (between (S lo) hi))))
(define (size_of rels) (fold (lambda acc r -> (+ acc (length r))) 0 rels))
;; the coins of a probabilistic rule in a recursion, kept by instance across the stages: the
;; instances xs, each (Pair KEY (Pair BODY HEADS)), with the coin of each KEY in table (a new
;; one drawn where it has none): (Pair TABLE' the heads, each (Pair TUPLE HOLDING))
(define (coin_of eq k table)
  (match table
    Nil => (Pair (False) (False))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) k) (Pair (True) (snd e)) (coin_of eq k rest))))
(define (attach eq draw pick table xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Pair table (Nil))
    Cons x rest =>
    (let ((found (coin_of eq (fst x) table))
          (c (if (fst found) (snd found) (draw)))
          (table2 (if (fst found) table (Cons (Pair (fst x) c) table)))
          (more (attach eq draw pick table2 rest))
          (body (fst (snd x))))
      (Pair (fst more) (append (mapi (lambda h i -> (Pair h (and body (pick c i)))) (snd (snd x))) (snd more))))))

(define-type sym (c_coin1) (c_coin2))
(define-type tuple1 (T1 a1))
(define (eq_heads a b) (match a T1 a1 => (match b T1 b1 => (constructor=? a1 b1))))
(define (eq_tails a b) (match a T1 a1 => (match b T1 b1 => (constructor=? a1 b1))))
(define (eq_fair a b) (match a T1 a1 => (match b T1 b1 => (constructor=? a1 b1))))
(define (eq_biased a b) (match a T1 a1 => (match b T1 b1 => (constructor=? a1 b1))))
(define (eq_toss a b) (match a T1 a1 => (match b T1 b1 => (constructor=? a1 b1))))
(define (eq_demand_1 a b) (match a T1 a1 => (match b T1 b1 => (constructor=? a1 b1))))

;; toss/1: 2 facts
(define toss_facts
  (Cons (Pair (T1 (c_coin1)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T1 (c_coin2)) (Sure))
  (Nil))))

;; the evidence and the queries
(define (program)
  (let ((toss_base (draw_all toss_facts))
        (toss toss_base)
        (rule4 (concat_map (lambda e1 -> (match (fst e1) T1 vCoin => (Cons (Cons (Pair (T1 vCoin) (True)) (Nil)) (Nil)))) toss))
        (rule5 (concat_map (lambda e2 -> (match (fst e2) T1 vCoin => (Cons (Cons (Pair (T1 vCoin) (True)) (Nil)) (Nil)))) toss))
        (demand_1 (union eq_demand_1 (Nil) (append (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule4) (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule5))))
        (rule1 (concat_map (lambda e3 -> (match (fst e3) T1 vCoin => (let (k4 (if (flip 0.9) 0 1)) (Cons (Cons (Pair (T1 vCoin) (and (snd e3) (== k4 0))) (Cons (Pair (T1 vCoin) (and (snd e3) (== k4 1))) (Nil))) (Nil))))) demand_1))
        (biased (union eq_biased (Nil) (map (lambda x -> (index 1 x)) rule1)))
        (fair (union eq_fair (Nil) (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule1)))
        (rule2 (concat_map (lambda e5 -> (match (fst e5) T1 vCoin => (concat_map (lambda e7 -> (match (fst e7) T1 a6 => (if (constructor=? a6 vCoin) (let (k8 (if (flip 0.5) 0 1)) (Cons (Cons (Pair (T1 vCoin) (and (and (snd e5) (snd e7)) (== k8 0))) (Cons (Pair (T1 vCoin) (and (and (snd e5) (snd e7)) (== k8 1))) (Nil))) (Nil))) (Nil)))) fair))) toss))
        (rule3 (concat_map (lambda e9 -> (match (fst e9) T1 vCoin => (concat_map (lambda e11 -> (match (fst e11) T1 a10 => (if (constructor=? a10 vCoin) (let (k12 (if (flip 0.6) 0 1)) (Cons (Cons (Pair (T1 vCoin) (and (and (snd e9) (snd e11)) (== k12 0))) (Cons (Pair (T1 vCoin) (and (and (snd e9) (snd e11)) (== k12 1))) (Nil))) (Nil))) (Nil)))) biased))) toss))
        (heads (union eq_heads (Nil) (append (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule2) (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule3))))
        (tails (union eq_tails (Nil) (append (map (lambda x -> (index 1 x)) rule2) (map (lambda x -> (index 1 x)) rule3))))
        (q13 (holds eq_heads heads (T1 (c_coin2))))
        (q14 (holds eq_tails tails (T1 (c_coin2))))
        (q15 (holds eq_heads heads (T1 (c_coin1))))
        (q16 (holds eq_tails tails (T1 (c_coin1)))))
    (Pair (True) (Cons q13 (Cons q14 (Cons q15 (Cons q16 (Nil))))))))

(query c0 (let ((m (program))) (Marginal (index 0 (snd m)))))
(query c1 (let ((m (program))) (Marginal (index 1 (snd m)))))
(query c2 (let ((m (program))) (Marginal (index 2 (snd m)))))
(query c3 (let ((m (program))) (Marginal (index 3 (snd m)))))

# cplint_mendel.pl: a ProbLog program written in SPPL by tddlog's scripts/problog2ppl.py,
# first order as it is written. The facts and the joins of the rules are Python
# constants, computed before the first sample: each rule's matches a list
# comprehension over the relations its body joins, a recursive component's
# tuples a fixpoint of its rules, and the tuples that the queries and the
# evidence read. Then each probabilistic fact and each instance of a
# probabilistic rule samples a coin, and each instance of a tuple that is read
# sets a variable of its own, in a `for` over its component's instances: 1
# where its body holds or an earlier instance of its tuple does, the last of a
# tuple's instances its holding. A cycle of tuples that read each other does so
# in as many stages as it has tuples, each stage reading the one before. The
# queries are the events of queries_(), asked of the model given the evidence:
#
#   sppl_dice.py PROGRAM.sppl
#
# queries
# component 0 bool query0
# component 1 bool query1
# component 2 bool query2
# component 3 bool query3
# component 4 bool query4
# component 5 bool query5

from functools import reduce
from itertools import accumulate

yes_ = lambda: true_ << {1}
no_ = lambda: true_ << {0}
all_ = lambda es_: reduce(lambda a_, b_: a_ & b_, es_) if es_ else yes_()
fix_ = lambda g_, x_: (lambda y_: x_ if y_ == x_ else fix_(g_, y_))(g_(x_))
dedup_ = lambda xs_: list(dict.fromkeys(xs_))
index_ = lambda ts_: {t_: j_ for j_, t_ in enumerate(ts_)}
by_ = lambda ts_, ps_: reduce(lambda d_, j_: d_.setdefault(tuple(ts_[j_][p_] for p_ in ps_), []).append(j_) or d_,
                              range(len(ts_)), {})
idiv_ = lambda a_, b_: abs(a_) // abs(b_) * (1 if (a_ < 0) == (b_ < 0) else -1)
# the heads of relation q_ that matches ms_ give; a coin's index for each probability below 1
heads_ = lambda q_, ms_: [h_ for m_ in ms_ for r_, h_ in m_[1] if r_ == q_]
coins_of_ = lambda ps_, c0_: [None if p_ >= 1 else c0_ + n_
                              for p_, n_ in zip(ps_, accumulate([0] + [int(x_ < 1) for x_ in ps_]))]
# a relation's instances, each (its tuple's index, its coin and value or None, its refs); their indexes by tuple
facts_ = lambda i_, ts_, cs_: [(i_[t_], None if c_ is None else (c_, 1), []) for t_, c_ in zip(ts_, cs_)]
inst_ = lambda q_, i_, ms_, ks_, c0_: [(i_[h_], None if ks_ is None else (c0_ + ks_[m_[0]], n_ + 1), m_[2])
                                      for m_ in ms_ for n_, (r_, h_) in enumerate(m_[1]) if r_ == q_]
by_tuple_ = lambda es_, n_: (lambda d_: [d_.get((j_,), []) for j_ in range(n_)])(by_(es_, (0,)))
# the tuples (relation, index) that a tuple's instances read; those that tuples us_ read in turn, where ok_
reads_ = lambda u_: ([(r_, k_) for m_ in of_[u_[0]][u_[1]] for r_, k_, _, _ in insts_[u_[0]][m_][2]]
                     if u_[0] in of_ else [])
reach_ = lambda us_, ok_: fix_(lambda s_: s_ | {w_ for u_ in s_ for w_ in reads_(u_) if ok_(w_)}, frozenset(us_))
# a component's steps, each (relation, instance, stage, cycle), over the tuples of its relations c_ that the
# queries and the evidence read: its cycles of tuples (the tuples that reach the same ones), each after the
# cycles it reads (which reach fewer), in as many stages as it has tuples, each stage reading the one before
cycles_ = lambda rs_: sorted(reduce(lambda d_, u_: d_.setdefault(rs_[u_], []).append(u_) or d_, sorted(rs_),
                                    {}).values(), key=lambda us_: (len(rs_[us_[0]]), us_[0]))
steps_ = lambda c_: [(u_[0], m_, s_, g_) for g_, us_ in enumerate(cycles_(
                         {u_: reach_([u_], lambda w_: w_[0] in c_) for u_ in used_ if u_[0] in c_}))
                     for s_ in range(1, len(us_) + 1) for u_ in us_ for m_ in of_[u_[0]][u_[1]]]
# a step's tuple and stage; the step of a tuple's last instance at each stage; a tuple's last stage and its
# cycle; the step before each, where it is an earlier instance of its tuple at its stage
key_ = lambda x_: (x_[0], insts_[x_[0]][x_[1]][0], x_[2])
at_of_ = lambda st_: {key_(x_): k_ for k_, x_ in enumerate(st_)}
ends_ = lambda st_: {key_(x_)[:2]: (x_[2], x_[3]) for x_ in st_}
prev_ = lambda st_: [k_ - 1 if k_ and key_(st_[k_ - 1]) == key_(st_[k_]) else None for k_ in range(len(st_))]
# events: a fact's; a tuple's at stage s_ (None its last, 0 before the first); a step's coin and body, which
# reads the tuples of its own cycle at the stage before; the step's or the one before it
fact_ = lambda c_, v_: (yes_() if v_ else no_()) if c_ is None else coins_[c_] << {v_}
value_ = lambda a_, at_s_, end_, u_, v_, s_: (lambda t_: (no_() if v_ else yes_()) if t_ == 0
                                              else a_[at_s_[u_ + (t_,)]] << {v_})(end_[u_][0] if s_ is None else s_)
coin_ = lambda c_: [] if c_ is None else [coins_[c_[0]] << {c_[1]}]
step_ = lambda st_, end_, k_: (lambda q_, m_, s_, g_: all_(coin_(insts_[q_][m_][1]) + [
    at_[r_](j_, v_, s_ - 1 if w_ and end_[(r_, j_)][1] == g_ else None)
    for r_, j_, v_, w_ in insts_[q_][m_][2]]))(*st_[k_])
ev_ = lambda e_, p_, acc_: e_ if p_ is None else e_ | (acc_(p_) << {1})
holds_ = lambda q_, t_, v_: (lambda j_: (no_() if v_ else yes_()) if j_ is None else at_[q_](j_, v_, None))(
    ix_[q_].get(t_))

# mother/2: 1 facts, each a tuple and its probability
mother_ft = [('m', 's')]
mother_fp = [1.0]
mother_c0 = 0
mother_cd = [{1: p_, 0: 1 - p_} for p_ in mother_fp if p_ < 1]
mother_fc = coins_of_(mother_fp, mother_c0)
# father/2: 1 facts, each a tuple and its probability
father_ft = [('f', 's')]
father_fp = [1.0]
father_c0 = mother_c0 + len(mother_cd)
father_cd = [{1: p_, 0: 1 - p_} for p_ in father_fp if p_ < 1]
father_fc = coins_of_(father_fp, father_c0)
# cg/3: 4 facts, each a tuple and its probability
cg_ft = [('m', 1, 'p'), ('m', 2, 'w'), ('f', 1, 'w'), ('f', 2, 'p')]
cg_fp = [1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0]
cg_c0 = father_c0 + len(father_cd)
cg_cd = [{1: p_, 0: 1 - p_} for p_ in cg_fp if p_ < 1]
cg_fc = coins_of_(cg_fp, cg_c0)

father_t = father_ft
father_i = index_(father_t)

mother_t = mother_ft
mother_i = index_(mother_t)

# cg/3: recursive; the tuples that hold in some world, a fixpoint of the rules
# rule 3: 0.5::cg(X,1,A); 0.5::cg(X,1,B) :- mother(Y,X), cg(Y,1,A), cg(Y,2,B).
rule3_g = lambda cg_r: (lambda cg_rby_1_2: [((X, A, B, Y), (('cg', (X, 1, A)), ('cg', (X, 1, B))), [('mother', j1, 1, 0), ('cg', j2, 1, 1), ('cg', j3, 1, 1)])
    for j1, (Y, X) in enumerate(mother_t)
    for j2 in cg_rby_1_2.get((Y, 1), [])
    for (_, _, A) in [cg_r[j2]]
    for j3 in cg_rby_1_2.get((Y, 2), [])
    for (_, _, B) in [cg_r[j3]]])(by_(cg_r, (0, 1)))
# rule 4: 0.5::cg(X,2,A); 0.5::cg(X,2,B) :- father(Y,X), cg(Y,1,A), cg(Y,2,B).
rule4_g = lambda cg_r: (lambda cg_rby_1_2: [((X, A, B, Y), (('cg', (X, 2, A)), ('cg', (X, 2, B))), [('father', j1, 1, 0), ('cg', j2, 1, 1), ('cg', j3, 1, 1)])
    for j1, (Y, X) in enumerate(father_t)
    for j2 in cg_rby_1_2.get((Y, 1), [])
    for (_, _, A) in [cg_r[j2]]
    for j3 in cg_rby_1_2.get((Y, 2), [])
    for (_, _, B) in [cg_r[j3]]])(by_(cg_r, (0, 1)))
comp3_t = fix_(lambda ts_: (dedup_(ts_[0] + cg_ft + heads_('cg', rule3_g(*ts_) + rule4_g(*ts_))),), ([],))
cg_t = comp3_t[0]
rule3_m = rule3_g(*comp3_t)
rule4_m = rule4_g(*comp3_t)
cg_i = index_(cg_t)
cg_by_3 = by_(cg_t, (2,))
cg_by_2_3 = by_(cg_t, (1, 2))
rule3_k = index_(dedup_([m_[0] for m_ in rule3_m]))
rule3_c0 = cg_c0 + len(cg_cd)
rule3_cd = [{1: 0.5, 2: 0.5}] * len(rule3_k)
rule4_k = index_(dedup_([m_[0] for m_ in rule4_m]))
rule4_c0 = rule3_c0 + len(rule3_cd)
rule4_cd = [{1: 0.5, 2: 0.5}] * len(rule4_k)
cg_inst = facts_(cg_i, cg_ft, cg_fc) + inst_('cg', cg_i, rule3_m, rule3_k, rule3_c0) + inst_('cg', cg_i, rule4_m, rule4_k, rule4_c0)
cg_of = by_tuple_(cg_inst, len(cg_t))

# rule 1: color(X,purple) :- cg(X,_,p).
rule1_m = [((X,), (('color', (X, 'purple')),), [('cg', j1, 1, 0)])
    for j1 in cg_by_3.get(('p',), [])
    for (X, _, _) in [cg_t[j1]]]
# rule 2: color(X,white) :- cg(X,1,w), cg(X,2,w).
rule2_m = [((X,), (('color', (X, 'white')),), [('cg', j1, 1, 0), ('cg', j2, 1, 0)])
    for j1 in cg_by_2_3.get((1, 'w'), [])
    for (X, _, _) in [cg_t[j1]]
    for j2 in [cg_i.get((X, 2, 'w'))] if j2 is not None]
color_t = dedup_(heads_('color', rule1_m + rule2_m))
color_i = index_(color_t)
color_inst = inst_('color', color_i, rule1_m, None, 0) + inst_('color', color_i, rule2_m, None, 0)
color_of = by_tuple_(color_inst, len(color_t))

at_ = {
    'father': lambda j_, v_, s_: fact_(father_fc[j_], v_),
    'mother': lambda j_, v_, s_: fact_(mother_fc[j_], v_),
    'cg': lambda j_, v_, s_: value_(comp3_acc, comp3_at, comp3_end, ('cg', j_), v_, s_),
    'color': lambda j_, v_, s_: value_(comp4_acc, comp4_at, comp4_end, ('color', j_), v_, s_),}
ix_ = {'father': father_i, 'mother': mother_i, 'cg': cg_i, 'color': color_i}
coin_d_ = mother_cd + father_cd + cg_cd + rule3_cd + rule4_cd
insts_ = {'cg': cg_inst, 'color': color_inst}
of_ = {'cg': cg_of, 'color': color_of}
# the tuples the queries and the evidence read, and those their instances read in turn
asked_ = [('color', ('s', 'purple')), ('color', ('s', 'white')), ('cg', ('s', 1, 'p')), ('cg', ('s', 1, 'w')),
    ('cg', ('s', 2, 'p')), ('cg', ('s', 2, 'w'))]
used_ = reach_([(q_, ix_[q_][t_]) for q_, t_ in asked_ if t_ in ix_.get(q_, {})], lambda w_: True)
comp3_steps = steps_({'cg'})
comp3_at = at_of_(comp3_steps)
comp3_end = ends_(comp3_steps)
comp3_prev = prev_(comp3_steps)
comp3_ev = lambda k_: ev_(step_(comp3_steps, comp3_end, k_), comp3_prev[k_], lambda i_: comp3_acc[i_])
comp4_steps = steps_({'color'})
comp4_at = at_of_(comp4_steps)
comp4_end = ends_(comp4_steps)
comp4_prev = prev_(comp4_steps)
comp4_ev = lambda k_: ev_(step_(comp4_steps, comp4_end, k_), comp4_prev[k_], lambda i_: comp4_acc[i_])
queries_ = lambda: [holds_('color', ('s', 'purple'), 1), holds_('color', ('s', 'white'), 1), holds_('cg', ('s', 1, 'p'), 1), holds_('cg', ('s', 1, 'w'), 1), holds_('cg', ('s', 2, 'p'), 1), holds_('cg', ('s', 2, 'w'), 1)]

coins_ = array(len(coin_d_))
comp3_acc = array(len(comp3_steps))
comp4_acc = array(len(comp4_steps))

true_ ~= atomic(loc=1)
for n_ in range(len(coin_d_)):
    coins_[n_] ~= discrete(coin_d_[n_])
# cg/3: an instance holds where its body or an earlier instance of its tuple does, a cycle of tuples in as many stages as it has tuples
for k_ in range(len(comp3_steps)):
    if comp3_ev(k_):
        comp3_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=1)
    else:
        comp3_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=0)
# color/2: an instance holds where its body or an earlier instance of its tuple does
for k_ in range(len(comp4_steps)):
    if comp4_ev(k_):
        comp4_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=1)
    else:
        comp4_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=0)

# cplint_earthquake.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    fault_rupture_facts = get(db, "fault_rupture/1", Relation())
    volcanic_eruption_facts = get(db, "volcanic_eruption/1", Relation())

    fault_rupture = fault_rupture_facts

    volcanic_eruption = volcanic_eruption_facts

    earthquake = Relation()
    # 0.3::earthquake(X,strong); 0.5::earthquake(X,moderate) :- fault_rupture(X).
    for ((X,), x1) in fault_rupture
        chosen = choose(0.3, 0.5)
        add!(earthquake, (X, :strong), x1 & chosen[1])
        add!(earthquake, (X, :moderate), x1 & chosen[2])
    end
    # 0.2::earthquake(X,strong); 0.6::earthquake(X,moderate) :- volcanic_eruption(X).
    for ((X,), x1) in volcanic_eruption
        chosen = choose(0.2, 0.6)
        add!(earthquake, (X, :strong), x1 & chosen[1])
        add!(earthquake, (X, :moderate), x1 & chosen[2])
    end

    queries = (holds(earthquake, (:stromboli, :strong)), holds(earthquake, (:stromboli, :moderate)), holds(earthquake, (:eyjafjallajkull, :strong)), holds(earthquake, (:eyjafjallajkull, :moderate)))
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

;; cplint_multiple_paths.pl: a ProbLog program written in Pluck by tddlog's scripts/problog2ppl.py,
;; first order as it is written. A relation is a list of its tuples, each (Pair
;; TUPLE HOLDING), a symbol a constructor of its own and an integer a natural;
;; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), drawn once; each rule a
;; concat_map over the relations its body joins, a tuple that several instances
;; give holding where one does (`union`). Query cK asks the K-th query, given the
;; evidence.

(define-type weight (Sure) (Chance p))
(define (draw w) (match w Sure => (True) Chance p => (flip p)))
(define (draw_all fs) (map (lambda f -> (Pair (fst f) (draw (snd f)))) fs))
;; rel with the tuple t, holding where v does too
(define (insert eq t v rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (Cons (Pair t v) (Nil))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (Cons (Pair t (or (snd e) v)) rest) (Cons e (insert eq t v rest)))))
(define (union eq rel xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => rel
    Cons x rest => (union eq (insert eq (fst x) (snd x) rel) rest)))
;; whether the tuple t of rel holds; whether one of the tuples that p accepts does
(define (holds eq rel t)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (snd e) (holds eq rest t))))
(define (any_holds p rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (p (fst e)) (or (snd e) (any_holds p rest)) (any_holds p rest))))
(define (concat_map f xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Nil)
    Cons x rest => (append (f x) (concat_map f rest))))
(define (between lo hi) (if (> lo hi) (Nil) (Cons lo (between (S lo) hi))))
(define (size_of rels) (fold (lambda acc r -> (+ acc (length r))) 0 rels))
;; the coins of a probabilistic rule in a recursion, kept by instance across the stages: the
;; instances xs, each (Pair KEY (Pair BODY HEADS)), with the coin of each KEY in table (a new
;; one drawn where it has none): (Pair TABLE' the heads, each (Pair TUPLE HOLDING))
(define (coin_of eq k table)
  (match table
    Nil => (Pair (False) (False))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) k) (Pair (True) (snd e)) (coin_of eq k rest))))
(define (attach eq draw pick table xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Pair table (Nil))
    Cons x rest =>
    (let ((found (coin_of eq (fst x) table))
          (c (if (fst found) (snd found) (draw)))
          (table2 (if (fst found) table (Cons (Pair (fst x) c) table)))
          (more (attach eq draw pick table2 rest))
          (body (fst (snd x))))
      (Pair (fst more) (append (mapi (lambda h i -> (Pair h (and body (pick c i)))) (snd (snd x))) (snd more))))))

(define-type tuple0 (T0))
(define (eq_a a b) (True))
(define (eq_b a b) (True))
(define (eq_c a b) (True))
(define (eq_d a b) (True))
(define (eq_p a b) (True))

;; a/0: 1 facts
(define a_facts
  (Cons (Pair (T0) (Chance 0.3))
  (Nil)))
;; b/0: 1 facts
(define b_facts
  (Cons (Pair (T0) (Chance 0.4))
  (Nil)))
;; c/0: 1 facts
(define c_facts
  (Cons (Pair (T0) (Chance 0.2))
  (Nil)))
;; d/0: 1 facts
(define d_facts
  (Cons (Pair (T0) (Chance 0.1))
  (Nil)))

;; the evidence and the queries
(define (program)
  (let ((a_base (draw_all a_facts))
        (b_base (draw_all b_facts))
        (c_base (draw_all c_facts))
        (d_base (draw_all d_facts))
        (a a_base)
        (b b_base)
        (c c_base)
        (d d_base)
        (rule1 (concat_map (lambda e2 -> (match (fst e2) T0 => (concat_map (lambda e3 -> (match (fst e3) T0 => (concat_map (lambda e4 -> (match (fst e4) T0 => (Cons (Cons (Pair (T0) (and (not (any_holds (lambda t1 -> (match t1 T0 => (True))) d)) (and (snd e2) (and (snd e3) (snd e4))))) (Nil)) (Nil)))) b))) a))) c))
        (rule2 (concat_map (lambda e7 -> (match (fst e7) T0 => (Cons (Cons (Pair (T0) (and (not (any_holds (lambda t5 -> (match t5 T0 => (True))) a)) (and (not (any_holds (lambda t6 -> (match t6 T0 => (True))) b)) (snd e7)))) (Nil)) (Nil)))) d))
        (p (union eq_p (Nil) (append (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule1) (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule2))))
        (q8 (holds eq_p p (T0))))
    (Pair (True) (Cons q8 (Nil)))))

(query c0 (let ((m (program))) (Marginal (index 0 (snd m)))))

# cplint_swish_smoking.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    smoker_facts = get(db, "smoker/0", Relation())

    smoker = smoker_facts

    tar = Relation()
    # 0.05::tar :- \+ smoker.
    add!(tar, (), !holds(smoker, ()) & flip(0.05))
    # 0.95::tar :- smoker.
    for x1 in probe(smoker, ())
        add!(tar, (), x1 & flip(0.95))
    end

    cancer = Relation()
    # 0.1::cancer :- \+ smoker, \+ tar.
    add!(cancer, (), !holds(smoker, ()) & !holds(tar, ()) & flip(0.1))
    # 0.9::cancer :- smoker, \+ tar.
    for x1 in probe(smoker, ())
        add!(cancer, (), !holds(tar, ()) & x1 & flip(0.9))
    end
    # 0.05::cancer :- \+ smoker, tar.
    for x1 in probe(tar, ())
        add!(cancer, (), !holds(smoker, ()) & x1 & flip(0.05))
    end
    # 0.85::cancer :- smoker, tar.
    for x1 in probe(smoker, ())
        for x2 in probe(tar, ())
            add!(cancer, (), x1 & x2 & flip(0.85))
        end
    end

    queries = (holds(cancer, ()),)
    evidence = holds(smoker, ())
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

/*
Program describing the Monty Hall puzzle which gets its name from the TV game 
show hosted by Monty Hall. A player is given the opportunity to
select one of three closed doors, behind one of which there is a prize. 
Behind the other two doors are empty rooms.
Once the player has made a selection, Monty is obligated to open one of the 
remaining closed doors which does not contain the prize, showing that the room 
behind it is empty. He then asks the player if he would like to switch
his selection to the other unopened door, or stay with his original choice. 
Here is the problem: Does it matter if he switches?
From
Chitta Baral, Michael Gelfond, and Nelson Rushton. "Probabilistic reasoning with answer sets." Theory and Practice of Logic Programming 9.01 (2009): 57-144.
*/
:- use_module(library(pita)).

:- if(current_predicate(use_rendering/1)).
:- use_rendering(c3).
:- endif.

:- pita.

:- begin_lpad.

% prize(A): the prize is behind door A, with A in {1,2,3}
% selected(A): the player selects door A
% open_door(A): Monty opens door A
% win_keep: the player wins in case he keeps his selection
% win_switch: the player wins in case he switches door


prize(1):1/3; prize(2):1/3; prize(3):1/3.
% the prize is behind each door with probability 1/3

selected(1).
% the player selected door 1

open_door(A):0.5; open_door(B):0.5:- 
  member(A,[1,2,3]),
  member(B,[1,2,3]),
  A<B,
  \+ prize(A),
  \+ prize(B),
  \+ selected(A),
  \+ selected(B).
% Monty opens door A with probability 0.5 and door B with probability 0.5 if
% A and B are different doors, the prize is not behind any of them and the
% player did not select any of them

open_door(A):-
  member(A,[1,2,3]),
  \+ prize(A),
  \+ selected(A),
  member(B,[1,2,3]),
  prize(B),
  \+ selected(B).
% Monty opens door A with probability 1 if the prize is not behind it, it is
% not selected by the player and the prize is behind another door A that is
% not selected

win_keep:- 
  selected(A), 
  prize(A).
% the player keeps his choice and wins if he has selected a door with the prize

win_switch:- 
  member(A,[1,2,3]),
  \+ selected(A), 
  prize(A), 
  \+ open_door(A).
% the player switches and wins if the prize is behind the door that he has 
% not selected and that Monty did not open

:- end_lpad.

/** <examples>

?- prob(win_keep,Prob). % what is the probability that the player wins if he keeps his choice?
% expcted result 0.3333333333333333
?- prob(win_switch,Prob). % what is the probability that the player wins if he switches door?
% expcted result 0.6666666666666667
% the probability if the player switches grows from 1/3 to 1/2
?- prob(win_keep,Prob),bar(Prob,C). % what is the probability that the player wins if he keeps his choice?
% expcted result 0.3333333333333333
?- prob(win_switch,Prob),bar(Prob,C). % what is the probability that the player wins if he switches door?
% the probability if the player switches grows from 1/3 to 1/2
% expcted result 0.6666666666666667
*/

# cplint_coin.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    toss_facts = get(db, "toss/1", Relation())

    toss = toss_facts

    demand_1 = Relation()
    # demand_1(Coin) :- toss(Coin).
    for ((Coin,), x1) in toss
        add!(demand_1, (Coin,), true)
    end
    # demand_1(Coin) :- toss(Coin).
    for ((Coin,), x1) in toss
        add!(demand_1, (Coin,), true)
    end

    biased = Relation()
    fair = Relation()
    # 0.9::fair(Coin); 0.1::biased(Coin) :- demand_1(Coin).
    for ((Coin,), x1) in demand_1
        chosen = choose(0.9, 0.1)
        add!(fair, (Coin,), x1 & chosen[1])
        add!(biased, (Coin,), x1 & chosen[2])
    end

    heads = Relation()
    tails = Relation()
    # 0.5::heads(Coin); 0.5::tails(Coin) :- toss(Coin), \+ biased(Coin).
    for ((Coin,), x1) in toss
        chosen = choose(0.5, 0.5)
        add!(heads, (Coin,), x1 & !holds(biased, (Coin,)) & chosen[1])
        add!(tails, (Coin,), x1 & !holds(biased, (Coin,)) & chosen[2])
    end
    # 0.6::heads(Coin); 0.4::tails(Coin) :- toss(Coin), biased(Coin).
    for ((Coin,), x1) in toss
        for x2 in probe(biased, (Coin,))
            chosen = choose(0.6, 0.4)
            add!(heads, (Coin,), x1 & x2 & chosen[1])
            add!(tails, (Coin,), x1 & x2 & chosen[2])
        end
    end

    queries = (holds(heads, (:coin,)), holds(tails, (:coin,)))
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

;; cplint_markov_factor.pl: a ProbLog program written in Pluck by tddlog's scripts/problog2ppl.py,
;; first order as it is written. A relation is a list of its tuples, each (Pair
;; TUPLE HOLDING), a symbol a constructor of its own and an integer a natural;
;; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), drawn once; each rule a
;; concat_map over the relations its body joins, a tuple that several instances
;; give holding where one does (`union`). Query cK asks the K-th query, given the
;; evidence.

(define-type weight (Sure) (Chance p))
(define (draw w) (match w Sure => (True) Chance p => (flip p)))
(define (draw_all fs) (map (lambda f -> (Pair (fst f) (draw (snd f)))) fs))
;; rel with the tuple t, holding where v does too
(define (insert eq t v rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (Cons (Pair t v) (Nil))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (Cons (Pair t (or (snd e) v)) rest) (Cons e (insert eq t v rest)))))
(define (union eq rel xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => rel
    Cons x rest => (union eq (insert eq (fst x) (snd x) rel) rest)))
;; whether the tuple t of rel holds; whether one of the tuples that p accepts does
(define (holds eq rel t)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (snd e) (holds eq rest t))))
(define (any_holds p rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (p (fst e)) (or (snd e) (any_holds p rest)) (any_holds p rest))))
(define (concat_map f xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Nil)
    Cons x rest => (append (f x) (concat_map f rest))))
(define (between lo hi) (if (> lo hi) (Nil) (Cons lo (between (S lo) hi))))
(define (size_of rels) (fold (lambda acc r -> (+ acc (length r))) 0 rels))
;; the coins of a probabilistic rule in a recursion, kept by instance across the stages: the
;; instances xs, each (Pair KEY (Pair BODY HEADS)), with the coin of each KEY in table (a new
;; one drawn where it has none): (Pair TABLE' the heads, each (Pair TUPLE HOLDING))
(define (coin_of eq k table)
  (match table
    Nil => (Pair (False) (False))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) k) (Pair (True) (snd e)) (coin_of eq k rest))))
(define (attach eq draw pick table xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Pair table (Nil))
    Cons x rest =>
    (let ((found (coin_of eq (fst x) table))
          (c (if (fst found) (snd found) (draw)))
          (table2 (if (fst found) table (Cons (Pair (fst x) c) table)))
          (more (attach eq draw pick table2 rest))
          (body (fst (snd x))))
      (Pair (fst more) (append (mapi (lambda h i -> (Pair h (and body (pick c i)))) (snd (snd x))) (snd more))))))

(define-type tuple0 (T0))
(define (eq_a a b) (True))
(define (eq_b a b) (True))
(define (eq_p a b) (True))
(define (eq_evidence a b) (True))

;; a/0: 1 facts
(define a_facts
  (Cons (Pair (T0) (Chance 0.5))
  (Nil)))
;; b/0: 1 facts
(define b_facts
  (Cons (Pair (T0) (Chance 0.5))
  (Nil)))

;; the evidence and the queries
(define (program)
  (let ((a_base (draw_all a_facts))
        (b_base (draw_all b_facts))
        (a a_base)
        (b b_base)
        (rule1 (concat_map (lambda e1 -> (match (fst e1) T0 => (concat_map (lambda e2 -> (match (fst e2) T0 => (Cons (Cons (Pair (T0) (and (and (snd e1) (snd e2)) (flip 0.3))) (Nil)) (Nil)))) b))) a))
        (rule2 (concat_map (lambda e4 -> (match (fst e4) T0 => (Cons (Cons (Pair (T0) (and (and (not (any_holds (lambda t3 -> (match t3 T0 => (True))) a)) (snd e4)) (flip 0.7))) (Nil)) (Nil)))) b))
        (rule3 (Cons (Cons (Pair (T0) (and (and (not (any_holds (lambda t5 -> (match t5 T0 => (True))) a)) (not (any_holds (lambda t6 -> (match t6 T0 => (True))) b))) (flip 0.4))) (Nil)) (Nil)))
        (rule4 (concat_map (lambda e8 -> (match (fst e8) T0 => (Cons (Cons (Pair (T0) (and (and (not (any_holds (lambda t7 -> (match t7 T0 => (True))) b)) (snd e8)) (flip 0.6))) (Nil)) (Nil)))) a))
        (p (union eq_p (Nil) (append (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule1) (append (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule2) (append (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule3) (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule4))))))
        (rule5 (concat_map (lambda e9 -> (match (fst e9) T0 => (concat_map (lambda e10 -> (match (fst e10) T0 => (Cons (Cons (Pair (T0) (and (snd e9) (snd e10))) (Nil)) (Nil)))) b))) p))
        (evidence (union eq_evidence (Nil) (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule5)))
        (q11 (holds eq_a a (T0))))
    (Pair (holds eq_evidence evidence (T0)) (Cons q11 (Nil)))))

(query c0 (let ((m (program))) (Posterior (index 0 (snd m)) (fst m))))

/*
Flexible probabilities: variable probabilistic annotations.
The example models drawing a person at random from a population and 
computing the probability that it is a male or a female.
From
J. Vennekens, S. Verbaeten, and M. Bruynooghe. Logic programs with annotated 
disjunctions. In International Conference on Logic Programming, 
volume 3131 of LNCS, pages 195-209. Springer, 2004.
*/
:- use_module(library(pita)).

:- if(current_predicate(use_rendering/1)).
:- use_rendering(c3).
:- endif.

:- pita.

:- begin_lpad.

male:M/P; female:F/P:-
  findall(Male,male(Male),LM),
  findall(Female,female(Female),LF),
  length(LM,M),
  length(LF,F),
  P is F+M.

:- end_lpad.

male(john).
male(david).

female(anna).
female(elen).
female(cathy).

/** <examples>

?- prob(male,Prob).  % what is the probability of sampling a male from the 
% population?
% expected result 0.4
?- prob(female,Prob). % what is the probability of sampling a female from the 
% population?
% expected result 0.6
?- prob(male,Prob),bar(Prob,C).  % what is the probability of sampling a male from the 
% population?
% expected result 0.4
?- prob(female,Prob),bar(Prob,C). % what is the probability of sampling a female from the 
% population?
% expected result 0.6
*/

 

main :-
    forall((Q = male, prob(Q, P)), format("~q:\t~w~n", [Q, P])),
    forall((Q = female, prob(Q, P)), format("~q:\t~w~n", [Q, P])).

From

flu(bob).

hay_fever(bob).

# cplint_swish_admission.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    female_facts = get(db, "female/0", Relation())
    qualified_facts = get(db, "qualified/0", Relation())

    female = female_facts

    deptB = Relation()
    # deptB :- female.
    for x1 in probe(female, ())
        add!(deptB, (), x1)
    end
    # 0.5::deptB :- \+ female.
    add!(deptB, (), !holds(female, ()) & flip(0.5))

    qualified = qualified_facts

    admitted = Relation()
    # admitted :- deptB, female, qualified.
    for x1 in probe(deptB, ())
        for x2 in probe(female, ())
            for x3 in probe(qualified, ())
                add!(admitted, (), x1 & x2 & x3)
            end
        end
    end
    # admitted :- \+ deptB, \+ female.
    add!(admitted, (), !holds(deptB, ()) & !holds(female, ()))

    queries = (holds(admitted, ()),)
    evidence = holds(female, ())
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

holdsAt(F, T) :- initially(F),
  \+ clipped(0, F, T).
holdsAt(F, T2) :- initiates(F, T1),
  T1 < T2 ,
  \+ clipped(T1 ,F, T2 ).
clipped(T1 ,F, T3) :- terminates(F, T2),
  T1 < T2 , T2 < T3.
