;; cplint_mendel.pl: a ProbLog program written for Roulette by tddlog's
;; scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a hash
;; from its tuples (lists of constants) to whether each holds, a Boolean of the
;; coins; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from the
;; facts file named on the command line; each rule is a loop over the
;; relations its body joins. Each query's distribution is Roulette's, at the
;; module's level (`display-pmf`), given the evidence; the program prints
;; `roulette K true P` and `roulette K false P` for the K-th query.

(require racket/port racket/string racket/match)

;; A statement of the program: a definition, which the language does not
;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

;; the tuple t of r holds also where x does
(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))
;; whether the tuple t of r holds
(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))
;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their
;; values at positions ps (from 0)
(define (index r . ps)
  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])
    (hash-update! ix (for/list ([p (in-list ps)]) (list-ref t p)) (λ (es) (cons (cons t x) es)) null))
  ix)
;; whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))
;; the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

(define (constant s) (or (string->number s) (string->symbol s)))
;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
(define (facts path)
  (define db (make-hash))
  (for ([line (in-lines (open-input-file path))])
    (define f (string-split line "\t" #:trim? #f))
    (define p (string->number (cadr f)))
    (add! (hash-ref! db (car f) make-hash) (map constant (cddr f)) (if (>= p 1) #t (flip p))))
  db)

;; The distribution of v, a list of (value . probability): Roulette's query
;; at the module's level (`display-pmf`), read back from the table it
;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone.
(define (distribution v)
  (define text (with-output-to-string (λ () (display-pmf v))))
  (define (datum s)
    (define d (read (open-input-string s)))
    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))
  (define rows
    (for/list ([line (in-list (string-split text "\n"))]
               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))
  (if (null? rows)
      (list (cons (datum text) 1))
      (for/list ([r (in-list rows)]
                 #:unless (equal? r '("Value" "Probability")))
        (cons (datum (car r)) (string->number (cadr r))))))
(define (real p) (if (exact? p) (exact->inexact p) p))
(define (probability dist v)
  (define e (assoc v dist))
  (if e (cdr e) 0))
(define (report dists)
  (for ([dist (in-list dists)] [k (in-naturals 1)])
    (printf "roulette ~a true ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #t)))
    (printf "roulette ~a false ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #f)))))

(define db (facts (vector-ref (current-command-line-arguments) 0)))
(define mother-facts (hash-ref db "mother/2" (make-hash)))
(define father-facts (hash-ref db "father/2" (make-hash)))
(define cg-facts (hash-ref db "cg/3" (make-hash)))

(define father father-facts)

(define mother mother-facts)

;; cg/3: recursive; the rules applied in stages from no tuple, each
;; reading the stage before, until a stage adds no tuple and the stages number the tuples
(define coins3 (make-hash))   ; by instance, of `0.5::cg(X,1,A); 0.5::cg(X,1,B) :- mother(Y,X), cg(Y,1,A), cg(Y,2,B).`
(define coins4 (make-hash))   ; by instance, of `0.5::cg(X,2,A); 0.5::cg(X,2,B) :- father(Y,X), cg(Y,1,A), cg(Y,2,B).`
(define (stage-cg cg)
  (define next-cg (hash-copy cg-facts))
  (define cg-by-1-2 (index cg 0 1))
  ;; 0.5::cg(X,1,A); 0.5::cg(X,1,B) :- mother(Y,X), cg(Y,1,A), cg(Y,2,B).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs mother)])
    (match-define (cons (list Y X) x1) t2)
    (for ([t4 (in-list (hash-ref cg-by-1-2 (list Y 1) null))])
      (match-define (cons (list _ _ A) x3) t4)
      (for ([t6 (in-list (hash-ref cg-by-1-2 (list Y 2) null))])
        (match-define (cons (list _ _ B) x5) t6)
        (let ([chosen (hash-ref! coins3 (list X A B Y) (λ () (choose 0.5 0.5)))])
          (add! next-cg (list X 1 A) (&& x1 x3 x5 (list-ref chosen 0)))
          (add! next-cg (list X 1 B) (&& x1 x3 x5 (list-ref chosen 1)))))))
  ;; 0.5::cg(X,2,A); 0.5::cg(X,2,B) :- father(Y,X), cg(Y,1,A), cg(Y,2,B).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs father)])
    (match-define (cons (list Y X) x1) t2)
    (for ([t4 (in-list (hash-ref cg-by-1-2 (list Y 1) null))])
      (match-define (cons (list _ _ A) x3) t4)
      (for ([t6 (in-list (hash-ref cg-by-1-2 (list Y 2) null))])
        (match-define (cons (list _ _ B) x5) t6)
        (let ([chosen (hash-ref! coins4 (list X A B Y) (λ () (choose 0.5 0.5)))])
          (add! next-cg (list X 2 A) (&& x1 x3 x5 (list-ref chosen 0)))
          (add! next-cg (list X 2 B) (&& x1 x3 x5 (list-ref chosen 1)))))))
  (list next-cg))
(define-values (cg)
  (let loop ([rels (list (make-hash))] [stage 0] [before -1])
    (define size (for/sum ([r (in-list rels)]) (hash-count r)))
    (if (or (< stage size) (not (= size before)))
        (loop (apply stage-cg rels) (+ stage 1) size)
        (apply values rels))))

(define cg-by-3 (index cg 2))
(define cg-by-2-3 (index cg 1 2))
(define color (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; color(X,purple) :- cg(X,_,p).
  (for ([t2 (in-list (hash-ref cg-by-3 (list 'p) null))])
    (match-define (cons (list X _ _) x1) t2)
    (add! color (list X 'purple) x1))
  ;; color(X,white) :- cg(X,1,w), cg(X,2,w).
  (for ([t2 (in-list (hash-ref cg-by-2-3 (list 1 'w) null))])
    (match-define (cons (list X _ _) x1) t2)
    (for ([x3 (in-list (probe cg (list X 2 'w)))])
      (add! color (list X 'white) (&& x1 x3)))))

(define dists
  (list (distribution (holds color (list 's 'purple)))
        (distribution (holds color (list 's 'white)))
        (distribution (holds cg (list 's 1 'p)))
        (distribution (holds cg (list 's 1 'w)))
        (distribution (holds cg (list 's 2 'p)))
        (distribution (holds cg (list 's 2 'w)))))
(statement (report dists))

# cplint_swish_sneezing_simple.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    flu_facts = get(db, "flu/1", Relation())
    hay_fever_facts = get(db, "hay_fever/1", Relation())

    flu = flu_facts

    hay_fever = hay_fever_facts

    sneezing = Relation()
    # 0.7::sneezing(X) :- flu(X).
    for ((X,), x1) in flu
        add!(sneezing, (X,), x1 & flip(0.7))
    end
    # 0.8::sneezing(X) :- hay_fever(X).
    for ((X,), x1) in hay_fever
        add!(sneezing, (X,), x1 & flip(0.8))
    end

    queries = (holds(sneezing, (:bob,)),)
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

# cplint_alarm.pl: a ProbLog program written in SPPL by tddlog's scripts/problog2ppl.py,
# first order as it is written. The facts and the joins of the rules are Python
# constants, computed before the first sample: each rule's matches a list
# comprehension over the relations its body joins, a recursive component's
# tuples a fixpoint of its rules, and the tuples that the queries and the
# evidence read. Then each probabilistic fact and each instance of a
# probabilistic rule samples a coin, and each instance of a tuple that is read
# sets a variable of its own, in a `for` over its component's instances: 1
# where its body holds or an earlier instance of its tuple does, the last of a
# tuple's instances its holding. A cycle of tuples that read each other does so
# in as many stages as it has tuples, each stage reading the one before. The
# queries are the events of queries_(), asked of the model given the evidence:
#
#   sppl_dice.py PROGRAM.sppl
#
# queries
# component 0 bool query0
# component 1 bool query1

from functools import reduce
from itertools import accumulate

yes_ = lambda: true_ << {1}
no_ = lambda: true_ << {0}
all_ = lambda es_: reduce(lambda a_, b_: a_ & b_, es_) if es_ else yes_()
fix_ = lambda g_, x_: (lambda y_: x_ if y_ == x_ else fix_(g_, y_))(g_(x_))
dedup_ = lambda xs_: list(dict.fromkeys(xs_))

by_ = lambda ts_, ps_: reduce(lambda d_, j_: d_.setdefault(tuple(ts_[j_][p_] for p_ in ps_), []).append(j_) or d_,

idiv_ = lambda a_, b_: abs(a_) // abs(b_) * (1 if (a_ < 0) == (b_ < 0) else -1)

heads_ = lambda q_, ms_: [h_ for m_ in ms_ for r_, h_ in m_[1] if r_ == q_]
coins_of_ = lambda ps_, c0_: [None if p_ >= 1 else c0_ + n_
                              for p_, n_ in zip(ps_, accumulate([0] + [int(x_ < 1) for x_ in ps_]))]
# a relation's instances, each (its tuple's index, its coin and value or None, its refs); their indexes by tuple
facts_ = lambda i_, ts_, cs_: [(i_[t_], None if c_ is None else (c_, 1), []) for t_, c_ in zip(ts_, cs_)]
inst_ = lambda q_, i_, ms_, ks_, c0_: [(i_[h_], None if ks_ is None else (c0_ + ks_[m_[0]], n_ + 1), m_[2])
                                      for m_ in ms_ for n_, (r_, h_) in enumerate(m_[1]) if r_ == q_]
by_tuple_ = lambda es_, n_: (lambda d_: [d_.get((j_,), []) for j_ in range(n_)])(by_(es_, (0,)))
# the tuples (relation, index) that a tuple's instances read; those that tuples us_ read in turn, where ok_
reads_ = lambda u_: ([(r_, k_) for m_ in of_[u_[0]][u_[1]] for r_, k_, _, _ in insts_[u_[0]][m_][2]]
                     if u_[0] in of_ else [])
reach_ = lambda us_, ok_: fix_(lambda s_: s_ | {w_ for u_ in s_ for w_ in reads_(u_) if ok_(w_)}, frozenset(us_))
# a component's steps, each (relation, instance, stage, cycle), over the tuples of its relations c_ that the
# queries and the evidence read: its cycles of tuples (the tuples that reach the same ones), each after the
# cycles it reads (which reach fewer), in as many stages as it has tuples, each stage reading the one before
cycles_ = lambda rs_: sorted(reduce(lambda d_, u_: d_.setdefault(rs_[u_], []).append(u_) or d_, sorted(rs_),
                                    {}).values(), key=lambda us_: (len(rs_[us_[0]]), us_[0]))
steps_ = lambda c_: [(u_[0], m_, s_, g_) for g_, us_ in enumerate(cycles_(
                         {u_: reach_([u_], lambda w_: w_[0] in c_) for u_ in used_ if u_[0] in c_}))
                     for s_ in range(1, len(us_) + 1) for u_ in us_ for m_ in of_[u_[0]][u_[1]]]
# a step's tuple and stage; the step of a tuple's last instance at each stage; a tuple's last stage and its
# cycle; the step before each, where it is an earlier instance of its tuple at its stage
key_ = lambda x_: (x_[0], insts_[x_[0]][x_[1]][0], x_[2])
at_of_ = lambda st_: {key_(x_): k_ for k_, x_ in enumerate(st_)}
ends_ = lambda st_: {key_(x_)[:2]: (x_[2], x_[3]) for x_ in st_}
prev_ = lambda st_: [k_ - 1 if k_ and key_(st_[k_ - 1]) == key_(st_[k_]) else None for k_ in range(len(st_))]
# events: a fact's; a tuple's at stage s_ (None its last, 0 before the first); a step's coin and body, which
# reads the tuples of its own cycle at the stage before; the step's or the one before it
fact_ = lambda c_, v_: (yes_() if v_ else no_()) if c_ is None else coins_[c_] << {v_}
value_ = lambda a_, at_s_, end_, u_, v_, s_: (lambda t_: (no_() if v_ else yes_()) if t_ == 0
                                              else a_[at_s_[u_ + (t_,)]] << {v_})(end_[u_][0] if s_ is None else s_)
coin_ = lambda c_: [] if c_ is None else [coins_[c_[0]] << {c_[1]}]
step_ = lambda st_, end_, k_: (lambda q_, m_, s_, g_: all_(coin_(insts_[q_][m_][1]) + [
    at_[r_](j_, v_, s_ - 1 if w_ and end_[(r_, j_)][1] == g_ else None)
    for r_, j_, v_, w_ in insts_[q_][m_][2]]))(*st_[k_])
ev_ = lambda e_, p_, acc_: e_ if p_ is None else e_ | (acc_(p_) << {1})
holds_ = lambda q_, t_, v_: (lambda j_: (no_() if v_ else yes_()) if j_ is None else at_[q_](j_, v_, None))(
    ix_[q_].get(t_))


# rule 2: 0.1::burg(t); 0.9::burg(f).
rule2_m = [((), (('burg', ('t',)), ('burg', ('f',))), [])
    for _ in [()]]
burg_t = dedup_(heads_('burg', rule2_m))
burg_i = index_(burg_t)
rule2_k = index_(dedup_([m_[0] for m_ in rule2_m]))
rule2_c0 = 0
rule2_cd = [{1: 0.1, 2: 0.9}] * len(rule2_k)
burg_inst = inst_('burg', burg_i, rule2_m, rule2_k, rule2_c0)
burg_of = by_tuple_(burg_inst, len(burg_t))

# rule 3: 0.2::earthq(t); 0.8::earthq(f).
rule3_m = [((), (('earthq', ('t',)), ('earthq', ('f',))), [])
    for _ in [()]]
earthq_t = dedup_(heads_('earthq', rule3_m))
earthq_i = index_(earthq_t)
rule3_k = index_(dedup_([m_[0] for m_ in rule3_m]))
rule3_c0 = rule2_c0 + len(rule2_cd)
rule3_cd = [{1: 0.2, 2: 0.8}] * len(rule3_k)
earthq_inst = inst_('earthq', earthq_i, rule3_m, rule3_k, rule3_c0)
earthq_of = by_tuple_(earthq_inst, len(earthq_t))

# rule 1: alarm(t) :- burg(t), earthq(t).
rule1_m = [((), (('alarm', ('t',)),), [('burg', j1, 1, 0), ('earthq', j2, 1, 0)])
    for j1 in [burg_i.get(('t',))] if j1 is not None
    for j2 in [earthq_i.get(('t',))] if j2 is not None]
# rule 4: 0.8::alarm(t); 0.2::alarm(f) :- burg(t), earthq(f).
rule4_m = [((), (('alarm', ('t',)), ('alarm', ('f',))), [('burg', j1, 1, 0), ('earthq', j2, 1, 0)])
    for j1 in [burg_i.get(('t',))] if j1 is not None
    for j2 in [earthq_i.get(('f',))] if j2 is not None]
# rule 5: 0.8::alarm(t); 0.2::alarm(f) :- burg(f), earthq(t).
rule5_m = [((), (('alarm', ('t',)), ('alarm', ('f',))), [('burg', j1, 1, 0), ('earthq', j2, 1, 0)])
    for j1 in [burg_i.get(('f',))] if j1 is not None
    for j2 in [earthq_i.get(('t',))] if j2 is not None]
# rule 6: 0.1::alarm(t); 0.9::alarm(f) :- burg(f), earthq(f).
rule6_m = [((), (('alarm', ('t',)), ('alarm', ('f',))), [('burg', j1, 1, 0), ('earthq', j2, 1, 0)])
    for j1 in [burg_i.get(('f',))] if j1 is not None
    for j2 in [earthq_i.get(('f',))] if j2 is not None]
alarm_t = dedup_(heads_('alarm', rule1_m + rule4_m + rule5_m + rule6_m))
alarm_i = index_(alarm_t)
rule4_k = index_(dedup_([m_[0] for m_ in rule4_m]))
rule4_c0 = rule3_c0 + len(rule3_cd)
rule4_cd = [{1: 0.8, 2: 0.2}] * len(rule4_k)
rule5_k = index_(dedup_([m_[0] for m_ in rule5_m]))
rule5_c0 = rule4_c0 + len(rule4_cd)
rule5_cd = [{1: 0.8, 2: 0.2}] * len(rule5_k)
rule6_k = index_(dedup_([m_[0] for m_ in rule6_m]))
rule6_c0 = rule5_c0 + len(rule5_cd)
rule6_cd = [{1: 0.1, 2: 0.9}] * len(rule6_k)
alarm_inst = inst_('alarm', alarm_i, rule1_m, None, 0) + inst_('alarm', alarm_i, rule4_m, rule4_k, rule4_c0) + inst_('alarm', alarm_i, rule5_m, rule5_k, rule5_c0) + inst_('alarm', alarm_i, rule6_m, rule6_k, rule6_c0)
alarm_of = by_tuple_(alarm_inst, len(alarm_t))

at_ = {
    'burg': lambda j_, v_, s_: value_(comp1_acc, comp1_at, comp1_end, ('burg', j_), v_, s_),
    'earthq': lambda j_, v_, s_: value_(comp2_acc, comp2_at, comp2_end, ('earthq', j_), v_, s_),
    'alarm': lambda j_, v_, s_: value_(comp3_acc, comp3_at, comp3_end, ('alarm', j_), v_, s_),}
ix_ = {'burg': burg_i, 'earthq': earthq_i, 'alarm': alarm_i}
coin_d_ = rule2_cd + rule3_cd + rule4_cd + rule5_cd + rule6_cd
insts_ = {'burg': burg_inst, 'earthq': earthq_inst, 'alarm': alarm_inst}
of_ = {'burg': burg_of, 'earthq': earthq_of, 'alarm': alarm_of}
# the tuples the queries and the evidence read, and those their instances read in turn
asked_ = [('alarm', ('t',)), ('alarm', ('f',))]
used_ = reach_([(q_, ix_[q_][t_]) for q_, t_ in asked_ if t_ in ix_.get(q_, {})], lambda w_: True)
comp1_steps = steps_({'burg'})
comp1_at = at_of_(comp1_steps)
comp1_end = ends_(comp1_steps)
comp1_prev = prev_(comp1_steps)
comp1_ev = lambda k_: ev_(step_(comp1_steps, comp1_end, k_), comp1_prev[k_], lambda i_: comp1_acc[i_])
comp2_steps = steps_({'earthq'})
comp2_at = at_of_(comp2_steps)
comp2_end = ends_(comp2_steps)
comp2_prev = prev_(comp2_steps)
comp2_ev = lambda k_: ev_(step_(comp2_steps, comp2_end, k_), comp2_prev[k_], lambda i_: comp2_acc[i_])
comp3_steps = steps_({'alarm'})
comp3_at = at_of_(comp3_steps)
comp3_end = ends_(comp3_steps)
comp3_prev = prev_(comp3_steps)
comp3_ev = lambda k_: ev_(step_(comp3_steps, comp3_end, k_), comp3_prev[k_], lambda i_: comp3_acc[i_])
queries_ = lambda: [holds_('alarm', ('t',), 1), holds_('alarm', ('f',), 1)]

coins_ = array(len(coin_d_))
comp1_acc = array(len(comp1_steps))
comp2_acc = array(len(comp2_steps))
comp3_acc = array(len(comp3_steps))

true_ ~= atomic(loc=1)
for n_ in range(len(coin_d_)):
    coins_[n_] ~= discrete(coin_d_[n_])
# burg/1: an instance holds where its body or an earlier instance of its tuple does
for k_ in range(len(comp1_steps)):
    if comp1_ev(k_):
        comp1_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=1)
    else:
        comp1_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=0)
# earthq/1: an instance holds where its body or an earlier instance of its tuple does
for k_ in range(len(comp2_steps)):
    if comp2_ev(k_):
        comp2_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=1)
    else:
        comp2_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=0)
# alarm/1: an instance holds where its body or an earlier instance of its tuple does
for k_ in range(len(comp3_steps)):
    if comp3_ev(k_):
        comp3_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=1)
    else:
        comp3_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=0)

/* Smoking and the Genotype Theory

From Section 3.3.3 of Pearl, Judea. Causality. Cambridge university press, 2009.

*/

:- use_module(library(pita)).

:- if(current_predicate(use_rendering/1)).
:- use_rendering(graphviz).
:- endif.

:- pita.

:- begin_lpad.

:- action smoker/0.
smoker:0.5.

tar:0.05:- \+ smoker.
tar:0.95:- smoker.

cancer:0.10:- \+ smoker,\+ tar.
cancer:0.90:- smoker,\+ tar.
cancer:0.05:- \+ smoker, tar.
cancer:0.85:- smoker, tar.

:-end_lpad.

smoking_effect_on_cancer(P):-
  prob(tar,smoker,P_z_x),
  prob(cancer,(smoker,tar),P_y_xz),
  prob(cancer,(smoker,\+ tar), P_y_xnz),
  prob(cancer,(\+ smoker,tar),P_y_nxz),
  prob(cancer,(\+ smoker,\+ tar), P_y_nxnz),
  prob(smoker,P_x),
  P_nx is 1-P_x,
  P_nz_x is 1-P_z_x,
  P is P_z_x*(P_y_xz*P_x+P_y_nxz*P_nx)+P_nz_x*(P_y_xnz*P_x+P_y_nxnz*P_nx).

no_smoking_effect_on_cancer(P):-
  prob(tar,\+ smoker,P_z_nx),
  prob(cancer,(smoker,tar),P_y_xz),
  prob(cancer,(smoker,\+ tar), P_y_xnz),
  prob(cancer,(\+ smoker,tar),P_y_nxz),
  prob(cancer,(\+ smoker,\+ tar), P_y_nxnz),
  prob(smoker,P_x),
  P_nx is 1-P_x,
  P_nz_nx is 1-P_z_nx,
  P is P_z_nx*(P_y_xz*P_x+P_y_nxz*P_nx)+P_nz_nx*(P_y_xnz*P_x+P_y_nxnz*P_nx).


/** <examples>
?- Network = dot(digraph(['Tar Z'->'Cancer Y','Smoking X'->'Tar Z','Smoking X'->'Cancer Y'])).
?- MutilatedNetwork = dot(digraph(['Drug C'->'Recovery E','Gender F'->'Recovery E'])).
?- smoking_effect_on_cancer(P).
?- no_smoking_effect_on_cancer(P).
?- prob(cancer,smoker,P).
?- prob(cancer,\+ smoker,P).
?- prob(cancer,tar,P).
?- prob(cancer,\+ tar,P).
*/

;; cplint_mendelc.pl: a ProbLog program written in Pluck by tddlog's scripts/problog2ppl.py,
;; first order as it is written. A relation is a list of its tuples, each (Pair
;; TUPLE HOLDING), a symbol a constructor of its own and an integer a natural;
;; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), drawn once; each rule a
;; concat_map over the relations its body joins, a tuple that several instances
;; give holding where one does (`union`). Query cK asks the K-th query, given the
;; evidence.

(define-type weight (Sure) (Chance p))
(define (draw w) (match w Sure => (True) Chance p => (flip p)))
(define (draw_all fs) (map (lambda f -> (Pair (fst f) (draw (snd f)))) fs))
;; rel with the tuple t, holding where v does too
(define (insert eq t v rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (Cons (Pair t v) (Nil))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (Cons (Pair t (or (snd e) v)) rest) (Cons e (insert eq t v rest)))))
(define (union eq rel xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => rel
    Cons x rest => (union eq (insert eq (fst x) (snd x) rel) rest)))
;; whether the tuple t of rel holds; whether one of the tuples that p accepts does
(define (holds eq rel t)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (snd e) (holds eq rest t))))
(define (any_holds p rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (p (fst e)) (or (snd e) (any_holds p rest)) (any_holds p rest))))
(define (concat_map f xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Nil)
    Cons x rest => (append (f x) (concat_map f rest))))
(define (between lo hi) (if (> lo hi) (Nil) (Cons lo (between (S lo) hi))))
(define (size_of rels) (fold (lambda acc r -> (+ acc (length r))) 0 rels))
;; the coins of a probabilistic rule in a recursion, kept by instance across the stages: the
;; instances xs, each (Pair KEY (Pair BODY HEADS)), with the coin of each KEY in table (a new
;; one drawn where it has none): (Pair TABLE' the heads, each (Pair TUPLE HOLDING))
(define (coin_of eq k table)
  (match table
    Nil => (Pair (False) (False))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) k) (Pair (True) (snd e)) (coin_of eq k rest))))
(define (attach eq draw pick table xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Pair table (Nil))
    Cons x rest =>
    (let ((found (coin_of eq (fst x) table))
          (c (if (fst found) (snd found) (draw)))
          (table2 (if (fst found) table (Cons (Pair (fst x) c) table)))
          (more (attach eq draw pick table2 rest))
          (body (fst (snd x))))
      (Pair (fst more) (append (mapi (lambda h i -> (Pair h (and body (pick c i)))) (snd (snd x))) (snd more))))))

(define-type sym (c_1) (c_2) (c_f) (c_ff) (c_fm) (c_m) (c_mf) (c_mm) (c_p) (c_purple) (c_s) (c_w) (c_white))
(define-type tuple2 (T2 a1 a2))
(define-type tuple3 (T3 a1 a2 a3))
(define-type tuple4 (T4 a1 a2 a3 a4))
(define (eq_mother a b) (match a T2 a1 a2 => (match b T2 b1 b2 => (and (constructor=? a1 b1) (constructor=? a2 b2)))))
(define (eq_father a b) (match a T2 a1 a2 => (match b T2 b1 b2 => (and (constructor=? a1 b1) (constructor=? a2 b2)))))
(define (eq_cg a b) (match a T3 a1 a2 a3 => (match b T3 b1 b2 b3 => (and (constructor=? a1 b1) (and (constructor=? a2 b2) (constructor=? a3 b3))))))
(define (eq_color a b) (match a T2 a1 a2 => (match b T2 b1 b2 => (and (constructor=? a1 b1) (constructor=? a2 b2)))))
(define (eq_k3 a b) (match a T4 a1 a2 a3 a4 => (match b T4 b1 b2 b3 b4 => (and (constructor=? a1 b1) (and (constructor=? a2 b2) (and (constructor=? a3 b3) (constructor=? a4 b4)))))))
(define (eq_k4 a b) (match a T4 a1 a2 a3 a4 => (match b T4 b1 b2 b3 b4 => (and (constructor=? a1 b1) (and (constructor=? a2 b2) (and (constructor=? a3 b3) (constructor=? a4 b4)))))))

;; mother/2: 3 facts
(define mother_facts
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_m) (c_s)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_mm) (c_m)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_mf) (c_f)) (Sure))
  (Nil)))))
;; father/2: 3 facts
(define father_facts
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_f) (c_s)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_fm) (c_m)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T2 (c_ff) (c_f)) (Sure))
  (Nil)))))
;; cg/3: 8 facts
(define cg_facts
  (Cons (Pair (T3 (c_mm) (c_1) (c_p)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T3 (c_mm) (c_2) (c_w)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T3 (c_fm) (c_1) (c_p)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T3 (c_fm) (c_2) (c_p)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T3 (c_mf) (c_1) (c_w)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T3 (c_mf) (c_2) (c_w)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T3 (c_ff) (c_1) (c_w)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T3 (c_ff) (c_2) (c_p)) (Sure))
  (Nil))))))))))

;; the evidence and the queries
(define (program)
  (let ((mother_base (draw_all mother_facts))
        (father_base (draw_all father_facts))
        (cg_base (draw_all cg_facts))
        (father father_base)
        (mother mother_base)
        (stage1 (lambda rels -> (let ((cg (index 0 (fst rels)))
        (coins3 (index 0 (snd rels)))
        (coins4 (index 1 (snd rels)))
        (rc3 (attach eq_k3 (lambda -> (if (flip 0.5) 0 1)) (lambda c i -> (== c i)) coins3 (concat_map (lambda e3 -> (match (fst e3) T2 vY vX => (concat_map (lambda e6 -> (match (fst e6) T3 a4 a5 vA => (if (and (constructor=? a4 vY) (constructor=? a5 (c_1))) (concat_map (lambda e9 -> (match (fst e9) T3 a7 a8 vB => (if (and (constructor=? a7 vY) (constructor=? a8 (c_2))) (Cons (Pair (T4 vX vA vB vY) (Pair (and (snd e3) (and (snd e6) (snd e9))) (Cons (T3 vX (c_1) vA) (Cons (T3 vX (c_1) vB) (Nil))))) (Nil)) (Nil)))) cg) (Nil)))) cg))) mother)))
        (rc4 (attach eq_k4 (lambda -> (if (flip 0.5) 0 1)) (lambda c i -> (== c i)) coins4 (concat_map (lambda e10 -> (match (fst e10) T2 vY vX => (concat_map (lambda e13 -> (match (fst e13) T3 a11 a12 vA => (if (and (constructor=? a11 vY) (constructor=? a12 (c_1))) (concat_map (lambda e16 -> (match (fst e16) T3 a14 a15 vB => (if (and (constructor=? a14 vY) (constructor=? a15 (c_2))) (Cons (Pair (T4 vX vA vB vY) (Pair (and (snd e10) (and (snd e13) (snd e16))) (Cons (T3 vX (c_2) vA) (Cons (T3 vX (c_2) vB) (Nil))))) (Nil)) (Nil)))) cg) (Nil)))) cg))) father))))
      (Pair (Cons (union eq_cg cg_base (append (snd rc3) (snd rc4))) (Nil)) (Cons (fst rc3) (Cons (fst rc4) (Nil)))))))
        (rels2 ((Y (lambda rec rels stage before -> (let (size (size_of (fst rels))) (if (or (< stage size) (not (== size before))) (rec (stage1 rels) (S stage) size) rels)))) (Pair (Cons (Nil) (Nil)) (Cons (Nil) (Cons (Nil) (Nil)))) 0 1))
        (cg (index 0 (fst rels2)))
        (rule1 (concat_map (lambda e19 -> (match (fst e19) T3 vX a17 a18 => (if (constructor=? a18 (c_p)) (Cons (Cons (Pair (T2 vX (c_purple)) (snd e19)) (Nil)) (Nil)) (Nil)))) cg))
        (rule2 (concat_map (lambda e22 -> (match (fst e22) T3 vX a20 a21 => (if (and (constructor=? a20 (c_1)) (constructor=? a21 (c_w))) (concat_map (lambda e26 -> (match (fst e26) T3 a23 a24 a25 => (if (and (constructor=? a23 vX) (and (constructor=? a24 (c_2)) (constructor=? a25 (c_w)))) (Cons (Cons (Pair (T2 vX (c_white)) (and (snd e22) (snd e26))) (Nil)) (Nil)) (Nil)))) cg) (Nil)))) cg))
        (color (union eq_color (Nil) (append (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule1) (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule2))))
        (q27 (holds eq_color color (T2 (c_s) (c_purple))))
        (q28 (holds eq_color color (T2 (c_s) (c_white))))
        (q29 (holds eq_cg cg (T3 (c_s) (c_1) (c_p))))
        (q30 (holds eq_cg cg (T3 (c_s) (c_1) (c_w))))
        (q31 (holds eq_cg cg (T3 (c_s) (c_2) (c_p))))
        (q32 (holds eq_cg cg (T3 (c_s) (c_2) (c_w)))))
    (Pair (True) (Cons q27 (Cons q28 (Cons q29 (Cons q30 (Cons q31 (Cons q32 (Nil))))))))))

(query c0 (let ((m (program))) (Marginal (index 0 (snd m)))))
(query c1 (let ((m (program))) (Marginal (index 1 (snd m)))))
(query c2 (let ((m (program))) (Marginal (index 2 (snd m)))))
(query c3 (let ((m (program))) (Marginal (index 3 (snd m)))))
(query c4 (let ((m (program))) (Marginal (index 4 (snd m)))))
(query c5 (let ((m (program))) (Marginal (index 5 (snd m)))))

/*
Model checking of a Markov chain: we want to know what is the likelihood
that on an execution of the chain from a start state s, a final state t
will be reached?
From
Gorlin, Andrey, C. R. Ramakrishnan, and Scott A. Smolka. "Model checking with probabilistic tabled logic programming." Theory and Practice of Logic Programming 12.4-5 (2012): 681-700.
*/

:- use_module(library(pita)).

:- if(current_predicate(use_rendering/1)).
:- use_rendering(c3).
:- use_rendering(graphviz).
:- endif.

:- pita.

:- set_pita(depth_bound,true).
:- set_pita(depth,5).


:- begin_lpad.

% reach(S, I, T) starting at state S at instance I,
%   state T is reachable.
reach(S, I, T) :-
  trans(S, I, U),
  reach(U, next(I), T).

reach(S, _, S).

% trans(S,I,T) transition from S at instance I goes to T

trans(s0,S,s0):0.5; trans(s0,S,s1):0.3; trans(s0,S,s2):0.2.

trans(s1,S,s1):0.4; trans(s1,S,s3):0.1; trans(s1,S,s4):0.5.

trans(s4,_,s3).
:- end_lpad.

markov_chain(digraph(G)):-
    findall(edge(A -> B,[label=P]),
      (clause(trans(A,_,B,_,_,_),
        (get_var_n(_,_,_,_,Probs,_),equalityc(_,_,N,_))),
        nth0(N,Probs,P)),
      G0),
    findall(edge(A -> B,[label=1.0]),
      clause(trans(A,_,B,_,_,_),onec(_,_)),
      G1),
    append(G0,G1,G).


/** <examples>

?- prob(reach(s0,0,s0),P).
% expecte result ~ 1.

?- prob(reach(s0,0,s1),P).
% expecte result ~ 0.5984054054054054.

?- prob(reach(s0,0,s2),P).
% expecte result ~ 0.4025135135135135.

?- prob(reach(s0,0,s3),P).
% expecte result ~ 0.5998378378378378.

?- prob(reach(s0,0,s4),P).
% expecte result ~ 0.49948717948717947.

?- prob(reach(s1,0,s0),P).
% expecte result ~ 0.

?- markov_chain(G).
% draw the Markov chain
*/

# cplint_alarm.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)

    burg = Relation()
    # 0.1::burg(t); 0.9::burg(f).
    chosen = choose(0.1, 0.9)
    add!(burg, (:t,), chosen[1])
    add!(burg, (:f,), chosen[2])

    earthq = Relation()
    # 0.2::earthq(t); 0.8::earthq(f).
    chosen = choose(0.2, 0.8)
    add!(earthq, (:t,), chosen[1])
    add!(earthq, (:f,), chosen[2])

    alarm = Relation()
    # alarm(t) :- burg(t), earthq(t).
    for x1 in probe(burg, (:t,))
        for x2 in probe(earthq, (:t,))
            add!(alarm, (:t,), x1 & x2)
        end
    end
    # 0.8::alarm(t); 0.2::alarm(f) :- burg(t), earthq(f).
    for x1 in probe(burg, (:t,))
        for x2 in probe(earthq, (:f,))
            chosen = choose(0.8, 0.2)
            add!(alarm, (:t,), x1 & x2 & chosen[1])
            add!(alarm, (:f,), x1 & x2 & chosen[2])
        end
    end
    # 0.8::alarm(t); 0.2::alarm(f) :- burg(f), earthq(t).
    for x1 in probe(burg, (:f,))
        for x2 in probe(earthq, (:t,))
            chosen = choose(0.8, 0.2)
            add!(alarm, (:t,), x1 & x2 & chosen[1])
            add!(alarm, (:f,), x1 & x2 & chosen[2])
        end
    end
    # 0.1::alarm(t); 0.9::alarm(f) :- burg(f), earthq(f).
    for x1 in probe(burg, (:f,))
        for x2 in probe(earthq, (:f,))
            chosen = choose(0.1, 0.9)
            add!(alarm, (:t,), x1 & x2 & chosen[1])
            add!(alarm, (:f,), x1 & x2 & chosen[2])
        end
    end

    queries = (holds(alarm, (:t,)), holds(alarm, (:f,)))
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

;; cplint_earthquake.pl: a ProbLog program written in Pluck by tddlog's scripts/problog2ppl.py,
;; first order as it is written. A relation is a list of its tuples, each (Pair
;; TUPLE HOLDING), a symbol a constructor of its own and an integer a natural;
;; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), drawn once; each rule a
;; concat_map over the relations its body joins, a tuple that several instances
;; give holding where one does (`union`). Query cK asks the K-th query, given the
;; evidence.

(define-type weight (Sure) (Chance p))
(define (draw w) (match w Sure => (True) Chance p => (flip p)))
(define (draw_all fs) (map (lambda f -> (Pair (fst f) (draw (snd f)))) fs))
;; rel with the tuple t, holding where v does too
(define (insert eq t v rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (Cons (Pair t v) (Nil))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (Cons (Pair t (or (snd e) v)) rest) (Cons e (insert eq t v rest)))))
(define (union eq rel xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => rel
    Cons x rest => (union eq (insert eq (fst x) (snd x) rel) rest)))
;; whether the tuple t of rel holds; whether one of the tuples that p accepts does
(define (holds eq rel t)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) t) (snd e) (holds eq rest t))))
(define (any_holds p rel)
  (match rel
    Nil => (False)
    Cons e rest => (if (p (fst e)) (or (snd e) (any_holds p rest)) (any_holds p rest))))
(define (concat_map f xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Nil)
    Cons x rest => (append (f x) (concat_map f rest))))
(define (between lo hi) (if (> lo hi) (Nil) (Cons lo (between (S lo) hi))))
(define (size_of rels) (fold (lambda acc r -> (+ acc (length r))) 0 rels))
;; the coins of a probabilistic rule in a recursion, kept by instance across the stages: the
;; instances xs, each (Pair KEY (Pair BODY HEADS)), with the coin of each KEY in table (a new
;; one drawn where it has none): (Pair TABLE' the heads, each (Pair TUPLE HOLDING))
(define (coin_of eq k table)
  (match table
    Nil => (Pair (False) (False))
    Cons e rest => (if (eq (fst e) k) (Pair (True) (snd e)) (coin_of eq k rest))))
(define (attach eq draw pick table xs)
  (match xs
    Nil => (Pair table (Nil))
    Cons x rest =>
    (let ((found (coin_of eq (fst x) table))
          (c (if (fst found) (snd found) (draw)))
          (table2 (if (fst found) table (Cons (Pair (fst x) c) table)))
          (more (attach eq draw pick table2 rest))
          (body (fst (snd x))))
      (Pair (fst more) (append (mapi (lambda h i -> (Pair h (and body (pick c i)))) (snd (snd x))) (snd more))))))

(define-type sym (c_eyjafjallajkull) (c_moderate) (c_stromboli) (c_strong))
(define-type tuple1 (T1 a1))
(define-type tuple2 (T2 a1 a2))
(define (eq_earthquake a b) (match a T2 a1 a2 => (match b T2 b1 b2 => (and (constructor=? a1 b1) (constructor=? a2 b2)))))
(define (eq_fault_rupture a b) (match a T1 a1 => (match b T1 b1 => (constructor=? a1 b1))))
(define (eq_volcanic_eruption a b) (match a T1 a1 => (match b T1 b1 => (constructor=? a1 b1))))

;; fault_rupture/1: 1 facts
(define fault_rupture_facts
  (Cons (Pair (T1 (c_stromboli)) (Sure))
  (Nil)))
;; volcanic_eruption/1: 2 facts
(define volcanic_eruption_facts
  (Cons (Pair (T1 (c_stromboli)) (Sure))
  (Cons (Pair (T1 (c_eyjafjallajkull)) (Sure))
  (Nil))))

;; the evidence and the queries
(define (program)
  (let ((fault_rupture_base (draw_all fault_rupture_facts))
        (volcanic_eruption_base (draw_all volcanic_eruption_facts))
        (fault_rupture fault_rupture_base)
        (volcanic_eruption volcanic_eruption_base)
        (rule1 (concat_map (lambda e1 -> (match (fst e1) T1 vX => (let (k2 (if (flip 0.3) 0 (if (flip 0.7142857142857143) 1 2))) (Cons (Cons (Pair (T2 vX (c_strong)) (and (snd e1) (== k2 0))) (Cons (Pair (T2 vX (c_moderate)) (and (snd e1) (== k2 1))) (Nil))) (Nil))))) fault_rupture))
        (rule2 (concat_map (lambda e3 -> (match (fst e3) T1 vX => (let (k4 (if (flip 0.2) 0 (if (flip 0.7499999999999999) 1 2))) (Cons (Cons (Pair (T2 vX (c_strong)) (and (snd e3) (== k4 0))) (Cons (Pair (T2 vX (c_moderate)) (and (snd e3) (== k4 1))) (Nil))) (Nil))))) volcanic_eruption))
        (earthquake (union eq_earthquake (Nil) (append (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule1) (append (map (lambda x -> (index 1 x)) rule1) (append (map (lambda x -> (index 0 x)) rule2) (map (lambda x -> (index 1 x)) rule2))))))
        (q5 (holds eq_earthquake earthquake (T2 (c_stromboli) (c_strong))))
        (q6 (holds eq_earthquake earthquake (T2 (c_stromboli) (c_moderate))))
        (q7 (holds eq_earthquake earthquake (T2 (c_eyjafjallajkull) (c_strong))))
        (q8 (holds eq_earthquake earthquake (T2 (c_eyjafjallajkull) (c_moderate)))))
    (Pair (True) (Cons q5 (Cons q6 (Cons q7 (Cons q8 (Nil))))))))

(query c0 (let ((m (program))) (Marginal (index 0 (snd m)))))
(query c1 (let ((m (program))) (Marginal (index 1 (snd m)))))
(query c2 (let ((m (program))) (Marginal (index 2 (snd m)))))
(query c3 (let ((m (program))) (Marginal (index 3 (snd m)))))

# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from

# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),

using Alea

const QUERY = :pr

# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over

        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix

holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)

# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest

    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))

# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()

        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end

function program(db)

    b_facts = get(db, "b/0", Relation())

#lang roulette/example/disrupt
;; cplint_sneezing.pl: a ProbLog program written for Roulette by tddlog's
;; scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a hash
;; from its tuples (lists of constants) to whether each holds, a Boolean of the
;; coins; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from the
;; facts file named on the command line; each rule is a loop over the
;; relations its body joins. Each query's distribution is Roulette's, at the
;; module's level (`display-pmf`), given the evidence; the program prints
;; `roulette K true P` and `roulette K false P` for the K-th query.

(require racket/port racket/string racket/match)

;; A statement of the program: a definition, which the language does not
;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

;; the tuple t of r holds also where x does
(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))
;; whether the tuple t of r holds
(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))
;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their
;; values at positions ps (from 0)
(define (index r . ps)
  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])
    (hash-update! ix (for/list ([p (in-list ps)]) (list-ref t p)) (λ (es) (cons (cons t x) es)) null))
  ix)
;; whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))
;; the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

(define (constant s) (or (string->number s) (string->symbol s)))
;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
(define (facts path)
  (define db (make-hash))
  (for ([line (in-lines (open-input-file path))])
    (define f (string-split line "\t" #:trim? #f))
    (define p (string->number (cadr f)))
    (add! (hash-ref! db (car f) make-hash) (map constant (cddr f)) (if (>= p 1) #t (flip p))))
  db)

;; The distribution of v, a list of (value . probability): Roulette's query
;; at the module's level (`display-pmf`), read back from the table it
;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone.
(define (distribution v)
  (define text (with-output-to-string (λ () (display-pmf v))))
  (define (datum s)
    (define d (read (open-input-string s)))
    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))
  (define rows
    (for/list ([line (in-list (string-split text "\n"))]
               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))
  (if (null? rows)
      (list (cons (datum text) 1))
      (for/list ([r (in-list rows)]
                 #:unless (equal? r '("Value" "Probability")))
        (cons (datum (car r)) (string->number (cadr r))))))
(define (real p) (if (exact? p) (exact->inexact p) p))
(define (probability dist v)
  (define e (assoc v dist))
  (if e (cdr e) 0))
(define (report dists)
  (for ([dist (in-list dists)] [k (in-naturals 1)])
    (printf "roulette ~a true ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #t)))
    (printf "roulette ~a false ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #f)))))

(define db (facts (vector-ref (current-command-line-arguments) 0)))
(define flu-facts (hash-ref db "flu/1" (make-hash)))
(define hay-fever-facts (hash-ref db "hay_fever/1" (make-hash)))

(define flu flu-facts)

(define hay-fever hay-fever-facts)

(define moderate-sneezing (make-hash))
(define strong-sneezing (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; 0.3::strong_sneezing(X); 0.5::moderate_sneezing(X) :- flu(X).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs flu)])
    (match-define (cons (list X) x1) t2)
    (let ([chosen (choose 0.3 0.5)])
      (add! strong-sneezing (list X) (&& x1 (list-ref chosen 0)))
      (add! moderate-sneezing (list X) (&& x1 (list-ref chosen 1)))))
  ;; 0.2::strong_sneezing(X); 0.6::moderate_sneezing(X) :- hay_fever(X).
  (for ([t2 (in-hash-pairs hay-fever)])
    (match-define (cons (list X) x1) t2)
    (let ([chosen (choose 0.2 0.6)])
      (add! strong-sneezing (list X) (&& x1 (list-ref chosen 0)))
      (add! moderate-sneezing (list X) (&& x1 (list-ref chosen 1))))))

(define dists
  (list (distribution (holds strong-sneezing (list 'bob)))
        (distribution (holds moderate-sneezing (list 'bob)))))
(statement (report dists))

/*
Program describing the Monty Hall puzzle which gets its name from the TV game 
show hosted by Monty Hall. A player is given the opportunity to
select one of three closed doors, behind one of which there is a prize. 
Behind the other two doors are empty rooms.
Once the player has made a selection, Monty is obligated to open one of the 
remaining closed doors which does not contain the prize, showing that the room 
behind it is empty. He then asks the player if he would like to switch
his selection to the other unopened door, or stay with his original choice. 
Here is the problem: Does it matter if he switches?
From
Chitta Baral, Michael Gelfond, and Nelson Rushton. "Probabilistic reasoning with answer sets." Theory and Practice of Logic Programming 9.01 (2009): 57-144.
*/
:- use_module(library(pita)).

:- if(current_predicate(use_rendering/1)).
:- use_rendering(c3).
:- endif.

:- pita.

:- begin_lpad.

% prize(A): the prize is behind door A, with A in {1,2,3}
% selected(A): the player selects door A
% open_door(A): Monty opens door A
% win_keep: the player wins in case he keeps his selection
% win_switch: the player wins in case he switches door


prize(1):1/3; prize(2):1/3; prize(3):1/3.
% the prize is behind each door with probability 1/3

selected(1).

;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))

(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))

;; values at positions ps (from 0)

  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])

  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))

;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

# cplint_light.pl: a ProbLog program written in Julia for Alea.jl by tddlog's
# scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a
# dictionary from its tuples to whether each holds, a Dist{Bool} of the coins
# or a Bool; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from
# the facts file FACTS; each rule is a loop over the relations its body
# joins. `model()` is the queries' holdings, given the evidence (`observe`),
# in the form of tddlog's data/alea programs: Alea.jl answers them with `pr`,
# and its tddlog backend writes their circuit for tddlog.
#
#   julia --project=ALEA alea_bench.jl run --file FACTS FACTS_PATH problog.jl
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const FACTS = ""   # the facts file (alea_bench.jl --file FACTS PATH)

const Relation = Dict{Tuple,Any}
const NONE = Pair{Tuple,Any}[]

# the tuple t of r holds also where x does
add!(r::Relation, t::Tuple, x) = (r[t] = haskey(r, t) ? r[t] | x : x; nothing)
# whether the tuple t of r holds
holds(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = get(r, t, false)
# whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
probe(r::Relation, t::Tuple) = haskey(r, t) ? (r[t],) : ()
# the tuples of r and whether each holds, by their values at positions ps
function index(r::Relation, ps...)
    ix = Dict{Tuple,Vector{Pair{Tuple,Any}}}()
    for (t, x) in r
        push!(get!(() -> Pair{Tuple,Any}[], ix, map(p -> t[p], ps)), t => x)
    end
    ix
end
# whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
holds_any(ix, k) = reduce(|, (x for (_, x) in get(ix, k, NONE)); init = false)
# the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
# head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
function choose(ps...)
    chosen, none, left = Any[], true, 1.0
    for p in ps
        q = left > 0 ? min(p / left, 1.0) : 1.0
        c = q >= 1.0 ? true : flip(q)
        push!(chosen, none & c)
        none, left = none & !c, left - p
    end
    chosen
end

constant(s) = something(tryparse(Int, s), tryparse(Float64, s), Some(Symbol(s)))
# the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
# a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
function facts(path)
    db = Dict{String,Relation}()
    for line in eachline(path)
        f = split(line, '\t')
        p = parse(Float64, f[2])
        add!(get!(Relation, db, f[1]), Tuple(constant.(f[3:end])), p >= 1 ? true : flip(p))
    end
    db
end

function program(db)
    push_facts = get(db, "push/0", Relation())

    push = push_facts

    light = Relation()
    # 0.4::light :- push.
    for x1 in probe(push, ())
        add!(light, (), x1 & flip(0.4))
    end

    replace = Relation()
    # replace :- \+ light.
    add!(replace, (), !holds(light, ()))

    queries = (holds(replace, ()), holds(light, ()))
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

    father = father_facts

    mother = mother_facts

    # cg/3: recursive; the rules applied in stages from no tuple, each
    # reading the stage before, until a stage adds no tuple and the stages number the tuples
    coins3 = Dict{Tuple,Any}()   # by instance, of `0.5::cg(X,1,A); 0.5::cg(X,1,B) :- mother(Y,X), cg(Y,1,A), cg(Y,2,B).`
    coins4 = Dict{Tuple,Any}()   # by instance, of `0.5::cg(X,2,A); 0.5::cg(X,2,B) :- father(Y,X), cg(Y,1,A), cg(Y,2,B).`
    cg = Relation()
    stage, before = 0, -1
    while stage < length(cg) || length(cg) != before
        before = length(cg)
        cg_by_1_2 = index(cg, 1, 2)
        next_cg = copy(cg_facts)
        # 0.5::cg(X,1,A); 0.5::cg(X,1,B) :- mother(Y,X), cg(Y,1,A), cg(Y,2,B).
        for ((Y, X), x1) in mother
            for ((_, _, A), x2) in get(cg_by_1_2, (Y, 1), NONE)
                for ((_, _, B), x3) in get(cg_by_1_2, (Y, 2), NONE)
                    chosen = get!(() -> choose(0.5, 0.5), coins3, (X, A, B, Y))
                    add!(next_cg, (X, 1, A), x1 & x2 & x3 & chosen[1])
                    add!(next_cg, (X, 1, B), x1 & x2 & x3 & chosen[2])
                end
            end
        end
        # 0.5::cg(X,2,A); 0.5::cg(X,2,B) :- father(Y,X), cg(Y,1,A), cg(Y,2,B).
        for ((Y, X), x1) in father
            for ((_, _, A), x2) in get(cg_by_1_2, (Y, 1), NONE)
                for ((_, _, B), x3) in get(cg_by_1_2, (Y, 2), NONE)
                    chosen = get!(() -> choose(0.5, 0.5), coins4, (X, A, B, Y))
                    add!(next_cg, (X, 2, A), x1 & x2 & x3 & chosen[1])
                    add!(next_cg, (X, 2, B), x1 & x2 & x3 & chosen[2])
                end
            end
        end
        cg = next_cg
        stage += 1
    end

    cg_by_3 = index(cg, 3)
    cg_by_2_3 = index(cg, 2, 3)
    color = Relation()
    # color(X,purple) :- cg(X,_,p).
    for ((X, _, _), x1) in get(cg_by_3, (:p,), NONE)
        add!(color, (X, :purple), x1)
    end
    # color(X,white) :- cg(X,1,w), cg(X,2,w).
    for ((X, _, _), x1) in get(cg_by_2_3, (1, :w), NONE)
        for x2 in probe(cg, (X, 2, :w))
            add!(color, (X, :white), x1 & x2)
        end
    end

    queries = (holds(color, (:s, :purple)), holds(color, (:s, :white)), holds(cg, (:s, 1, :p)), holds(cg, (:s, 1, :w)), holds(cg, (:s, 2, :p)), holds(cg, (:s, 2, :w)))
    evidence = true
    queries, evidence
end

# The queries' holdings, the evidence observed: Alea's `@alea` keeps the
# observation, and the relations are built outside it, as plain Julia.
function model()
    qs, ev = program(facts(FACTS))
    ev === true && return qs
    @alea begin
        observe(ev)
        qs
    end
end

/*
Computing the probability of a path between two nodes in a probabilistic graph.
Each edge has a probability of being present.
From
L. De Raedt, A. Kimmig, and H. Toivonen. ProbLog: A probabilistic Prolog and
its application in link discovery. In International Joint Conference on
Artificial Intelligence, pages 2462-2467, 2007.
*/
:- use_module(library(pita)).

:- if(current_predicate(use_rendering/1)).
:- use_rendering(c3).
:- use_rendering(graphviz).
:- use_rendering(table,[header(['Multivalued variable index','Rule index','Grounding substitution'])]).
:- endif.

:- pita.

:- begin_lpad.

% path(X,Y) is true if there is a path between nodes X and Y
% edge(a,b) indicates that there is an edge between a and b

path(X,X).
% there is surely a path between a node and itself

path(X,Y):-
  edge(X,Z),path(Z,Y).
% there is surely a path between X and Y if there is another node Z such that
% there is an edge between X and Z and there is a path between Z and Y

edge(a,b):0.2.
% there is an edge between a and b with probability 0.2
edge(b,e):0.5.
edge(a,c):0.3.
edge(c,d):0.4.
edge(d,e):0.4.
edge(a,e):0.1.

:- end_lpad.

graph(digraph([rankdir='LR'|G])):-
    findall(edge((A -> B),[label=P]),
      clause(edge(A,B,_,_),(get_var_n(_,_,_,_,[P|_],_),_)),
      G).


/** <examples>

?- prob(path(a,e),Prob). % what is the probability that a and e are connected?
% expected result 0.22888
?- prob(path(a,e),Prob),bar(Prob,C). % what is the probability that a and e are connected?
% expected result 0.22888
?- graph(G). % shows the probabilistic graph

?- bdd_dot_string(path(a,e),BDD,Var).
% What is the BDD for query path(a,e)?
% A solid edge indicates a 1-child, a dashed edge indicates a 0-child and
% a dotted
% edge indicates a negated 0-child.
% The table Var contains the associations between the rule groundings and the
% multivalued variables.

*/

main :-
    forall((Q = path(a,e), prob(Q, P)), format("~q:\t~w~n", [Q, P])).

# cplint_simpson.pl: a ProbLog program written in SPPL by tddlog's scripts/problog2ppl.py,
# first order as it is written. The facts and the joins of the rules are Python
# constants, computed before the first sample: each rule's matches a list
# comprehension over the relations its body joins, a recursive component's
# tuples a fixpoint of its rules, and the tuples that the queries and the
# evidence read. Then each probabilistic fact and each instance of a
# probabilistic rule samples a coin, and each instance of a tuple that is read
# sets a variable of its own, in a `for` over its component's instances: 1
# where its body holds or an earlier instance of its tuple does, the last of a
# tuple's instances its holding. A cycle of tuples that read each other does so
# in as many stages as it has tuples, each stage reading the one before. The
# queries are the events of queries_(), asked of the model given the evidence:
#
#   sppl_dice.py PROGRAM.sppl
#
# queries
# component 0 bool query0

from functools import reduce
from itertools import accumulate

yes_ = lambda: true_ << {1}
no_ = lambda: true_ << {0}
all_ = lambda es_: reduce(lambda a_, b_: a_ & b_, es_) if es_ else yes_()
fix_ = lambda g_, x_: (lambda y_: x_ if y_ == x_ else fix_(g_, y_))(g_(x_))
dedup_ = lambda xs_: list(dict.fromkeys(xs_))
index_ = lambda ts_: {t_: j_ for j_, t_ in enumerate(ts_)}
by_ = lambda ts_, ps_: reduce(lambda d_, j_: d_.setdefault(tuple(ts_[j_][p_] for p_ in ps_), []).append(j_) or d_,
                              range(len(ts_)), {})
idiv_ = lambda a_, b_: abs(a_) // abs(b_) * (1 if (a_ < 0) == (b_ < 0) else -1)
# the heads of relation q_ that matches ms_ give; a coin's index for each probability below 1
heads_ = lambda q_, ms_: [h_ for m_ in ms_ for r_, h_ in m_[1] if r_ == q_]
coins_of_ = lambda ps_, c0_: [None if p_ >= 1 else c0_ + n_
                              for p_, n_ in zip(ps_, accumulate([0] + [int(x_ < 1) for x_ in ps_]))]
# a relation's instances, each (its tuple's index, its coin and value or None, its refs); their indexes by tuple
facts_ = lambda i_, ts_, cs_: [(i_[t_], None if c_ is None else (c_, 1), []) for t_, c_ in zip(ts_, cs_)]
inst_ = lambda q_, i_, ms_, ks_, c0_: [(i_[h_], None if ks_ is None else (c0_ + ks_[m_[0]], n_ + 1), m_[2])
                                      for m_ in ms_ for n_, (r_, h_) in enumerate(m_[1]) if r_ == q_]
by_tuple_ = lambda es_, n_: (lambda d_: [d_.get((j_,), []) for j_ in range(n_)])(by_(es_, (0,)))
# the tuples (relation, index) that a tuple's instances read; those that tuples us_ read in turn, where ok_
reads_ = lambda u_: ([(r_, k_) for m_ in of_[u_[0]][u_[1]] for r_, k_, _, _ in insts_[u_[0]][m_][2]]
                     if u_[0] in of_ else [])
reach_ = lambda us_, ok_: fix_(lambda s_: s_ | {w_ for u_ in s_ for w_ in reads_(u_) if ok_(w_)}, frozenset(us_))
# a component's steps, each (relation, instance, stage, cycle), over the tuples of its relations c_ that the
# queries and the evidence read: its cycles of tuples (the tuples that reach the same ones), each after the
# cycles it reads (which reach fewer), in as many stages as it has tuples, each stage reading the one before
cycles_ = lambda rs_: sorted(reduce(lambda d_, u_: d_.setdefault(rs_[u_], []).append(u_) or d_, sorted(rs_),
                                    {}).values(), key=lambda us_: (len(rs_[us_[0]]), us_[0]))
steps_ = lambda c_: [(u_[0], m_, s_, g_) for g_, us_ in enumerate(cycles_(
                         {u_: reach_([u_], lambda w_: w_[0] in c_) for u_ in used_ if u_[0] in c_}))
                     for s_ in range(1, len(us_) + 1) for u_ in us_ for m_ in of_[u_[0]][u_[1]]]
# a step's tuple and stage; the step of a tuple's last instance at each stage; a tuple's last stage and its
# cycle; the step before each, where it is an earlier instance of its tuple at its stage
key_ = lambda x_: (x_[0], insts_[x_[0]][x_[1]][0], x_[2])
at_of_ = lambda st_: {key_(x_): k_ for k_, x_ in enumerate(st_)}
ends_ = lambda st_: {key_(x_)[:2]: (x_[2], x_[3]) for x_ in st_}
prev_ = lambda st_: [k_ - 1 if k_ and key_(st_[k_ - 1]) == key_(st_[k_]) else None for k_ in range(len(st_))]
# events: a fact's; a tuple's at stage s_ (None its last, 0 before the first); a step's coin and body, which
# reads the tuples of its own cycle at the stage before; the step's or the one before it
fact_ = lambda c_, v_: (yes_() if v_ else no_()) if c_ is None else coins_[c_] << {v_}
value_ = lambda a_, at_s_, end_, u_, v_, s_: (lambda t_: (no_() if v_ else yes_()) if t_ == 0
                                              else a_[at_s_[u_ + (t_,)]] << {v_})(end_[u_][0] if s_ is None else s_)
coin_ = lambda c_: [] if c_ is None else [coins_[c_[0]] << {c_[1]}]
step_ = lambda st_, end_, k_: (lambda q_, m_, s_, g_: all_(coin_(insts_[q_][m_][1]) + [
    at_[r_](j_, v_, s_ - 1 if w_ and end_[(r_, j_)][1] == g_ else None)
    for r_, j_, v_, w_ in insts_[q_][m_][2]]))(*st_[k_])
ev_ = lambda e_, p_, acc_: e_ if p_ is None else e_ | (acc_(p_) << {1})
holds_ = lambda q_, t_, v_: (lambda j_: (no_() if v_ else yes_()) if j_ is None else at_[q_](j_, v_, None))(
    ix_[q_].get(t_))

# female/0: 1 facts, each a tuple and its probability
female_ft = [()]
female_fp = [0.5]
female_c0 = 0
female_cd = [{1: p_, 0: 1 - p_} for p_ in female_fp if p_ < 1]
female_fc = coins_of_(female_fp, female_c0)

female_t = female_ft
female_i = index_(female_t)

# rule 5: 0.75::drug :- \+ female.
rule5_m = [((), (('drug', ()),), [] + n2)
    for n2 in [[('female', j1, 0, 0) for j1 in [female_i.get(())] if j1 is not None]]]
# rule 6: 0.25::drug :- female.
rule6_m = [((), (('drug', ()),), [('female', j1, 1, 0)])
    for j1 in [female_i.get(())] if j1 is not None]
drug_t = dedup_(heads_('drug', rule5_m + rule6_m))
drug_i = index_(drug_t)
rule5_k = index_(dedup_([m_[0] for m_ in rule5_m]))
rule5_c0 = female_c0 + len(female_cd)
rule5_cd = [{1: 0.75, 0: 1 - (0.75)}] * len(rule5_k)
rule6_k = index_(dedup_([m_[0] for m_ in rule6_m]))
rule6_c0 = rule5_c0 + len(rule5_cd)
rule6_cd = [{1: 0.25, 0: 1 - (0.25)}] * len(rule6_k)
drug_inst = inst_('drug', drug_i, rule5_m, rule5_k, rule5_c0) + inst_('drug', drug_i, rule6_m, rule6_k, rule6_c0)
drug_of = by_tuple_(drug_inst, len(drug_t))

# rule 1: 0.6::recovery :- drug, \+ female.
rule1_m = [((), (('recovery', ()),), [('drug', j3, 1, 0)] + n2)
    for n2 in [[('female', j1, 0, 0) for j1 in [female_i.get(())] if j1 is not None]]
    for j3 in [drug_i.get(())] if j3 is not None]
# rule 2: 0.7::recovery :- \+ drug, \+ female.
rule2_m = [((), (('recovery', ()),), [] + n2 + n4)
    for n2 in [[('drug', j1, 0, 0) for j1 in [drug_i.get(())] if j1 is not None]]
    for n4 in [[('female', j3, 0, 0) for j3 in [female_i.get(())] if j3 is not None]]]
# rule 3: 0.2::recovery :- drug, female.
rule3_m = [((), (('recovery', ()),), [('drug', j1, 1, 0), ('female', j2, 1, 0)])
    for j1 in [drug_i.get(())] if j1 is not None
    for j2 in [female_i.get(())] if j2 is not None]
# rule 4: 0.3::recovery :- \+ drug, female.
rule4_m = [((), (('recovery', ()),), [('female', j3, 1, 0)] + n2)
    for n2 in [[('drug', j1, 0, 0) for j1 in [drug_i.get(())] if j1 is not None]]
    for j3 in [female_i.get(())] if j3 is not None]
recovery_t = dedup_(heads_('recovery', rule1_m + rule2_m + rule3_m + rule4_m))
recovery_i = index_(recovery_t)
rule1_k = index_(dedup_([m_[0] for m_ in rule1_m]))
rule1_c0 = rule6_c0 + len(rule6_cd)
rule1_cd = [{1: 0.6, 0: 1 - (0.6)}] * len(rule1_k)
rule2_k = index_(dedup_([m_[0] for m_ in rule2_m]))
rule2_c0 = rule1_c0 + len(rule1_cd)
rule2_cd = [{1: 0.7, 0: 1 - (0.7)}] * len(rule2_k)
rule3_k = index_(dedup_([m_[0] for m_ in rule3_m]))
rule3_c0 = rule2_c0 + len(rule2_cd)
rule3_cd = [{1: 0.2, 0: 1 - (0.2)}] * len(rule3_k)
rule4_k = index_(dedup_([m_[0] for m_ in rule4_m]))
rule4_c0 = rule3_c0 + len(rule3_cd)
rule4_cd = [{1: 0.3, 0: 1 - (0.3)}] * len(rule4_k)
recovery_inst = inst_('recovery', recovery_i, rule1_m, rule1_k, rule1_c0) + inst_('recovery', recovery_i, rule2_m, rule2_k, rule2_c0) + inst_('recovery', recovery_i, rule3_m, rule3_k, rule3_c0) + inst_('recovery', recovery_i, rule4_m, rule4_k, rule4_c0)
recovery_of = by_tuple_(recovery_inst, len(recovery_t))

at_ = {
    'female': lambda j_, v_, s_: fact_(female_fc[j_], v_),
    'drug': lambda j_, v_, s_: value_(comp2_acc, comp2_at, comp2_end, ('drug', j_), v_, s_),
    'recovery': lambda j_, v_, s_: value_(comp3_acc, comp3_at, comp3_end, ('recovery', j_), v_, s_),}
ix_ = {'female': female_i, 'drug': drug_i, 'recovery': recovery_i}
coin_d_ = female_cd + rule5_cd + rule6_cd + rule1_cd + rule2_cd + rule3_cd + rule4_cd
insts_ = {'drug': drug_inst, 'recovery': recovery_inst}
of_ = {'drug': drug_of, 'recovery': recovery_of}
# the tuples the queries and the evidence read, and those their instances read in turn
asked_ = [('recovery', ()), ('drug', ())]
used_ = reach_([(q_, ix_[q_][t_]) for q_, t_ in asked_ if t_ in ix_.get(q_, {})], lambda w_: True)
comp2_steps = steps_({'drug'})
comp2_at = at_of_(comp2_steps)
comp2_end = ends_(comp2_steps)
comp2_prev = prev_(comp2_steps)
comp2_ev = lambda k_: ev_(step_(comp2_steps, comp2_end, k_), comp2_prev[k_], lambda i_: comp2_acc[i_])
comp3_steps = steps_({'recovery'})
comp3_at = at_of_(comp3_steps)
comp3_end = ends_(comp3_steps)
comp3_prev = prev_(comp3_steps)
comp3_ev = lambda k_: ev_(step_(comp3_steps, comp3_end, k_), comp3_prev[k_], lambda i_: comp3_acc[i_])
queries_ = lambda: [holds_('recovery', (), 1)]
evidence_ = lambda: all_([holds_('drug', (), 1)])

coins_ = array(len(coin_d_))
comp2_acc = array(len(comp2_steps))
comp3_acc = array(len(comp3_steps))

true_ ~= atomic(loc=1)
for n_ in range(len(coin_d_)):
    coins_[n_] ~= discrete(coin_d_[n_])
# drug/0: an instance holds where its body or an earlier instance of its tuple does
for k_ in range(len(comp2_steps)):
    if comp2_ev(k_):
        comp2_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=1)
    else:
        comp2_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=0)
# recovery/0: an instance holds where its body or an earlier instance of its tuple does
for k_ in range(len(comp3_steps)):
    if comp3_ev(k_):
        comp3_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=1)
    else:
        comp3_acc[k_] ~= atomic(loc=0)
condition(evidence_())

/*
Probabilistic context-free grammar. The grammar is left-recursive, depth bounded
inference is necessary to ensure termination.
0.4:S->SS
0.3:S->a
0.3:S->b
From
 Taisuke Sato and Keiichi Kubota. Viterbi training in PRISM. 
Theory and Practice of Logic Programming,  doi:10.1017/S1471068413000677. 
*/
:- use_module(library(pita)).

:- if(current_predicate(use_rendering/1)).
:- use_rendering(c3).
:- endif.

:- pita.

:- set_pita(depth_bound,true).
:- set_pita(depth,5).

:- begin_lpad.

% pcfg(LT): LT is string of terminals accepted by the grammar
% pcfg(L,LT,LT0) L is a tring of terminals and not terminals that derives
% the list of terminals in LT-LT0

pcfg(L):- pcfg(['S'],[],_Der,L,[]).
% L is accepted if it can be derived from the start symbol S and an empty
% string of previous terminals

pcfg([A|R],Der0,Der,L0,L2):-
  grammar_rule(A,Der0,RHS),
  pcfg(RHS,[rule(A,RHS)|Der0],Der1,L0,L1),
  pcfg(R,Der1,Der,L1,L2).
% if there is a rule for A (i.e. it is a non-terminal), expand A using the rule
% and continue with the rest of the list

pcfg([A|R],Der0,Der,[A|L1],L2):-
  terminal(A),
  pcfg(R,Der0,Der,L1,L2).
% if A is a terminal, move it to the output string

pcfg([],Der,Der,L,L).
% there are no more symbols to expand

grammar_rule('S',Der,['S','S']):0.4; grammar_rule('S',Der,[a]):0.3; 
  grammar_rule('S',Der,[b]):0.3.
% encodes the three rules of the grammar

terminal(a).
terminal(b).

:- end_lpad.


/** <examples>
?- prob(pcfg([a]),Prob).
% expected result ~ 0.2986666666666667.

?- prob(pcfg([b]),Prob).
% expected result ~ 0.2976666666666667.

?- prob(pcfg([a,a]),Prob).
% expected result ~ 0.035666666666666666.

?- prob(pcfg([b,b]),Prob).
% expected result ~ 0.036833333333333336.

?- prob(pcfg([a,b]),Prob).
% expected result ~ 0.035833333333333335.

?- prob(pcfg([a,b,a]),Prob).
% expected result ~ 0.009.


*/

#lang roulette/example/disrupt
;; cplint_bag_game.pl: a ProbLog program written for Roulette by tddlog's
;; scripts/problog2ppl.py, first order as it is written. A relation is a hash
;; from its tuples (lists of constants) to whether each holds, a Boolean of the
;; coins; each probabilistic fact is a coin of its own (`flip`), read from the
;; facts file named on the command line; each rule is a loop over the
;; relations its body joins. Each query's distribution is Roulette's, at the
;; module's level (`display-pmf`), given the evidence; the program prints
;; `roulette K true P` and `roulette K false P` for the K-th query.

(require racket/port racket/string racket/match)

;; A statement of the program: a definition, which the language does not
;; run as a query of its own (it runs each expression of the module as one).
(define-syntax-rule (statement e ...) (define-values () (begin e ... (values))))

;; the tuple t of r holds also where x does
(define (add! r t x)
  (hash-set! r t (if (hash-has-key? r t) (|| (hash-ref r t) x) x)))
;; whether the tuple t of r holds
(define (holds r t) (hash-ref r t #f))
;; whether t holds, if it is a tuple of r: none or one value to loop over
(define (probe r t) (if (hash-has-key? r t) (list (hash-ref r t)) null))
;; the tuples of r and whether each holds, (tuple . holding) each, by their
;; values at positions ps (from 0)
(define (index r . ps)
  (define ix (make-hash))
  (for ([(t x) (in-hash r)])
    (hash-update! ix (for/list ([p (in-list ps)]) (list-ref t p)) (λ (es) (cons (cons t x) es)) null))
  ix)
;; whether a tuple of the index's key k holds
(define (holds-any ix k)
  (for/fold ([some #f]) ([e (in-list (hash-ref ix k null))]) (|| some (cdr e))))
;; the choice of an annotated disjunction p1::h1; ...; pn::hn: whether each
;; head is the one chosen, the k-th with probability pk and none with the rest
(define (choose . ps)
  (let loop ([ps ps] [left 1.0] [none #t])
    (if (null? ps)
        null
        (let* ([q (if (> left 0) (min 1.0 (/ (car ps) left)) 1.0)]
               [c (if (>= q 1.0) #t (flip q))])
          (cons (&& none c) (loop (cdr ps) (- left (car ps)) (&& none (! c))))))))

(define (constant s) (or (string->number s) (string->symbol s)))
;; the relations of the facts file: a line `relation probability argument...`
;; a fact, a coin of its own where its probability is below one
(define (facts path)
  (define db (make-hash))
  (for ([line (in-lines (open-input-file path))])
    (define f (string-split line "\t" #:trim? #f))
    (define p (string->number (cadr f)))
    (add! (hash-ref! db (car f) make-hash) (map constant (cddr f)) (if (>= p 1) #t (flip p))))
  db)

;; The distribution of v, a list of (value . probability): Roulette's query
;; at the module's level (`display-pmf`), read back from the table it
;; prints, or from the one value it prints alone.
(define (distribution v)
  (define text (with-output-to-string (λ () (display-pmf v))))
  (define (datum s)
    (define d (read (open-input-string s)))
    (if (and (pair? d) (eq? (car d) 'quote)) (cadr d) d))
  (define rows
    (for/list ([line (in-list (string-split text "\n"))]
               #:when (regexp-match? #rx"[│|]" line))
      (filter (λ (s) (not (string=? s ""))) (map string-trim (regexp-split #rx"[│|]" line)))))
  (if (null? rows)
      (list (cons (datum text) 1))
      (for/list ([r (in-list rows)]
                 #:unless (equal? r '("Value" "Probability")))
        (cons (datum (car r)) (string->number (cadr r))))))
(define (real p) (if (exact? p) (exact->inexact p) p))
(define (probability dist v)
  (define e (assoc v dist))
  (if e (cdr e) 0))
(define (report dists)
  (for ([dist (in-list dists)] [k (in-naturals 1)])
    (printf "roulette ~a true ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #t)))
    (printf "roulette ~a false ~a\n" k (real (probability dist #f)))))

(define db (facts (vector-ref (current-command-line-arguments) 0)))
(define red-facts (hash-ref db "red/0" (make-hash)))
(define green-facts (hash-ref db "green/0" (make-hash)))
(define blue-facts (hash-ref db "blue/0" (make-hash)))
(define yellow-facts (hash-ref db "yellow/0" (make-hash)))

(define blue blue-facts)

(define green green-facts)

(define red red-facts)

(define yellow yellow-facts)

(define win (make-hash))
(statement
  ;; win :- red, green.
  (for ([x1 (in-list (probe red (list)))])
    (for ([x2 (in-list (probe green (list)))])
      (add! win (list) (&& x1 x2))))
  ;; win :- blue, yellow.
  (for ([x1 (in-list (probe blue (list)))])
    (for ([x2 (in-list (probe yellow (list)))])
      (add! win (list) (&& x1 x2)))))

(define dists
  (list (distribution (holds win (list)))))
(statement (report dists))

# cplint_earthquake.pl: a ProbLog program written in SPPL by tddlog's scripts/problog2ppl.py,
# first order as it is written. The facts and the joins of the rules are Python
# constants, computed before the first sample: each rule's matches a list
# comprehension over the relations its body joins, a recursive component's
# tuples a fixpoint of its rules, and the tuples that the queries and the
# evidence read. Then each probabilistic fact and each instance of a
# probabilistic rule samples a coin, and each instance of a tuple that is read
# sets a variable of its own, in a `for` over its component's instances: 1
# where its body holds or an earlier instance of its tuple does, the last of a
# tuple's instances its holding. A cycle of tuples that read each other does so
# in as many stages as it has tuples, each stage reading the one before. The
# queries are the events of queries_(), asked of the model given the evidence:
#
#   sppl_dice.py PROGRAM.sppl

# component 0 bool query0
# component 1 bool query1
# component 2 bool query2
# component 3 bool query3

from functools import reduce
from itertools import accumulate

yes_ = lambda: true_ << {1}
no_ = lambda: true_ << {0}
all_ = lambda es_: reduce(lambda a_, b_: a_ & b_, es_) if es_ else yes_()
fix_ = lambda g_, x_: (lambda y_: x_ if y_ == x_ else fix_(g_, y_))(g_(x_))
dedup_ = lambda xs_: list(dict.fromkeys(xs_))

by_ = lambda ts_, ps_: reduce(lambda d_, j_: d_.setdefault(tuple(ts_[j_][p_] for p_ in ps_), []).append(j_) or d_,
                              range(len(ts_)), {})
idiv_ = lambda a_, b_: abs(a_) // abs(b_) * (1 if (a_ < 0) == (b_ < 0) else -1)
# the heads of relation q_ that matches ms_ give; a coin's index for each probability below 1
heads_ = lambda q_, ms_: [h_ for m_ in ms_ for r_, h_ in m_[1] if r_ == q_]
coins_of_ = lambda ps_, c0_: [None if p_ >= 1 else c0_ + n_
                              for p_, n_ in zip(ps_, accumulate([0] + [int(x_ < 1) for x_ in ps_]))]
# a relation's instances, each (its tuple's index, its coin and value or None, its refs); their indexes by tuple
facts_ = lambda i_, ts_, cs_: [(i_[t_], None if c_ is None else (c_, 1), []) for t_, c_ in zip(ts_, cs_)]
inst_ = lambda q_, i_, ms_, ks_, c0_: [(i_[h_], None if ks_ is None else (c0_ + ks_[m_[0]], n_ + 1), m_[2])
                                      for m_ in ms_ for n_, (r_, h_) in enumerate(m_[1]) if r_ == q_]
by_tuple_ = lambda es_, n_: (lambda d_: [d_.get((j_,), []) for j_ in range(n_)])(by_(es_, (0,)))
# the tuples (relation, index) that a tuple's instances read; those that tuples us_ read in turn, where ok_
reads_ = lambda u_: ([(r_, k_) for m_ in of_[u_[0]][u_[1]] for r_, k_, _, _ in insts_[u_[0]][m_][2]]
                     if u_[0] in of_ else [])
reach_ = lambda us_, ok_: fix_(lambda s_: s_ | {w_ for u_ in s_ for w_ in reads_(u_) if ok_(w_)}, frozenset(us_))
# a component's steps, each (relation, instance, stage, cycle), over the tuples of its relations c_ that the
# queries and the evidence read: its cycles of tuples (the tuples that reach the same ones), each after the
# cycles it reads (which reach fewer), in as many stages as it has tuples, each stage reading the one before
cycles_ = lambda rs_: sorted(reduce(lambda d_, u_: d_.setdefault(rs_[u_], []).append(u_) or d_, sorted(rs_),
                                    {}).values(), key=lambda us_: (len(rs_[us_[0]]), us_[0]))
steps_ = lambda c_: [(u_[0], m_, s_, g_) for g_, us_ in enumerate(cycles_(
                         {u_: reach_([u_], lambda w_: w_[0] in c_) for u_ in used_ if u_[0] in c_}))
                     for s_ in range(1, len(us_) + 1) for u_ in us_ for m_ in of_[u_[0]][u_[1]]]

# cycle; the step before each, where it is an earlier instance of its tuple at its stage
key_ = lambda x_: (x_[0], insts_[x_[0]][x_[1]][0], x_[2])
at_of_ = lambda st_: {key_(x_): k_ for k_, x_ in enumerate(st_)}
ends_ = lambda st_: {key_(x_)[:2]: (x_[2], x_[3]) for x_ in st_}
prev_ = lambda st_: [k_ - 1 if k_ and key_(st_[k_ - 1]) == key_(st_[k_]) else None for k_ in range(len(st_))]

fault_rupture_fp = [1.0]
fault_rupture_c0 = 0

volcanic_eruption_c0 = fault_rupture_c0 + len(fault_rupture_cd)
volcanic_eruption_cd = [{1: p_, 0: 1 - p_} for p_ in volcanic_eruption_fp if p_ < 1]
volcanic_eruption_fc = coins_of_(volcanic_eruption_fp, volcanic_eruption_c0)

fault_rupture_t = fault_rupture_ft
fault_rupture_i = index_(fault_rupture_t)

volcanic_eruption_t = volcanic_eruption_ft
volcanic_eruption_i = index_(volcanic_eruption_t)

rule1_m = [((X,), (('earthquake', (X, 'strong')), ('earthquake', (X, 'moderate'))), [('fault_rupture', j1, 1, 0)])
    for j1, (X,) in enumerate(fault_rupture_t)]
# rule 2: 0.2::earthquake(X,strong); 0.6::earthquake(X,moderate) :- volcanic_eruption(X).
rule2_m = [((X,), (('earthquake', (X, 'strong')), ('earthquake', (X, 'moderate'))), [('volcanic_eruption', j1, 1, 0)])
    for j1, (X,) in enumerate(volcanic_eruption_t)]

earthquake_i = index_(earthquake_t)
